text: Rule under which the lump-sum payout from a life insurance or pension insurance policy is taxed favourably if the contract has run for at least twelve years and the payout is made no earlier than after the 62nd birthday (the 60th for contracts from the years 2005 to 2011). Under Section 20(1) no. 6 sentence 2 EStG (Income Tax Act), only half of the difference between the payout and the premiums paid in is then taxable, albeit at the personal tax rate.
Variant of the doubling rule with 70 in the numerator. It is more accurate at low rates and is therefore commonly used for inflation and loss of purchasing power.
Approximation for the doubling time in which 72 is divided by the interest rate as a percentage. It is exact at 7.85% and usable between 1% and 15%.

Threshold for drawdown, rule adherence, statistical evidence or time spent, set in advance and in writing. Once it is reached, trading is suspended without the matter being debated afresh at that moment.

Separate tax rate of 25% on private capital income under Section 32d EStG (Income Tax Act), unchanged since 2009. Including the solidarity surcharge, the burden is 26.375%, and with 8% or 9% church tax around 27.82% or 27.99% respectively. The tax does not always have a final withholding effect; Section 32d(2) EStG excludes, among other things, loans between related parties, to which the personal income tax scale applies.

Once the tax has been withheld at source, the income tax on the income is settled in full under Section 43(5) EStG (Income Tax Act), so the income no longer has to be declared. Exceptions are governed by Section 32d(2) EStG.

Difference between reported profit and operating cash flow, usually expressed relative to the balance sheet total. High accruals mean profit without an inflow of cash and are empirically associated with weaker subsequent earnings.

Self-imposed waiting period between an investment idea and the order, usually 24 hours to seven days, combined with a written rationale. It is modelled on statutory withdrawal periods such as the one under Section 8 VVG (Insurance Contract Act).

Systematic allocation of the acquisition or production cost of an asset over its useful life. It reduces profit without any cash flowing out and is therefore added back in the indirect cash flow statement. If investment stays below depreciation over the long term, the company's asset base erodes.
siehe: EBITDA, Cash flow statement, Free cash flow, Impairment

text: State that a process never leaves once it has reached it. For wealth, this is ruin or any other point at which you have to get out.

Clause that allows the insurer to refer the insured person to another occupation that would theoretically be reasonable and to refuse benefits, even if the person does not work in that occupation. Good policies do without it.
A standard deviation that only takes into account periods below a set target return. It forms the denominator of the Sortino ratio.

Accrual items (Abgrenzungen), that is, the difference between net profit and operating cash flow that is tied up in receivables, inventories, provisions and capitalised costs. Relative to the balance sheet total, this gives the accrual ratio, an early indicator of aggressive accounting.

Morningstar study series that measures active funds against the asset-weighted average of index funds in the same category rather than against an index. A fund only counts as a success if it survives the period and beats this average.

Obligation of listed issuers under Article 17 of the EU Market Abuse Regulation (MAR) to publish inside information without delay. It is a legal precondition for prices to absorb public information quickly.

Earnings measures defined by the company itself outside the accounting framework, called alternative performance measures in supervisory law. Since 3 July 2016, the ESMA guidelines have required a clear definition, a reconciliation to the closest IFRS measure, a prior-year comparison and no greater prominence than the IFRS figure. Special items that are adjusted out again every year are recurring costs.

American depositary receipt, a certificate issued by a US bank for shares held in custody in their home market. It makes foreign shares tradable in the USA, incurs custody fees and additionally carries the risk of the programme and of the depositary bank.

Allowance for wear and tear (Absetzung für Abnutzung), the tax depreciation of the building for let properties; land is never depreciated. Straight-line AfA under Section 7(4) EStG (Income Tax Act) is 3% for completion after 31 December 2022, 2% for construction years 1925 to 2022 and 2.5% before that. For residential buildings where construction starts or the purchase contract is signed between 1 October 2023 and 30 September 2029, 5% declining-balance depreciation on the residual value is available as an alternative (Section 7(5a) EStG).

The depreciable portion of the acquisition or construction cost of a building. It comprises the purchase price and incidental purchase costs, less the portion attributable to the land. Depreciation is only applied to this amount.

Securitised stake in the share capital of a public limited company (AG). The shareholder is a co-owner with voting, dividend and subscription rights but is not liable beyond their contribution; in insolvency, the shareholder ranks behind all creditors.
siehe: No-par-value share, Preference share, Annual general meeting (AGM), Dividend

text: A separately maintained loss offset pot at the bank for losses from the sale of individual shares. Under Section 20(6) sentence 4 EStG (Income Tax Act), these losses may only be offset against gains from share sales, not against ETF gains, interest or dividends.

Remuneration of employees in shares or options, which under IFRS 2 must be recognised as an expense at fair value. It is non-cash and therefore does not appear as an outflow in operating cash flow, but it dilutes the stake of existing shareholders. What matters is the diluted share count, even if the expense is presented as a special item.

Present-value-weighted average period for which capital is tied up in the expected payments of a share. In the Gordon model, D = (1+r)/(r−g). Typical values are 15 to 40 years, considerably more than for most bonds.

Purchase of its own shares by the company, limited in Germany to 10% of share capital under Section 71 AktG (Stock Corporation Act). It increases earnings per share because the number of shares falls, and economically it is an alternative to the dividend. Its value to the shareholder depends on whether the company buys back below or above intrinsic value.

Division of existing shares into a larger number of shares with a correspondingly lower price. The value of the position and the value of the company remain unchanged; the split only changes the denomination and thus how easily small amounts can be traded.

Separately maintained loss offset pot at the bank for losses from the sale of individual shares. Under Section 20(6) sentence 4 EStG (Income Tax Act), these losses can only be offset against gains from share sales, not against interest, dividends or fund gains.

Monthly pension in euros that one earnings point (Entgeltpunkt) yields. Since 1 July 2026 it has been €42.52, up from €40.79 before, an adjustment of 4.24%. The value is adjusted every year on 1 July, mainly in line with wage growth (Section 68 SGB VI). Since 1 July 2023, a single nationwide value has applied; the distinction between West and East has been abolished.

Internal bank account for all other losses from capital assets, that is, from funds and ETFs, bonds, certificates, derivative transactions (Termingeschäfte) and bad debts. These losses may be offset against any positive capital income, including gains on shares.

The return left over after deducting the return explained by the risk model. Jensen's alpha measures the distance from the security market line of the CAPM: Alpha = R − [Rf + Beta × (Rm − Rf)]. Measured against a multi-factor model, the alpha of most funds falls to zero because it turns out to be a factor premium.
siehe: Beta, Capital asset pricing model (CAPM), Factor premium, Information ratio

text: Number of people aged 67 and over per 100 people aged 20 to 66. The ratio is purely demographic and says nothing about how many of these people pay contributions.

Metric defined by the company itself outside the accounting standards, such as an adjusted EBIT. The ESMA guidelines require a definition, a reconciliation to the closest IFRS measure, comparative figures and consistent application.

Metrics defined by the company itself alongside the IFRS financial statements, such as adjusted EBITDA or adjusted EPS. Under the ESMA guidelines, a definition, a reconciliation to the IFRS measure and consistent use are mandatory.

Successor model for new Riester business from 1 January 2027, adopted with the Retirement Provision Reform Act 2026 (Altersvorsorgereformgesetz). The first €360 of annual contributions is subsidised at 50 cents per euro and further contributions up to €1,800 at 25 cents per euro, together up to €540 of basic allowance, plus €300 per child and a €200 career starter bonus. For the first time, investment without guarantees in funds and ETFs up to risk class 5 and in euro bonds of public issuers is possible, while individual shares are excluded; in addition, there is a standard product with the reduction in yield (Effektivkosten) capped at 1.0%.

Score for estimating the insolvency risk of listed industrial companies: Z = 1.2 × working capital/total assets + 1.4 × retained earnings/total assets + 3.3 × EBIT/total assets + 0.6 × market value of equity/liabilities + 1.0 × revenue/total assets. Values above 2.99 are considered safe, 1.81 to 2.99 a grey zone, and anything below that a distress zone. It is not applicable to banks and insurers.
siehe: Working capital, Equity ratio, Beneish M-score, Piotroski F-score

text: Allocation following exercise by the option holder. For American-style equity options, it can happen at any time during the term and is assigned by random draw by the clearing house.

Speculator, stock market columnist and storyteller (born 1906 in Budapest, died 1999 in Paris) who shaped the post-war generation of German investors. He is the source of Kostolany's egg as a cycle model, the distinction between shaky and strong hands, and the image of the man with the dog for the relationship between the stock market and the economy.
siehe: Kostolany's egg, Shaky hands (zittrige Hände), Strong hands (hartgesottene Hände)

text: Repayment portion in the first year as a percentage of the loan amount. Together with the borrowing rate (Sollzins), it gives the annuity, for example 3.90% plus 2.00% equals 5.90% of the loan amount per year.

Sudden increase in the price or scarcity of an input, such as energy. A supply shock raises the price level and at the same time lowers output. A demand shock, by contrast, moves both in the same direction.

Collection of information on the customer's knowledge and experience before non-advised transactions under Section 63(10) WpHG (Securities Trading Act). It is based on self-disclosure and does not apply to non-complex instruments in execution-only business.

The notes explain the balance sheet and income statement: valuation methods, remaining maturities, contingent liabilities, related parties, remuneration of board members, auditor fees. The management report under Section 289 HGB (Commercial Code) is a separate instrument with an economic report, a forecast report and a report on opportunities and risks. The most important information about a company is usually found there rather than in the tables of figures.
siehe: Balance sheet, Income statement, HGB (German Commercial Code)

text: A number, once mentioned, shifts later estimates, even if it appears to be random. Tversky and Kahneman (1974) used a rigged wheel of fortune; with an anchor of 10, participants estimated the share of African countries in the UN at a median of 25%, with an anchor of 65 at 45%. On the stock market, the purchase price, the all-time high and other people's price targets act as anchors.

Income tax return form for income from capital assets. It is needed for the most-favourable assessment (Günstigerprüfung), loss offsetting across banks, correcting the substitute tax base (Ersatzbemessungsgrundlage), the allowance for grandfathered fund units (Alt-Anteile) and the subsequent declaration of church tax after a blocking notice (Sperrvermerk). For foreign funds without German tax withholding, the investment fund income annex (Anlage KAP-INV) is added.

Supplementary form for income from investment funds that was not subject to domestic tax withholding, typically from fund units in a foreign securities account. On this form, you have to calculate the distribution, the advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale) and the capital gain yourself.

Annex to the income tax return for other income, including private disposal transactions (private Veräußerungsgeschäfte) and income under Section 22 no. 3 EStG (Income Tax Act). Since 2023, it has had separate lines for crypto assets.

Gold in the form of bars or bullion coins with at least a legally specified fineness. It is exempt from VAT in the EU. In Germany, capital gains are tax-free after a holding period of more than one year.
Group of assets with a common source of return and a similar risk driver, that is, equities, bonds, property, commodities or bank deposits.

Written advance commitment, in a few sentences, on the purpose of the money, target figure, allocation, exclusion criteria, cost limit and behaviour in a decline, supplemented by a rule on when the document may be changed.

Written set of rules for a portfolio covering target allocation, building blocks, contributions, rebalancing rule and emergency rule. It is drawn up in calm times so that it applies in turbulent ones.

All assets that serve the business on a long-term basis: intangible assets, tangible assets, financial assets (Section 266 HGB, assets side, item A). They are not held for sale; depreciable items such as buildings and machinery are depreciated systematically over their useful life, land and financial assets are not. A high share is characteristic of capital-intensive businesses with high operating leverage from fixed costs.
siehe: Current assets, Balance sheet, Depreciation, Return on capital employed (ROCE)

text: An investor's money-weighted return, calculated as the internal rate of return of all deposits and withdrawals including the final value. It shows what was earned on the money invested rather than what the fund achieved.

Gap between a fund's reported return and the return on the average unit of money invested. It arises solely from the timing and size of purchases and sales and grows with the volatility of the product.

Loan in the form of a security. The investor is a creditor, receives a coupon periodically and the face value at maturity. Prices are quoted as a percentage of face value, which is why a bond can trade above par (more than 100) or below par.

Splitting an amount across several maturity years. Each year one rung matures and, if the money is not needed, is reinvested at the long end. This averages the interest rate level over time and saves decisions about when to buy.

Written list of every valuation assumption with its value, source, date, confidence assessment and the finding that would refute it. The log protects against bending the numbers to fit the result after the fact.

Quarterly change extrapolated to a full year, the standard for GDP in the USA. An annualised rate of 1.5% corresponds to around 0.37% growth over the previous quarter, the presentation customary in Europe.

Quarterly change extrapolated to a full year, the usual reporting format in the USA. The conversion to the quarterly rate is (1 + annual rate)^(1/4) − 1. Germany and Eurostat, by contrast, report the change on the previous quarter directly.

Constant payment over several periods. The annuity factor converts a present value into such a series of payments: a = i / (1 − (1+i)^−n). The instalment stays constant, but as the outstanding balance falls, the ratio of interest to repayment shifts.
siehe: Present value, Future value, Discount rate

text: Standard form of mortgage financing with a constant instalment whose composition changes. At first, the interest portion is large and the repayment portion small; with each instalment, the outstanding balance falls and with it the interest portion, while the repayment portion grows at an accelerating pace. Formula: Instalment = Loan × ((1+i)^n × i) / ((1+i)^n − 1); because banks calculate monthly, the effective interest rate is higher than the borrowing rate (Sollzins).

A return pattern that an established pricing model does not explain. One example is a systematic excess return on shares with a particular characteristic that cannot be justified by their market risk.

Tendency No. 1 in Munger's list. People align their behaviour with their remuneration more strongly than they themselves believe. With every recommendation, you should therefore check who is paying the person making it, and for what.

Expenditure on repairs and modernisation within three years of the purchase that exceeds 15% of the building's acquisition cost, net of VAT. Under Section 6(1) no. 1a EStG (Income Tax Act), the entire amount is then capitalised and only has an effect through depreciation.
Variant of the same fund with its own ISIN but an identical portfolio. The classes differ in distribution policy, currency hedging or minimum investment; the securities held are the same.

Taleb's term for systems that get better under stress, whereas robust systems merely withstand stress unchanged. It is put into practice through asymmetry with limited losses and open-ended upside. To this end, the barbell strategy combines a very safe majority with a small, broadly diversified speculative remainder, around 90 to 10, and avoids medium risks.
Supervisory instrument under Section 10d KWG (Banking Act). In times of strong credit growth, banks must hold additional equity capital, which is released in a crisis.
Voluntary tax return, filed without any legal obligation, to reclaim overpaid tax. It is possible within the four-year assessment period under Section 169(2) sentence 1 no. 2 AO (Fiscal Code).
Value added per hour worked (or per person employed). It is the only source of permanently rising real wages and is hard to measure for services and digital goods.

begriff: Arithmetic of active management (Arithmetik der aktiven Verwaltung)
text: Identity described by William Sharpe (1991). Since all investors together hold the market, the capital-weighted average of actively managed money earns exactly the market return before costs and necessarily less after costs.

Identity described by William Sharpe (1991). Since all investors together hold the market, the average active return before costs is exactly equal to the market return and after costs is necessarily below it. The statement follows from an arithmetic rule and requires no empirical data.

The simple average of the individual returns. It is the right measure for the expectation of a single future period but overstates the long-term growth in wealth actually achieved. For the S&P 500 (1928 to 2025), it is 11.86%, the geometric mean 10.02%; the difference grows with the square of volatility.
siehe: Geometric mean, Standard deviation, Compound annual growth rate (CAGR)

text: The division of wealth among asset classes, in the narrower sense the ratio of the risky portion to the low-risk portion. It determines expected return and depth of losses more than the selection of individual products.

Subordinated bank bond that counts as Additional Tier 1 capital for regulatory purposes. It can be written down or converted into shares if a certain capital ratio is undershot or the supervisor orders it. At Credit Suisse, such bonds worth CHF 16 billion were written off completely in 2023.
The unnoticed replacement of a difficult question with an easy one, for example “How likely is a crash?” with “How easily can I think of a crash?”.

Extra cost of acquiring the underlying via a warrant compared with buying it directly, expressed as a percentage of the underlying. For warrants in the money or at the money, the premium equals the time value; for warrants out of the money, the gap between the strike price and the current price is added.
Minimum distance or minimum duration from which leaving the zone counts as a breakout. The filter reduces false signals and at the same time worsens the entry price.

Fee per savings plan execution, either as a fixed amount or as a percentage of the contribution. It acts like a permanent cut in every contribution. With a monthly contribution of €300, 1.75% costs €63 a year.
One-off sales charge when buying fund units, added on top of the net amount invested. A 5% charge corresponds to 4.76% of the amount paid in.
Condition, set in advance and in writing, under which a product or a decision is rejected without further examination. It works because it is set before the specific offer arrives.

Dividend per share divided by earnings per share. Values above 100% mean that the dividend is being paid out of the company's substance or on credit. The ratio is more meaningful than the dividend yield because it does not depend on the share price.

Approved trading bank which, under a contract with the fund management company, is exclusively permitted to create new ETF units and which returns units to the fund in large blocks. For this purpose, it delivers the index's basket of shares or receives it on redemption. Through this arbitrage, it keeps the exchange price close to the fund's value.

Existing rules in tax and social security law that change the budget balance in line with the business cycle without any new decision. They include the progressive tax scale, contribution-financed social insurance, and unemployment benefit and short-time work allowance (Kurzarbeitergeld). They take effect without delay and reverse symmetrically in an upswing.

Wilder-smoothed average of the true range, that is, the largest of the three ranges formed from the daily high, daily low and previous day's close. The ATR is an amount in price units and measures swings, not direction.

Simulation of a strategy on historical data; its result is only a hypothesis. Before the launch of the corresponding ETF, smart beta indices delivered an excess return of around 3% a year and afterwards −0.5% to −1%. Always check since when an index has been calculated live and what before that date has only been calculated retrospectively.
siehe: Overfitting, Look-ahead bias, Survivorship bias, Smart beta

text: Fitting a strategy to random patterns in historical data by trying out many variants. The more attempts are made, the longer the data series must be for a good result to be meaningful.

Market situation in which the futures price is below the spot price, typically when physical supply is tight. Rolling a long position then produces a roll gain because the next contract is cheaper than the expiring one.

Loss participation of owners and creditors in the resolution of a bank, introduced after the financial crisis as an alternative to the taxpayer-funded bail-out. The liability cascade runs from equity through subordinated and unsecured bonds to large deposits; deposits protected by law up to €100,000 are exempt. For investors, this means that a bank bond is not a deposit and a certificate is a bearer bond (Inhaberschuldverschreibung) without deposit protection.

Rebalancing only when a set deviation is exceeded, instead of on fixed dates. A common approach is the 5/25 rule with thresholds of 5 percentage points in absolute terms or 25% relative to the target weight.

Distance between the upper and lower Bollinger Bands divided by the middle band. The measure shows how widely the last 20 closing prices were dispersed, not how widely they will be dispersed in future.

Mass simultaneous withdrawal of deposits that makes even a solvent institution unable to pay because its assets cannot be turned into cash at short notice. At Silicon Valley Bank, customers withdrew around $42 billion on 9 March 2023 alone; at the end of 2022, around nine tenths of its $175 billion in deposits were above the deposit protection limit. In the EU, deposits of up to €100,000 per customer per institution are protected by law, which reduces the risk of panic among retail customers.

Today's value of a future payment: PV = Z / (1+i)^n. Present value is the basis of every valuation, from the bond price to the DCF. The higher the discount rate and the further away the payment, the smaller the present value.
siehe: Discount rate, Future value, Discounted cash flow method (DCF), Terminal value

text: The discount a retailer grants for immediate payment. If it is given up in exchange for 0% financing, the forgone discount is the interest on that financing.

Notional minimum return of a fund under Section 18 InvStG (Investment Tax Act), calculated as the value on the first valuation day of the year times the base interest rate (Basiszins) times 0.7. After deducting distributions, the remainder is the advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale).
Mandatory document under the PRIIPs Regulation for packaged investment products. In a few pages, it sets out the risk indicator, performance scenarios, total costs and recommended holding period.

A payment account with basic functions to which every person in Germany is entitled under the Payment Accounts Act (Zahlungskontengesetz), even without sufficient creditworthiness or a fixed address. Banks may only refuse it in narrowly defined exceptional cases; the fee must be reasonable.
The price set in the option contract at which the underlying may be bought or sold, also called the strike or exercise price. It remains constant over the term.
One hundredth of a percentage point. 25 basis points are 0.25 percentage points. Fees and interest rate steps are usually stated in basis points.
Historical frequency of an event without taking the current situation into account. It is the starting point of every well-calibrated forecast and is what poor forecasts most often overlook.

Lifelong annuity in the first layer of retirement provision, usually called the Rürup pension after its namesake. Contributions of up to €30,826 (2026) are fully deductible as special expenses (Sonderausgaben), and the pension is subject to deferred taxation. Surrender, a lump-sum option and borrowing against the contract are excluded.
Risk arising from the difference between the underlying of the hedge and the assets held. It turns a hedge into a separate bet on the relative performance of two markets.

First layer of retirement provision, comprising the statutory pension, the professional pension scheme (Versorgungswerk), the old-age security scheme for farmers (Alterssicherung der Landwirte) and the Rürup pension. The only payout is a lifelong annuity that cannot be surrendered or converted into a lump sum, but in return it comes with a high deduction as special expenses (Sonderausgaben) and protection from seizure.
The reference variable of a derivative, for example a share, index, interest rate, exchange rate, commodity or any other variable whose value on the due date can be determined beyond dispute.

The risk-free rate used in valuation practice. In Germany, under the convention of the IDW (Institute of Public Auditors in Germany), it is derived from the Bundesbank's Svensson-estimated yield curve, smoothed and rounded to 0.25 percentage points. This is why it deviates from the yield on any given day.

begriff: Base interest rate for fund taxation (Basiszins)
text: Interest rate that the Bundesbank calculates from the yield curve for public-sector bonds with a remaining maturity of 15 years as at the first trading day of the year and that the Federal Ministry of Finance (BMF) publishes. For 2026 it is 3.20% (BMF circular of 13 January 2026), the highest value since its introduction; after the reduction to 70%, this gives 2.24% of the value at the start of the year. It must be distinguished from the basic rate of interest under Section 247 BGB (Civil Code) for default interest.

Reference rate calculated every six months under Section 247 BGB (Civil Code) and published by the Deutsche Bundesbank. Since 1 July 2026, it has been 1.52%. Default interest charged to consumers is five percentage points above the basic rate of interest.

begriff: Basic rate of interest under Section 247 BGB
text: A reference figure that the Bundesbank updates every six months and that has stood at 1.52% since 1 July 2026. It is neither an investment rate nor a lending rate and serves as the reference for default interest under Section 288 BGB (plus 5 or 9 percentage points respectively). It must be distinguished from the base interest rate (Basiszins) for the advance lump sum under Section 18 InvStG (Investment Tax Act).

Index of prices for the construction of new residential buildings. It describes the development of replacement costs excluding land; in regions with demand, rising construction prices also support the prices of existing properties. In May 2026, it was 5.0% above the same month of the previous year.

Rule by which a probability is updated when new evidence becomes available. It combines the base rate with the strength of the evidence and converts P(evidence given hypothesis) into P(hypothesis given evidence).

Energy performance certificate whose rating is calculated from the building envelope, windows and building services and therefore does not depend on the occupants' heating habits. Its counterpart is the consumption-based certificate (Verbrauchsausweis), which evaluates the bills of the last three years.

Capital increase resolved by the annual general meeting to service conversion and option rights, to prepare business combinations or for employee programmes (Section 192 AktG). The shares only come into existence when the rights are exercised.
Tendency No. 24 in Munger's list. A request or recommendation meets with considerably more agreement as soon as it is followed by any “because” at all, even if the reason given is empty.

The gap between a fund's return and the return its investors achieve because they get in too late and out too early. Morningstar measures it for funds domiciled in the USA in its “Mind the Gap” study; in the decade to the end of 2025, the funds returned 9.9% a year and the average dollar invested 8.7%. Barber and Odean (2000) show a related effect among private investors holding individual shares; there, the average household earned 16.4% a year, the most active fifth only 11.4% and the market 17.9%, with barely any difference in gross returns. The difference there arose almost entirely from the costs of trading.

Income limit up to which social security contributions are levied. In 2026, it is €8,450 a month (€101,400 a year) nationwide in the statutory pension insurance, and €5,812.50 a month in health and long-term care insurance. Above it, neither contributions nor additional earnings points (Entgeltpunkte) arise; for high salaries, the social contribution rate on total income therefore falls.

Ratio of the loan to the mortgage lending value of the property; it determines the interest rate premium more than almost any other feature. Incidental purchase costs do not increase the mortgage lending value; if they are financed as well, the ratio rises without any additional collateral. If the purchase price is also largely financed, the ratio is then above 100% and the interest rate considerably higher.

Screening score built from eight ratio indices: M = −4.84 + 0.920 DSRI + 0.528 GMI + 0.404 AQI + 0.892 SGI + 0.115 DEPI − 0.172 SGAI + 4.679 TATA − 0.327 LVGI. Values above −1.78 are considered a sign of possible accounting manipulation. The score only provides an indication and is not applicable to financial institutions.
siehe: Altman Z-score, Piotroski F-score, Cash conversion cycle

text: Joint will in which spouses appoint each other as sole heirs and the children only inherit after the death of the surviving spouse. It provides for the survivor but lets the children's inheritance tax allowance lapse on the first death and binds the survivor to the joint will.

Insurance that pays an agreed monthly benefit if, for an expected period of at least six months, the insured person can perform their most recent occupation to an extent of less than 50%. It protects lifetime income, not health.

Register of all resolutions and relevant operative parts of court judgments, with date and wording, which the property manager must keep (Section 24(7) WEG). Every owner may inspect it, prospective buyers only with the seller's authorisation.
A variable measured at a specific date: wealth, debts, money supply, balance sheet total. It has no time interval, whereas flow variables such as income always need a period.

Ongoing remuneration that a fund management company passes on from its management fee to the custodian bank or the intermediary for as long as the fund unit remains in the securities account. It is not tied to a sale. Its amount depends on the volume rather than on the quality of the advice.

Rule under which a change in the law leaves existing situations unaffected. In tax law, this applies, for example, to securities bought before 1 January 2009, which therefore remained exempt from the flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) on price gains.

The tendency to preferentially seek out, remember and find convincing information that supports your own position. In a portfolio, it leads to arguments against a position you hold being systematically given less weight. Procedures rather than willpower help against it, such as a counter-thesis set down in writing, exit criteria set in advance and a pre-mortem.

The statutory auditor's opinion under Section 322 HGB (Commercial Code) on the financial statements and management report. It certifies reasonable assurance based on sample testing and does not rule out fraud. Qualifications and emphasis-of-matter paragraphs in the opinion are warning signs in their own right.

Sensitivity of an investment to the overall market: Beta = Covariance(Ri, Rm) / Variance(Rm) = Correlation × (Sigma_i / Sigma_m). By definition, the market has a beta of 1. In the KPMG cost of capital study 2025, the average levered beta of the companies examined from Germany, Austria and Switzerland was 1.03.
siehe: Capital asset pricing model (CAPM), Covariance, Weighted average cost of capital (WACC), Low-volatility anomaly

text: Systematic loss of value of a factor certificate in volatile sideways markets. It arises because the leverage is recalculated every day on the basis of the previous day's close.

Second pillar of old-age provision with five funding vehicles (Durchführungswege): direct pension commitment (Direktzusage), support fund (Unterstützungskasse), direct insurance (Direktversicherung), Pensionskasse and Pensionsfonds. Only the direct pension commitment is provided directly by the employer; with the others, a third party pays, but the employer is secondarily liable (Section 1(1) sentence 3 BetrAVG). Take-up is stagnating. In 2023, 18.1 million people had an active entitlement; in firms with fewer than ten employees only around 25%, in large firms 86%.

Apparently low volatility of a unit price that arises only because it is based on periodic appraisals rather than market prices. The risk is no smaller as a result; it merely shows up later and abruptly.

Consequence of valuation by appraisers instead of by market prices. As a result, the measured volatility and the measured correlation with the stock market come out too low, although the economic risk is unchanged.

Right of an existing shareholder to subscribe for new shares in a capital increase in proportion to their existing stake (Section 186 AktG). It protects against dilution, is itself tradable and may be excluded for cash capital increases of up to 20% of share capital if the new shares are issued close to the market price.

Figure stating how many old shares entitle the holder to subscribe for one new share (e.g. 4:1). For an ADR, it states how many original shares one depositary receipt represents. Without this figure, no price comparison is possible.
The bias of recognising cognitive errors in others while overlooking them in yourself. It makes mere knowledge of biases largely ineffective.

Comparison, as at a reporting date, of assets (Aktiva) and sources of capital (Passiva). Under Section 266 HGB (Commercial Code), it takes the account form: the assets side comprises fixed and current assets, the equity and liabilities side comprises equity, provisions and liabilities. It shows a state, not a development, and says nothing about the earning power of the assets.
siehe: Income statement, Cash flow statement, Fixed assets, Current assets

text: The distributable amount of a public limited company (AG). It is calculated as net profit for the year plus profit carried forward, less loss carried forward and transfers to statutory and other revenue reserves. The annual general meeting decides only on this amount (Section 174 AktG).
Sum of all assets, equivalent to the sum of all equity and liabilities. It measures the size of the capital employed rather than success.
Simultaneous growth of the assets side and the liabilities side of a balance sheet. When a loan is granted, the claim and the deposit are created in a single step, without any change in equity.

Gross domestic product, the value of all goods and services produced within a country in a given period. Real GDP excludes price increases, nominal GDP does not; only real GDP measures volumes. Germany and the euro area report the change on the previous quarter, the USA an annualised figure. A US figure of 1.5% corresponds to around 0.37% quarterly growth; a direct comparison without conversion is wrong.

Weighting countries by economic output instead of market value. It has a countercyclical effect and reduces concentration in highly valued markets. There is no theoretical justification for higher returns, and implementation generates turnover and costs.

Decentralised cryptocurrency, launched with the genesis block on 3 January 2009. The supply is capped at 21 million units, and the block reward halves roughly every four years. The price history shows four comparable cycles with declines of around 77% to 93% between the highs.

Continuously updated, cryptographically linked ledger of transactions that many participants maintain in parallel. The technology replaces a central custodian with a consensus mechanism; it says nothing about the economic value of what is recorded on it.

Average location value of land per square metre, which the valuation committee (Gutachterausschuss) determines at least every two years under Section 196 BauGB (Federal Building Code) and which can be accessed via the portals of the federal states. It is used to split the purchase price into a land portion and a building portion.

Call centre, usually abroad, that sells financial products unsolicited, following a script and for commission on each sale. It has no licence under Section 32 KWG (Banking Act) or Section 15 WpIG (Investment Firm Act).

Assessment of the probability that someone will meet their payment obligations as agreed. Credit agencies such as SCHUFA assess payment and contractual behaviour for this purpose, not income or wealth.
The annual hedging premium at which a hedged strategy achieves exactly the same final return over a period as the unhedged one. It can only be determined in hindsight.
Share of winning trades at which the expected value per trade is zero. Without costs, p = 1/(1 + reward-to-risk ratio). Fees, spread and slippage raise this threshold noticeably.

Difference between nominal and real yields of the same maturity, that is, the average inflation priced in by the market. In September 2026, a nominal yield of 4.94% minus a TIPS real yield of 2.61% gave a ten-year break-even rate of 2.33%.

International monetary order agreed in 1944. The dollar was tied to gold at $35 per fine ounce and convertible only for central banks; all other currencies were pegged to the dollar within narrow bands. The system ended de facto in 1971 and formally in 1973.
Measure of the quality of probability forecasts. It is the mean squared distance between the stated probability and the actual outcome. Zero is perfect; always guessing 50% gives 0.25.

Revenue less the production cost of the goods and services sold. It is a mandatory line item only under the cost of sales method in accordance with Section 275(3) HGB (Commercial Code). The gross margin derived from it measures pricing power.

The annual net basic rent relative to the purchase price, calculated before incidental purchase costs and before all running costs. It serves as a quick indicator and is not a return in the investment sense.
Reconciliation from enterprise value to the value of equity. Net financial debt, pension provisions and non-controlling interests are deducted, and non-operating assets are added.

British act of June 1720 that prohibited the formation of joint-stock companies without a royal charter. It slowed the spread of this legal form until its repeal in 1825 but did not address the mechanisms of speculation.
Non-interest-bearing Treasury bill of the German federal government with a maturity of up to twelve months. It is issued below face value and redeemed at 100%; the difference is the return.
Balances in accounts at commercial banks, also called deposit money. Legally, a claim against the bank, not against the central bank. In the euro area, around 84% of the money supply M3.

Market capitalisation of all listed companies divided by gross domestic product, used as a rough valuation measure for an entire stock market. It is distorted because large corporations earn a growing share of their profits abroad, which does not show up in domestic GDP. The long-term upward trend is therefore partly structural and not purely a bubble signal.

Debt security of the German federal government and the benchmark for the entire euro interest rate market. The federal government issues Bubills with maturities of up to twelve months, Schatz notes with two years, Bobls with five and federal bonds (Bunds) with 7 to 30 years, plus green variants. It has not issued any new inflation-linked federal securities since 2024; those already issued continue to be traded.
siehe: Bond, Yield curve, Pfandbrief (German covered bond)

text: Durable competitive advantage that protects high returns on capital from competition. Common forms are cost advantages, brand and intangible assets, switching costs, network effects and efficient scale. In economic terms, a moat means that ROIC stays above WACC over the long term.
siehe: Return on invested capital (ROIC), Weighted average cost of capital (WACC), Margin of safety, Intrinsic value

text: Amount by which a company's monthly spending exceeds its income. The burn rate and the cash available give the time remaining until the next funding round.

Method commonly used in Germany to calculate fund performance, in which distributions are treated as reinvested and the initial charge is disregarded. The reported figure is therefore higher than what an investor paying the charge achieves.

Organised marketplace with rules for admission, price determination and settlement. The price is formed by matching buy and sell orders in the order book; securities transactions in the EU are currently settled two business days after the trade (T+2).

Compound annual growth rate, the geometric annual return: CAGR = (Final value/Initial value)^(1/n) − 1. It describes the steady path that would have led from the initial to the final value and ignores all fluctuations in between. Two investments with the same CAGR may have followed completely different paths.
siehe: Geometric mean, Time-weighted return (TWR), Maximum drawdown

text: Sale of a short-dated option and purchase of a long-dated option with the same strike price. The profit comes from the faster time decay of the shorter maturity; the position is net long vega.
Upper limit on the redemption amount of a certificate. Above the cap, the investor no longer participates in further price gains of the underlying. In return, the certificate is sold at a discount.

Capital market model for expected returns: E(Ri) = Rf + Beta × (E(Rm) − Rf). Its core statement is that only systematic risk is rewarded, because unsystematic risk can be diversified away. Empirically, it is contradicted by the size, value and low-beta effects; in addition, there is Roll's critique, according to which the true market portfolio cannot be observed.
siehe: Beta, Market risk premium, Alpha, Fama-French models

text: Profit share of the fund management, usually 20% of the return above a hurdle. In Germany, for asset-managing venture capital companies, it is taxed under Section 18(1) no. 4 EStG (Income Tax Act), with 40% remaining tax-free under Section 3 no. 40a EStG.

Borrowing in a low-interest currency and investing in a high-interest currency; the profit is the interest rate differential, the risk an appreciation of the funding currency. Historically, it has often been profitable; in return, it carries the risk of abrupt unwinding. In early August 2024, for example, many yen-funded positions were unwound at the same time; the yen appreciated sharply, and the Nikkei 225 lost around 12% in a single day on 5 August.
Operating cash flow divided by net profit. Over a full cycle, the figure should be at or above 1, because depreciation reduces profit without costing cash.

Period for which capital is tied up in operating business: CCC = DIO + DSO − DPO, that is, inventory days plus receivable days minus payable days. With a negative CCC, the customer pays before the supplier is paid, and the business finances itself interest-free. Rising days sales outstanding without a change in the business model is one of the oldest warning signs.
siehe: Working capital, Beneish M-score, Free cash flow

text: Sale of a put for which the purchase price for a possible assignment is deposited in cash. The maximum profit is the premium; the maximum loss is the strike price minus the premium.

Reserve of two to three years' withdrawals in the low-risk portion, which is drawn on in loss-making years instead of selling units. Economically, it largely corresponds to a slightly lower equity allocation and at the same time is an effective rule against panic selling.
Dividend divided by free cash flow. It shows whether the payout is covered by the current cash surplus. The ratio based on profit does not show this, because profit contains non-cash items.
Restoring the target allocation by directing new contributions rather than by selling. No gains are realised in the process, so the largest cost item of a reallocation disappears.

Over-the-counter contract for difference with high leverage. Since the ESMA measures of 2018, fixed leverage limits for retail clients have applied, ranging from 30:1 for major currency pairs to 2:1 for crypto assets, along with a requirement to close out positions at 50% of the minimum margin and negative balance protection. In Germany, the obligation to make additional payments (Nachschusspflicht) has been ruled out since 2017.
Ratio of the average gain to the amount at risk (1R). Together with the win rate, it determines the expected value E = p × reward-to-risk ratio − (1 − p).

Buffett's circle of competence. Its size is secondary; what matters is knowing its boundaries precisely and not overstepping them. The most common mistake is confusing it with familiarity; using a product every day does not yet mean that you understand the provider's business model, capital intensity and competition.

Rule-based trading halt on a stock exchange after a specified price decline. In the USA, they have existed since 1988. Today, trading pauses for 15 minutes at minus 7% and minus 13% in the S&P 500; at minus 20%, the trading day ends.

The quoted bond price excluding accrued interest. On purchase, the dirty price including accrued interest must be paid. Exchange prices and charts show the clean price so that the price history does not jump in a sawtooth pattern around the coupon dates.

State in which the existing portfolio will grow to the target amount by retirement age through growth in value alone. Further contributions are no longer necessary; current expenses continue to be covered by earned income.
Share position with a bought put as a floor and a sold call as a cap. In a zero-cost collar, the call premium fully finances the put; the price paid is the capped upside.

Claims and expenses of a property and casualty insurer divided by earned premiums. Below 100%, the insurance business is profitable in its own right; above it, underwriting is cross-subsidised by investment income.

Company that can reinvest a large part of its profits in its own business at a return well above its cost of capital. It can be recognised by a high return on capital combined with a high reinvestment rate.

Market situation in which the futures price is above the spot price, for example because of financing and storage costs. Since the futures contract converges to the spot price at maturity, rolling a long position produces a structural roll loss; you sell cheap and buy dearer.

Principle formulated by John Bogle according to which gross return minus costs equals net return, regardless of how efficient markets are. Costs are the only factor affecting return that an investor knows in advance and determines themselves.

When buying constant amounts, you acquire more units at low prices and fewer at high prices; as a result, the average cost per unit is below the average price. The effect is an arithmetical consequence of the regular contributions and not a return advantage over an immediate lump-sum investment.
Sale of a call on shares already held in the portfolio. The result per share is min(S_T, K) − S_0 + premium. The gain is capped; the price risk remains almost unchanged.

Document filled in beforehand with the portfolio value, loss amounts in euros, the reason for investing and permitted actions. In a crash, it is only read, and looking things up takes the place of making a decision.

Creation and return of ETF units in large blocks (creation units) on the primary market, usually in exchange for securities rather than cash. As a result, the transaction costs are borne by those entering or leaving rather than by the fund's assets.

Contract in which the buyer pays an ongoing premium and receives a compensation payment if a specific debtor or security defaults. Economically, it corresponds to credit default insurance; legally, it is a derivative without insurance supervision.

Yield premium of a bond over a government bond of the same maturity, compensating for default risk, expected loss and illiquidity. It fluctuates far more than realised default rates; in September 2026, it stood at 0.78 percentage points for US investment grade and 2.70 percentage points for US high yield.
Current assets divided by current liabilities. Graham required a value of at least 2.0 for the defensive investor; for business models with payment in advance, a lower value is normal.
Searching data sets for patterns without a prior hypothesis. In capital market research, it leads to chance findings being published as regularities, because only the successful tests are visible.

Searching through many variants of rules and parameters until one looks good. Because the number of attempts is not taken into account, random noise appears as a finding. Remedies include higher t-statistic hurdles and the deflated Sharpe ratio.
Free, complete disclosure of all data stored about a person under Article 15(3) GDPR. It is intended for your own review, not for presenting to landlords.

Index of the 40 largest listed German companies, selected by free-float market capitalisation, minimum liquidity and positive EBITDA. The weight of a single constituent is capped at 15%. From 1988 to 2025, the total return index achieved 8.78% a year.
siehe: Index, Total return index, Free float (Streubesitz)

text: Valuation as the present value of future cash flows, not of future profits. In the entity approach, FCFF is discounted at the WACC, which gives the enterprise value; in the equity approach, FCFE is discounted at the cost of equity. Every DCF valuation depends on two unknown quantities: the cash flow forecast and the discount rate.
siehe: FCFF and FCFE, Weighted average cost of capital (WACC), Terminal value, Reverse DCF

text: Mechanism described by Irving Fisher in 1933 in which falling prices and incomes increase the real burden of debts fixed in nominal terms. Simultaneous attempts to repay depress demand and thus prices further.

Exchange of debt instruments for shares in the debtor. In 1719/20, the Mississippi Company and the South Sea Company took over government debt in exchange for their own shares; the creditors received shares in the company rather than in the debtor, the state. Today, the debt-for-equity swap is a common instrument in restructurings.
Liquid assets divided by monthly fixed costs. The coverage period measures wealth in months without income rather than in euros and shows how much room for manoeuvre a sum provides.
Share of the estimated net requirement in retirement that is already covered by entitlements acquired. The remainder is the gap from which the target capital is derived.

Legally ring-fenced pool of mortgage loans or public-sector loans that secures a Pfandbrief in addition to the bank's liability. If the bank becomes insolvent, it does not form part of the insolvency estate. Section 4 PfandBG (Pfandbrief Act) requires overcollateralisation of at least 2% on a present-value basis.

Adjustment to the Sharpe ratio proposed by Bailey and López de Prado that takes into account the number of strategy variants tested, the length of the time series, and the skewness and kurtosis of returns.

Persistently falling price level. It is considered more dangerous than mild inflation because it reinforces itself. Consumption is postponed, the real debt burden rises (debt deflation according to Irving Fisher), and at the effective lower bound the central bank can no longer lower the real interest rate sufficiently. This is why central banks aim for 2% rather than 0% inflation.

Depreciation of 5% of the respective residual value for new residential buildings under Section 7(5a) EStG (Income Tax Act) if the start of construction or the purchase contract falls between 30 September 2023 and 1 October 2029. Switching to straight-line AfA is permitted.

Revocation of the admission to trading on a stock exchange. On the regulated market, since the reform of Section 39 BörsG (Stock Exchange Act) in 2015, it has only been permitted if it is preceded by an acquisition offer whose consideration is at least equal to the weighted average price over the last six months.

Change in the option price per unit change in the price of the underlying. Delta lies between 0 and 1 for a call and between -1 and 0 for a put, corresponds to the hedge ratio and gives only a rough indication of the probability of expiring in the money.

Account for the safekeeping of securities, usually in collective safe custody (Girosammelverwahrung), in which the customer remains a co-owner of the collective holding. The securities therefore do not form part of the bank's insolvency estate; the settlement account alongside it is covered by deposit protection.
siehe: Settlement account, Deposit protection, International Securities Identification Number (ISIN)

text: Contract whose value is derived from an underlying, such as an option, futures contract, swap or certificate. Derivatives transfer risks but do not create them; what one party gains, the other side loses, less costs.
siehe: Option, Futures contract, Swap, Contract for difference (CFD)

text: Market maker approved by the exchange that undertakes to provide binding bid and ask prices for a security on a continuous basis. In doing so, it must observe a minimum volume, a maximum spread and a minimum quotation time.
Contract that fixes an exchange rate today for a future date. Currency forwards are the building blocks of any currency hedge; funds usually roll them over monthly.

Survey index that measures how many respondents report an improvement rather than how strong it is. The threshold of 50 separates expansion from contraction. Purchasing managers' indices are the best-known example.

Transactions by executives on their own account that must be reported under Article 19 of the EU Market Abuse Regulation (MAR). From an annual volume of €20,000, in Germany since 2026 from €50,000, a reporting deadline of three business days applies, as does a trading ban in the 30 calendar days before an interim or annual report.

Interest rate at which future payments are discounted to today, economically the price of time and risk. In a company DCF, it is the WACC or the cost of equity; for bonds, the yield to maturity. Half a percentage point more changes the value of long payment streams by a double-digit percentage.
siehe: Present value, Weighted average cost of capital (WACC), Terminal value, Gordon growth model

text: The tendency to sell winners too early and hold on to losers for too long. In 10,000 accounts, Odean (1998) found a realisation rate of 14.8% for gains and 9.8% for losses; in the following year, the winners sold outperformed the losers held by 3.4 percentage points. Only in December is the pattern reversed; investors are therefore able to realise losses but do not do so for eleven months.

Spreading money across many investments whose performance does not move in step. The effect depends on the covariances; the mere number of holdings is not enough. With equal weighting, portfolio variance tends towards the average covariance as the number of holdings increases. In Elton and Gruber's data, the standard deviation falls from 49.2% for one share to 23.9% for ten and 20.9% for thirty, but never below around 19%.
siehe: Correlation, Covariance, Standard deviation, Efficient frontier

text: Distribution of the distributable profit (Bilanzgewinn) to shareholders, resolved by the annual general meeting. In the DAX, dividends contributed around 2.78 percentage points a year to the total return between 1988 and 2025; the total return index achieved 8.78% p.a., the price return index 6.00%.
siehe: Ex-dividend date, Total return index, Price return index

text: Arithmetical reduction of the share price on the ex-dividend date by the dividend resolved. The amount is transferred from the price to the settlement account, so no loss arises. For tax purposes, however, the dividend is income received, and tax must be withheld on it immediately.
Share whose high dividend yield has arisen solely from a fall in the share price. The payout is then usually no longer covered by earnings and is cut.
Thin line above and below the body of a candle. It marks the high and low of the interval, that is, prices that were reached but not held until the end of the interval.

Treaty between states that determines which state may tax which income and usually limits withholding tax to 15%. For funds, it applies at fund level. Thanks to the Irish-US treaty, an ETF domiciled in Ireland pays 15% instead of 30% US withholding tax, which affects the net return of a global equity ETF by something of the order of 0.15 percentage points a year.

Main disadvantage of salary sacrifice (Entgeltumwandlung). Saving is done out of gross pay; in the payout phase, the company pension is subject to the full health insurance contribution (around 17.5% in 2026) and the long-term care insurance contribution, which the pensioner bears alone. The only relief is the allowance for pension-type income (Versorgungsbezüge) of €197.75 a month, and only in health insurance; in long-term care insurance, an exemption threshold (Freigrenze) applies, above which the entire amount is subject to contributions. Under Section 229(1) sentence 3 SGB V (Social Code Book V), a lump-sum payment is subject to contributions for ten years, on one hundred-and-twentieth of the amount each month.

Oldest systematic body of chart analysis, developed from the editorials of Dow and Hamilton. It distinguishes three degrees of trend and three phases and requires confirmation by a second index and by volume.
Percentage decline from the previous peak. The maximum drawdown is the deepest of these declines before a new peak is reached.

Days sales outstanding (average collection period), calculated as average trade receivables divided by revenue times 365. If it rises without a change in the business model, this points to customers' payment problems or premature revenue recognition.

Breakdown of return on equity into its components: ROE = net margin × asset turnover × equity multiplier, that is, (net profit/revenue) × (revenue/total assets) × (total assets/equity). The five-step variant additionally separates the tax burden and interest burden from the operating margin. The analysis shows whether a high ROE comes from the margin, from efficiency or from debt.
siehe: Return on equity (ROE), Profit margin, Leverage effect, Debt-to-equity ratio

text: Breakdown of ROE into net margin, asset turnover and equity multiplier. It shows whether a return on equity comes from pricing power, from efficiency or merely from debt.

Present-value-weighted average period for which capital is tied up, in years. Modified duration uses this to measure the price effect. The price changes by approximately minus modified duration times the change in interest rates in percentage points. One of the largest US bond ETFs, the iShares Core U.S. Aggregate Bond ETF, had an effective (option-adjusted) duration of 5.75 years in September 2026.

Legal form in which the pension commitment is implemented, that is, direct pension commitment (Direktzusage), support fund (Unterstützungskasse), direct insurance (Direktversicherung), Pensionskasse or Pensionsfonds. The funding vehicle determines the limits of state support, the investment of capital and insolvency protection.
Total income tax divided by taxable income. It is always lower than the marginal tax rate and only meaningful in retrospect.

Earnings before interest and taxes, that is, operating profit independent of financing and tax law. It is the appropriate numerator for enterprise value multiples and for ROCE. Unlike with EBITDA, depreciation and amortisation, and thus part of the consumption of capital, have been deducted.
siehe: EBITDA, EV/EBIT, Return on capital employed (ROCE), Economic value added (EVA)

text: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation, that is, net profit + taxes + interest expense + depreciation and amortisation. It is not defined in any accounting standard, every company calculates it differently, and on principle it does not take the need for reinvestment into account. Since IFRS 16, it has risen simply because rental expense becomes depreciation and interest.
siehe: EBIT, Adjusted metrics, IFRS 16, Free cash flow

text: Database of the US securities regulator SEC containing the mandatory filings of US-listed companies, including the 10-K annual report, the 20-F report for foreign issuers, the 8-K current report for ad hoc disclosures and the DEF 14A proxy statement on remuneration.
Interest rate sensitivity determined numerically from simulated interest rate shocks. It is needed for securities with call or conversion rights and is a standard figure in ETF factsheets.

Interest rate level below which a central bank cannot lower the nominal rate any further, because cash is available as an interest-free alternative. With negative inflation expectations, the real interest rate remains positive there, and monetary policy loses its most important instrument.

The price of a loan per year as a percentage, including processing fees, the disbursement rate and the payment frequency. Under the Price Indication Ordinance (Preisangabenverordnung), it must be stated for every consumer loan. Only with it can two offers be compared reliably; the borrowing rate (Sollzins) alone is not sufficient for this.
siehe: Borrowing rate (Sollzins), Annuity loan (Annuitätendarlehen), Arranged overdraft

text: Twice the distance between the execution price achieved and the midpoint between bid and ask at the moment the order is received. It is the only measure of the real costs of a specific order. The order itself bears half of it.

Statutory key figure for insurance products (Insurance Information Obligations Ordinance, VVG-InfoV). It states the reduction in return per year caused by all the costs of the contract, including the acquisition and administration costs of the insurance wrapper.
Short form of the annual percentage rate, the annual price of a loan including ancillary costs and payment frequency. Only with it can two loan offers be compared.

Economic moat created by a narrow market. The market only supports one or two providers, and an attacker would make both unprofitable. Typical of networks, airports and pipelines, which are mostly regulated and therefore capped in the level of their returns.

Set of all portfolios that offer the highest expected return for a given level of risk, obtained by minimising portfolio variance subject to return and budget constraints for all target returns from the return of the minimum variance portfolio upwards. This portfolio with the lowest volatility is its leftmost vertex. It is mathematically elegant but tricky in practice, because it is based on estimated expected values and covariances.
siehe: Minimum variance portfolio, Tangency portfolio, Capital market line, Covariance

text: Assumption that prices already contain all available information; a distinction is made between the weak form (price history), the semi-strong form (all public information) and the strong form (including insider knowledge). The Grossman-Stiglitz paradox shows that perfect efficiency is impossible, because then nobody would have any incentive to gather information. What matters in practice is the weaker statement that most people find it very hard to beat the market after costs.
siehe: Random walk, SPIVA, Alpha, Factor premium

text: Equity divided by the balance sheet total. It measures how much loss a company can withstand before creditors are affected. Around 30% is generally considered solid, but the figure depends heavily on the sector; banks are well below it, and IFRS 16 lowers the ratio simply by putting leases on the balance sheet.
siehe: Debt-to-equity ratio, Net debt, Balance sheet, IFRS 16

text: Decision that is impossible or expensive to reverse (Type 1). Its counterpart is the two-way door (Type 2), where returning to the starting position costs almost nothing.

VAT on the import of goods from third countries (Section 1(1) no. 4 UStG). Under Section 11 UStG (VAT Act), the tax base is the customs value plus customs duty. Businesses entitled to deduct input tax deduct it again under Section 15(1) sentence 1 no. 2 UStG.

Facility that allows banks to deposit surplus central bank money with the central bank overnight. With full allotment since October 2008 and the excess liquidity, its interest rate became the de facto decisive key interest rate of the Eurosystem; since March 2024, the ECB has explicitly steered its monetary policy stance through this rate. Since 16 September 2026, it has been 2.50%.

Statutory protection of bank deposits up to €100,000 per customer per institution, uniformly regulated in the EU and payable within seven business days. Securities in a securities account are not covered, because they remain the customer's property in any case; certificates and ETNs are protected in neither way.
siehe: Securities account, Issuer risk, Instant-access savings account

text: The interest rate that banks receive on their deposits with the central bank. It forms the floor for money market rates and, since the transition to ample excess liquidity, has been the decisive key interest rate of the Eurosystem; since 16 September 2026, it has been 2.50%.

Care-related part of the care home bill, which is the same for care levels (Pflegegrade) 2 to 5 within a given home. On 1 July 2026, the national average was €2,088 a month. Only this item is reduced by the care home supplement (Leistungszuschlag).
Liability of the employer for the promised benefit, even if a third party provides it (Section 1(1) sentence 3 BetrAVG). It distinguishes the company pension from a private contract.

Value of the existing insurance portfolio, calculated as adjusted net asset value plus the present value of future profits from contracts already concluded, less the cost of capital. New business is not included. Adding new business gives the appraisal value.

Risk that the issuer of a debt security defaults. Certificates, warrants, ETNs and ETCs are legally bearer bonds (Inhaberschuldverschreibungen) without deposit protection. The Lehman insolvency in September 2008 is the standard example; in response, collateralised certificates were created.
siehe: Segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen), Certificate (structured product), Deposit protection

text: Value of an investment at the end of the term: FV = K × (1+i)^n, plus the compounded contributions in the case of regular payments. Future value and present value are based on the same equation, read once forwards and once backwards. It must be distinguished from the terminal value in a DCF.
siehe: Present value, Annuity, Compound annual growth rate (CAGR), Terminal value

text: Expected value across many parallel paths at a single point in time. This is the figure found in prospectuses and statistics.

Value of the entire operating business, independent of financing. You get from enterprise value to equity value by deducting net financial debt, minority interests and pension obligations and adding non-operating assets. If the FCFF discounted at the WACC is divided directly by the number of shares, the debt is missing, and the value is systematically overstated.
siehe: Net debt, EV/EBIT, Discounted cash flow method (DCF), Multiples

text: Unit of calculation for the statutory pension. A year with exactly the average earnings of all insured persons yields 1.0 points, twice that 2.0 and half of it 0.5 points. The provisional average earnings for 2026 are €51,944. Because of the contribution assessment ceiling (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze), at most around 1.95 points a year can be achieved. The monthly pension is calculated as earnings points × pension access factor (Zugangsfaktor) × pension type factor (Rentenartfaktor) × current pension value (aktueller Rentenwert).

Conversion of gross salary into an entitlement under an occupational pension (betriebliche Altersvorsorge). In 2026, contributions of up to 8% of the contribution assessment ceiling (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze) are tax-free (€8,112), but only up to 4% are also exempt from social security contributions (€4,056). To the extent that the employer saves social security contributions, it must contribute an additional 15% of the converted pay. At the same time, the gross pay subject to pension insurance contributions falls, and with it earnings points (Entgeltpunkte), sickness benefit (Krankengeld), unemployment benefit and parental allowance.

Share of the portfolio value that is withdrawn each year. The target figure is the annual requirement divided by the percentage. At 3.5%, it corresponds to 28.6 times the annual requirement, at 3.0% to 33.3 times.

The share of starting wealth that is withdrawn in the first year of retirement and then adjusted in line with inflation. The Trinity study (1998, US data from 1926 to 1995, 30-year horizon) classifies 3% to 4% as largely safe. More recent analyses arrive at about 3.25% to 3.5% for horizons of 50 years and at high valuation levels. The only criterion of success was that the wealth was not used up prematurely. German taxes and costs are not reflected in these figures.
Record of every investment decision with the thesis, forecast range, emotional state, condition for refutation and review date. It makes your own hit rate measurable instead of leaving it to memory.
Reconciliation from enterprise value to the value of equity. Net financial debt, pension obligations and minority interests are deducted, and non-operating assets are added.

Several heirs form a joint ownership community (Gesamthandsgemeinschaft) under Sections 2032 et seq. BGB (Civil Code). They can only dispose of individual items in the estate jointly (Section 2040 BGB).

Tax on the transfer of assets on death, following the same rules as gift tax. After deduction of the allowances, the rate in tax class I (spouses, children) rises in stages from 7% to 30%, in class II from 15% to 43% and in class III from 30% to 50%. In addition to the personal allowances, there is a special pension allowance (Versorgungsfreibetrag) of €256,000 for spouses and graduated amounts for children under Section 17 ErbStG (Inheritance and Gift Tax Act).
Evaluating a decision by its outcome instead of by the information that was available when the decision was made. Resulting means that bad decisions which happened to turn out well are repeated.
Evaluating a decision by its outcome instead of by the process. In decisions under uncertainty, it rewards lucky hits and punishes good reasoning.

A process is ergodic if the average across many parallel paths equals the average of a single path over time. The development of wealth with leverage or a risk of ruin is not ergodic. The expected value across all paths says nothing about the path that an individual investor experiences. This leads to the practical rule of avoiding bets that include the possibility of a total loss, even if their expected value is positive.
siehe: Expected value, Kelly criterion, Geometric mean, Monte Carlo simulation

text: The part of capital expenditure that merely keeps existing operations going. It is not reported separately; scheduled depreciation serves as a first approximation.

Amount that a community of unit owners must build up for future maintenance; Section 19(2) no. 4 WEG (Apartment Ownership Act) requires an appropriate level. The law does not put a figure on this level. A reserve that is too low shifts the costs into a later special levy (Sonderumlage).
The time from a peak until the same peak is reached again. It is only loosely related to the depth of the decline and depends more on whether the cause permanently shifts earnings and interest rates.
The gain that the remaining capital has to achieve after a loss to get back to its previous level: 1/(1-v)-1. After minus 50%, that is plus 100%.

If the bank lacks the acquisition data for a security, under Section 43a(2) sentence 7 EStG (Income Tax Act) it applies a flat 30% of the sale proceeds as the taxable amount. This can only be corrected through the tax return.

Ratio of income in retirement to income before retirement. It is only meaningful on a net basis and only if both reference figures are specified. The statutory pension level (Rentenniveau) is not a personal replacement rate.

Form of taxation for private life annuities funded from income that has already been taxed. Only a flat-rate portion of the annuity is taxable, depending on the age at which it starts. If it starts at 67, the portion is 17%, at 65 or 66 it is 18% and at 63 it is 20%; the rest remains tax-free.
Specification in the prospectus of whether a fund distributes or accumulates. In the fund name, it can be recognised by the suffixes “Dist” or “Acc”.
Probability of default multiplied by the share lost in a default (1 minus the recovery rate). This part of the spread should be treated like a provision and does not count as income.

Sum of all possible outcomes weighted by their probabilities. It is the right measure for many repeated, mutually independent decisions with small stakes. For one-off decisions involving your entire wealth, it is misleading because it does not take account of the path and the risk of ruin.
siehe: Ergodicity, Kelly criterion, Monte Carlo simulation, Value at risk

text: Share of people in the reference population who are working or actively looking for work; in US statistics, this means all civilians aged 16 and over who are not in institutions, with no upper age limit. If it falls, the unemployment rate can fall even though no additional people have been employed. That is why it is indispensable when reading labour market data.

Exchange Traded Commodity, a secured debt security on a commodity. Unlike an ETF, an ETC is not a fund with separate fund assets and carries issuer risk, which is usually reduced by depositing the physical commodity or collateral.
siehe: Exchange-traded note (ETN), Gold ETC, Issuer risk

text: Exchange-traded fund, usually an index fund and in Europe as a rule a UCITS (OGAW), whose assets are kept separate from the assets of the management company; many ETFs launched in Germany are segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen). The assets under management of the European ETF market reached a record high of around €3.1 trillion at the end of June 2026. For index ETFs, the UCITS Directive (Article 53; in Germany, Section 209 KAGB, the German Investment Code) permits relaxed investment limits of 20% per issuer and up to 35% for a single issuer.
siehe: Index, TER, Replication, Segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen)

text: Exchange Traded Note, an unsecured or partially secured bearer bond on an index or underlying. If the issuer becomes insolvent, a total loss is possible, regardless of how the underlying performs. In September 2026, 361 ETNs and 2,971 ETFs were listed on Deutsche Börse.
siehe: Exchange-traded commodity (ETC), Issuer risk, Certificate (structured product)

text: Enterprise value divided by operating profit. Unlike the P/E ratio, the multiple is independent of the capital structure and can therefore be compared between companies with different levels of debt. For the US market as a whole, EV/EBIT stood at 29.1 in January 2026, and at 25.7 excluding financials.

Enterprise value divided by EBITDA; for the US market as a whole, it stood at 19.7 in January 2026, and at 17.0 excluding financials. Because EBITDA excludes depreciation, the multiple makes capital-intensive businesses look cheaper. For them, EV/EBIT or the FCF yield is more meaningful.

Economic Value Added, the residual income after the cost of capital: EVA = NOPAT − WACC × invested capital, or equivalently (ROIC − WACC) × invested capital. A positive EVA means value creation, a negative one value destruction, even when a book profit is reported. The present value of all future EVA is the Market Value Added.
siehe: Return on invested capital (ROIC), Weighted average cost of capital (WACC), Economic moat, Discounted cash flow method (DCF)

text: Stream of payments with no end date. The present value is annual payment / discount rate, or, for a growing payment, annual payment / (discount rate − growth).

First trading day on which a share is traded without the entitlement to the dividend that has been approved. The price is notionally reduced by the amount of the distribution. In Germany, this is the trading day after the annual general meeting; payment is made on the third business day after the annual general meeting.
