The risk of a loss that ends your economic existence because it can be borne neither from income nor from savings, such as unlimited liability for personal injury or the permanent loss of earned income. Only such risks should be insured.
Growth in which the stock is multiplied by a constant factor each period instead of a constant amount being added. A large part of the growth arises towards the end of the period.

Exports of goods and services in relation to a country's economic output. In Germany it has been around 40% for years, in the USA it is in the low teens. The ratio shows how strongly foreign demand feeds through to domestic profits.
Regression coefficient that indicates how strongly the return of a fund depends on a factor. A value of 1 corresponds to the full factor; long-only ETFs usually reach 0.3 to 0.5.

Systematic excess return of a long-short portfolio formed on the basis of a characteristic. Geometric US figures from 1963 to July 2026: market 6.15%, momentum 6.33, value (HML) 3.10, quality (RMW) 2.81, investment factor (CMA) 2.74, size (SMB) 1.72. These academic factors take no account of costs, taxes or short-selling limits and are therefore not investable products.
siehe: Fama-French models, Value factor, Momentum, Smart beta

text: Product with constant daily leverage on a strategy index. Because of the daily reset, it is path-dependent. In volatile sideways markets, a systematic volatility loss arises that costs money even if the underlying ends up unchanged.

Bond issued as investment grade and later downgraded to the speculative range. Index exclusion and regulatory selling pressure usually push the price down further than the changed probability of default explains.
Observable finding, set in advance, whose occurrence means that an assumption or the entire valuation counts as refuted, for example a margin below a threshold in two consecutive quarters.

Extensions of the CAPM: the three-factor model (market, SMB, HML; 1993), the Carhart four-factor model (plus momentum; 1997) and the five-factor model (plus RMW and CMA; 2015). For US portfolios, the five-factor model explains over 90% of the dispersion of returns, the CAPM only around 70%. HML and CMA are so strongly correlated, at 0.68, that Fama and French regard HML as largely redundant in the five-factor model.
siehe: Capital asset pricing model (CAPM), Factor premium, Value factor, Quality factor

text: Tendency to regard what is familiar as safer and easier to assess. Related to it is home bias, in which investors weight their home market more heavily than its share of the world market warrants.

Owner-occupied residential property that passes tax-free under Section 13(1) nos. 4a to 4c ErbStG (Inheritance and Gift Tax Act). For acquisitions on death, the exemption for spouses and children is conditional on ten years of owner-occupation and, for children, is also limited to 200 square metres of living space.

Free cash flow divided by market capitalisation or, more cleanly, by enterprise value. It is the most direct yield indicator for a share because it starts from the cash available instead of from book profit. As with free cash flow itself, comparability depends on the definition, in this case that of the denominator.
siehe: Free cash flow, Enterprise value, P/E ratio, Multiples

text: FCFF is the cash flow to all providers of capital: EBIT × (1 − s) + depreciation − capital expenditure − change in working capital. FCFE is the flow to the owners only: FCFF − interest expense × (1 − s) + net new borrowing. FCFF is discounted at the WACC and leads to the enterprise value; FCFE is discounted at the cost of equity and leads directly to the equity value.
siehe: Discounted cash flow method (DCF), Weighted average cost of capital (WACC), Enterprise value, Free cash flow

text: Rule of thumb that compares the earnings yield of the stock index with the yield on ten-year government bonds. Edward Yardeni gave it its name in 1997. It is theoretically questionable because it compares a real quantity with a nominal one, and it has no demonstrable predictive power.
Movement in which the price leaves a zone and returns to it within a few periods. The breakout thesis is thereby refuted and not merely postponed.

Deposit with a fixed term and a fixed interest rate, as a rule not available before maturity, or only with a deduction. The interest advantage over an instant-access savings account compensates for tying up the money; the saver bears the interest rate risk on reinvestment.
siehe: Instant-access savings account, Deposit protection, Yield curve

text: Money with no claim to redemption in a commodity. Its value rests solely on general acceptance and on the scarcity policy of the issuing central bank. Since 1971 this has applied to all major currencies.

First in, first out. When selling, under Section 20(4) sentence 7 EStG (Income Tax Act) the units bought first are mandatorily deemed to have been sold first, and this applies per securities account. An instruction from the customer to sell the expensive units is irrelevant for tax purposes. The order can only be influenced by using separate securities accounts or sub-accounts.

For securities held in collective safe custody, under Section 20(4) sentence 7 EStG (Income Tax Act) the units bought first are deemed to have been sold first. When rebalancing, the oldest units with the highest gains are therefore realised.

Tax rule under Section 20(4) sentence 7 EStG (Income Tax Act) according to which, for securities of the same kind in the same securities account, the units bought first are deemed to have been sold first.

begriff: Deemed sale at the end of 2017 (fiktive Veräußerung)
text: Under Section 56(2) InvStG (Investment Tax Act), all fund units are deemed to have been sold on 31 December 2017 and newly acquired on 1 January 2018. For old units acquired before 2009, there is an allowance of €100,000 on the increases in value from 2018 onwards.

Reduction of government debt through an interest rate kept artificially below inflation, supported by regulation and capital controls. The creditor is paid in full in nominal terms, but only partly in real terms.

Measure of how many euros gross domestic product rises by when the state spends one additional euro. It is not constant and, depending on capacity utilisation, the central bank's response, the import ratio, the type of measure and the credibility of the financing, lies between close to zero and more than two.

Expenses that cannot be changed in the short term because they are tied to contracts, notice periods or laws. Regular expenses are not automatically fixed costs: groceries arise every month but can be influenced immediately.

Bond with a floating coupon that is reset periodically as a reference rate (such as 3-month Euribor or €STR) plus a fixed margin. The price stays close to 100, and interest rate risk is almost zero. The credit risk, however, remains unchanged.
Fear of missing an opportunity. It is not a cognitive bias in its own right and arises from the interplay of social proof, envy, recency bias and the urge to act. That is why it is so hard to resist.

Pool of assets managed collectively, into which many investors pay. Its units reflect the value of the portfolio. Retail funds launched in Germany or authorised under UCITS have fund assets that are kept separate from the assets of the fund management company (for German funds, usually segregated fund assets, known as Sondervermögen) and are therefore ring-fenced from an insolvency of the fund management company.
siehe: Segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen), UCITS, Exchange-traded fund (ETF)

text: Liquidation of a fund by the fund management company. The units are settled at net asset value, and the gain accrued up to that point is compulsorily realised and taxed, regardless of whether the timing suits the investor.

Country in which the fund is domiciled, recognisable from the first two characters of the ISIN (IE = Ireland, LU = Luxembourg). It determines the applicable double taxation agreement and therefore the non-refundable withholding tax on dividends within the fund's assets.

Pension insurance policy whose balance is invested in funds. The tax advantages are tax deferral, tax-free fund switches and the 12/62 rule. Together with the partial exemption (Teilfreistellung) of 15%, effectively only around 42.5% of the gain is then taxable. Set against this are typical market reductions in yield (Effektivkosten) of about 1.8% to 2.7% a year. A direct ETF savings plan, including the TER, usually costs less than 0.3%.

A binding or conditional statement by a central bank about its future interest rate path. It lowers today's long-term interest rates without deploying money, but costs credibility if the pledge later has to be broken.

Loan that locks in the interest rate for later follow-up financing up to 60 months in advance. It costs a forward premium for each month of lead time and must be drawn down; otherwise a non-acceptance fee (Nichtabnahmeentschädigung) is charged. You do not benefit from falling interest rates. It serves as a hedge against rising interest rates, not as speculation.

Deliberately staking a fraction c of the Kelly fraction. The growth rate is then (2c − c²) times the maximum, and the probability of a decline to the fraction a of capital is a to the power of (2/c − 1).

The same information leads to different decisions depending on how it is worded. In Tversky and Kahneman's Asian disease problem (1981), 72% chose the certain option when it was described as “saves 200 lives”, but only 22% when the same option was worded as “400 die”. In investing, the frame also plays a part in the decision: “minus 30%” and “back to the level of three years ago” describe the same portfolio.

In simplified terms, operating cash flow minus capital expenditure on property, plant and equipment and intangible assets. There is no statutory definition; some companies deduct only replacement investment or exclude lease repayments. Before comparing the free cash flow figures of two companies, you should therefore always check the reconciliation.
siehe: Cash flow statement, Owner earnings, FCF yield, FCFF and FCFE

text: Cash flow left for the owners after interest, repayments and new borrowing. It is discounted at the cost of equity and gives the value of equity directly.

begriff: Free cash flow to the firm
text: Cash flow to all providers of capital, calculated before interest as EBIT × (1 − tax rate) + depreciation − capital expenditure − increase in working capital. It is discounted at the WACC and gives the enterprise value.

The freely tradable part of the share capital, excluding strategic fixed holdings. Index providers weight by free-float market capitalisation so that the index weight corresponds to what investors can buy on the market.

Threshold from which the entire amount, and not just the excess, becomes taxable. Under Section 23 EStG (Income Tax Act), the gain remains tax-free only if it is less than €1,000 per person per year; for other income under Section 22 no. 3 EStG, only if it is less than €256.

Instruction to the bank to exempt capital income up to the amount of the saver's allowance (Sparerpauschbetrag) from tax deduction. A separate order must be given to each bank, and it must include the tax identification number. The Federal Central Tax Office (BZSt) cross-checks the total of all orders nationwide. Without an order, the bank withholds tax from the first euro. An order given only during the year also applies to the advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale) booked in January. Under Section 44b(5) EStG (Income Tax Act), the bank subsequently refunds the tax already paid over on it; if the bank has already issued the tax certificate, the remaining route is the tax return.

Banks' business model in which short-term deposits that can be withdrawn at any time finance long-term, illiquid loans and bonds. The interest margin compensates for the associated risk. The risk materialises when depositors withdraw their money at the same time or when rising interest rates erode the value of the long-dated assets. Silicon Valley Bank failed because of this in 2023.
The property of money of being freely interchangeable. A euro from your salary, from a refund or from a sale is the same euro.

Exchange-traded forward contract that is binding on both parties. For the DAX future FDAX, one index point equals €25; at 20,000 points, the notional value is therefore €500,000. It is settled in cash, and the last trading day is the third Friday of the expiry month.

Change in delta per unit of price change, that is, the curvature of the price curve. Gamma is greatest at the money and shortly before expiry, and it determines how quickly a delta hedge becomes unusable.
Deposits of up to €100,000 per customer and institution. They are exempt from bail-in. In a resolution, deposit protection takes their place and pays out within seven working days.
Arbitrage condition under which the forward rate between two currencies fully reflects their interest rate differential. It determines the ongoing cost of currency hedging.
Difference between the highest bid to buy (bid) and the lowest offer to sell (ask). It is the price of being able to trade immediately and widens when trading is thin and outside core trading hours.
The internal rate of return of all payments. It weights each euro by how long it was invested, measures the investor's result and is abbreviated to MWR.

Market for loans and deposits with maturities of up to one year. Participants are banks, central banks, governments, companies and funds. Private investors can only access it through deposits, funds or short-dated government securities.

Fund that invests in very short-dated deposits and debt instruments and is subject to the EU Money Market Funds Regulation. Short-term money market funds may not exceed a weighted average maturity of 60 days. Money market funds have fund assets that are kept separate from the assets of the management company, but they are not covered by deposit protection.
siehe: Instant-access savings account, Segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen), Deposit protection

text: The money supply is measured in aggregates that build on one another: M1 comprises cash and overnight deposits, M2 also includes deposits with a maturity of up to two years and a period of notice of up to three months, and M3 additionally includes repos, money market fund units and short-term debt securities. In July 2026, M3 in the euro area stood at €17,614 billion, M2 at €16,436 billion and M1 at €11,293 billion, of which only €1,613 billion was cash. A different measure is the monetary base, made up of cash and banks' reserves at the central bank.

Ratio of the money supply to the monetary base. The value is neither constant nor the expression of a causal relationship. It is a ratio that results from the behaviour of banks, non-banks and the central bank.

Tax valuation standard under Section 9 BewG (Valuation Act), specified in more detail for shares in corporations in Section 11 BewG. For listed shares, the lowest price on the valuation date applies; otherwise the value is derived from sales between unrelated third parties or from earnings prospects.

Order of up to €2,000 given by both spouses. It applies to joint accounts and to both spouses' individual accounts at the same institution and allows the bank to offset the losses of one spouse against the gains of the other.

begriff: Community of unit owners (Gemeinschaft der Wohnungseigentümer)
text: Since 1 December 2020, a legal entity in its own right under Section 9a WEG (Apartment Ownership Act). It is responsible for management, concludes contracts, holds the joint assets including the maintenance reserve (Erhaltungsrücklage) and is a party to court proceedings.

A target level of wealth or spending set in advance that does not move up when your income or social environment rises. Without this fixed reference point, the yardstick automatically shifts to the next higher peer group.

The rate at which a single capital sum grows over time, calculated using the logarithm of the period factors. It is always below the arithmetic expected value, and the difference grows with volatility.

The growth rate of wealth achieved on average: (product of all growth factors)^(1/n) − 1. With fluctuating returns, it is always below the arithmetic mean, and the gap widens as the fluctuation increases, because losses weigh more heavily than gains of the same size. For the development of wealth, the geometric mean is the only accurate measure.
siehe: Arithmetic mean, Compound annual growth rate (CAGR), Standard deviation, Maximum drawdown

text: Share of fund assets that the provider has deducted in the financial year for management, custody, auditing and the index licence. The fund's transaction costs, swap fees and taxes at fund level are not included.
A mandatory indicator from 1 to 7 in the key information document, derived from historical fluctuation (market risk measure) and the issuer's default risk (credit risk measure).

Under Section 421 BGB (Civil Code), each of several borrowers owes the full amount, and the creditor can demand it from each of them individually. Agreements on how it is divided apply only between the debtors (Section 426 BGB).

The capitalised excess that a buyer has paid over the remeasured net assets of the acquired company. Under the HGB (Commercial Code) it must be amortised on a scheduled basis; under IFRS it must be tested for impairment every year.
A means of payment that may not be refused in settlement of a monetary debt. The term concerns the obligation to accept it and says nothing about its value.

Statement of income and expenses for a period, presented in vertical format under the HGB (Commercial Code). The nature of expense method classifies by type of expense and in doing so shows changes in inventories and own work capitalised; the cost of sales method classifies by function and instead shows the gross margin. Profit does not equal the cash inflow, because income is recorded when it is realised, not when payment is received.
siehe: Balance sheet, Cash flow statement, Profit margin, EBIT

text: Book money in current accounts, that is, a claim against a commercial bank and not central bank money. It is created through lending, not by lending on savings deposits. The bank books the loan amount as a sight deposit on the liabilities side and the claim on the assets side, a balance sheet expansion without any prior inflow of deposits. Money creation is limited by capital and liquidity rules, profitable demand for credit and the central bank's interest rate policy; reserves do not limit it.

Standard form of securities custody in Germany. All units of a class are held by a central securities depository in a collective holding, in which the investor has fractional co-ownership. This is why they can be separated from the estate if the broker becomes insolvent.

Closing an open derivatives position through the corresponding offsetting transaction; for an option writer, this means buying back the option written. For tax purposes, closing out is a separate transaction with its own time of receipt.
Construction in which every index constituent receives the same share. It requires the weights to be reset regularly and contains a systematic tilt towards smaller companies.

The change in the equity allocation planned over a lifetime (also written glidepath). In theory, it can be justified by shrinking human capital; age itself is not a reason. That is why it runs flat for a long time and only falls steeply in the last years of working life.

Settlement between ten US investment banks and the regulatory authorities in April 2003 for around $1.4 billion. It forced the organisational separation of equity research and the underwriting business.
Weight α with which the current price enters an exponential average. The usual choice is α = 2/(n+1), so that EMA(n) and SMA(n) have the same average lag of (n−1)/2 periods.

Change in the person of the securities account holder. Under Section 43(1) sentences 4 and 5 EStG (Income Tax Act), it counts as a sale for tax deduction purposes unless the transfer is expressly reported as being free of charge.

Debt security with a claim to delivery of physically deposited gold, in Germany for example Xetra-Gold. According to the case law of the Federal Fiscal Court (BFH) from 2015, such securities with a delivery claim are subject to the rules on private disposal transactions (private Veräußerungsgeschäfte), not to those of the flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer).
siehe: Exchange-traded commodity (ETC), Commodity future, Issuer risk

text: Monetary order in which the central bank redeems its currency in gold at a fixed rate. The money supply therefore follows gold holdings. Balance of payments imbalances are corrected through falling domestic prices and wages instead of through the exchange rate.

The excess of the purchase price over the fair value of the net assets acquired. Internally generated goodwill may never be capitalised. Under the HGB (Commercial Code), it is amortised on a scheduled basis, over ten years if its useful life cannot be estimated reliably (Section 253(3) HGB). Under IFRS, it is instead tested for impairment at least once a year. A group whose growth comes mainly from acquisitions with high goodwill deserves particular attention.
siehe: Impairment, IFRS, HGB (German Commercial Code), Balance sheet

text: Present value of a payment growing at g in perpetuity: value = payment(next period) / (discount rate − g). In a DCF, it provides the terminal value; in dividend valuation, the share value. Because the denominator is small, even 0.5 percentage points on the WACC or g change the value considerably, by around 10% if the denominator is 5%.
siehe: Terminal value, Discount rate, Discounted cash flow method (DCF), Present value

text: Price ceiling for defensive investors, calculated as the square root of (22.5 × earnings per share × book value per share). The factor 22.5 is the product of the limits P/E 15 and P/B 1.5.

The change in NOPAT divided by the change in invested capital over several years. It measures what the most recently invested money earns. It can be far below the reported ROIC, because the latter is supported by the legacy business.

The tax rate at which the next euro earned is taxed, as distinct from the average tax rate. In 2026, above the basic tax-free allowance (Grundfreibetrag), the tax scale starts at 14%, reaches 42% from €69,879 of taxable income and 45% from €277,826. The marginal tax rate is decisive for the most-favourable assessment (Günstigerprüfung) and for how much tax a deduction for special expenses (Sonderausgaben) saves.
With an officially fixed exchange rate, the worse money drives the better money out of circulation, because the better money is hoarded. Without a legally enforced rate, the effect is reversed.

Finding from 1980 according to which a perfectly informationally efficient market cannot exist, because nobody would then have an incentive to gather information any more. Markets therefore need a paid minority that does research.

Tax levied by the federal states (Länder) on the purchase price of a property. It arises with the purchase contract and becomes due one month after notification of the tax assessment. In 2026, the rates range from 3.5% in Bavaria through 5.0% (including Baden-Württemberg, Lower Saxony and Thuringia) to 6.5% in Brandenburg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Saarland and Schleswig-Holstein. For a purchase price of €400,000, that is €14,000 instead of €26,000. The difference of €12,000 results solely from the federal state.

The part of income that secures the subsistence minimum and remains tax-free. In 2026, under Section 32a EStG (Income Tax Act), it is €12,348 for single people and €24,696 for joint assessment. Taxpayers below this limit can apply for a non-assessment certificate (NV-Bescheinigung) for capital income and thus also avoid withholding at source.

The nominal capital of an AG (public limited company) laid down in its articles of association, at least €50,000 under Section 7 AktG (Stock Corporation Act). It is divided into shares and determines what fraction of the company a single share represents.

Annual municipal tax on real estate, calculated since the reform effective 1 January 2025 as property tax value (Grundsteuerwert) × tax base rate (Steuermesszahl) × the municipality's multiplier (Hebesatz). In the federal model, the base rate for residential property is 0.31 per mille; several federal states use their own models. The aim was revenue neutrality for each municipality. For the individual owner, the burden can nevertheless rise or fall considerably. As an operating cost, it remains recoverable from tenants.

Intermediate figure in the calculation of property tax (Grundsteuer). It is the property tax value (Grundsteuerwert) multiplied by the tax base rate (Steuermesszahl) under Section 15 GrStG (Property Tax Act), which is 0.31 per mille for residential property. The municipality applies its multiplier (Hebesatz) to the base amount.

Guardrails around the initial withdrawal rate, usually ±20%. If the current rate leaves this corridor, the withdrawal is cut or raised by a fixed percentage. The guardrails form the central part of the set of rules by Guyton and Klinger (2006).

Application under Section 32d(6) EStG (Income Tax Act), made in line 4 of the capital income annex (Anlage KAP), to have capital income taxed at the personal tax rate instead of at 25%. It pays off if the marginal tax rate is below 25% and cannot do any harm, because the tax office automatically applies the more favourable option. The application applies only uniformly to all capital income and only for one year. The income from all banks must be declared.

Measure of how many percentage points of GDP the government budget balance changes by when the output gap shifts by one percentage point. For Germany, the European Commission works with a value of around 0.5.
Version of the efficient market hypothesis according to which all publicly available information is already incorporated in the price. This form is the most disputed in the debate.
Halving of the Bitcoin block reward every 210,000 blocks, that is roughly every four years. The date has been known since 2009 and is therefore not a surprise supply event.

Set of tradable securities defined in advance, together with the trading time window. It is defined by verifiable criteria such as index membership, minimum turnover and minimum price, and not by an assessment made by eye.

The tendency to do something because doing nothing looks worse in hindsight. Bar-Eli and colleagues analysed 286 penalty kicks. Goalkeepers almost always dive to the left or right, although staying put would be the best option. For your portfolio, this means that acting in a crisis feels right but is usually wrong.

Also called a barbell. Portfolio structure consisting of a very safe main part and a small, deliberately risky remainder, with no investments in the medium risk class. Taleb cites a split of roughly 90 to 10 as one variant.
According to Kostolany, investors who have all four Gs, that is, money (Geld), thoughts (Gedanken), patience (Geduld) and luck (Glück). That is why they can buy in the capitulation phase.

Annual meeting of shareholders that decides on the appropriation of profit, the discharge of the management board and supervisory board, the election of the auditor and amendments to the articles of association. It is convened at least 30 days in advance. Amendments to the articles of association usually require three quarters of the share capital represented.

Monthly advance payment towards the costs of the community of unit owners, based on the budget under Section 28(1) WEG (Apartment Ownership Act). It covers operating costs that are recoverable from tenants as well as non-recoverable items such as the property manager's fee and allocations to the reserve.

Ratio of the amount of capital moved to the equity committed. Leverage magnifies gains and losses to the same extent. As soon as an obligation to make additional payments (Nachschusspflicht) or a barrier takes effect, a temporary fall in price becomes a permanent loss.
siehe: Margin (collateral), Knock-out certificate, Contract for difference (CFD)

text: Share class of a fund whose foreign currency positions are hedged against a target currency, recognisable by the suffix “EUR hedged” and by its own ISIN. The net asset value is hedged as of a reference date, not continuously.
The observation that a higher level of consumption becomes the new normal after a few weeks to months. The feeling of happiness returns to its baseline, while the costs remain permanently.

The tendency to invest a disproportionately large amount in shares of your own country. It increases cluster risk because your job, your property and your portfolio follow the same business cycle. Japan in 1989 is the most costly documented case.

Following the behaviour of others, even against your own perception. Asch showed that 74% of participants gave an obviously wrong answer at least once, just because the group gave it. When tested alone, the error rate was below 0.7%. In markets, the effect is amplified because rising prices seem to confirm the consensus after the fact.

The German Commercial Code (Handelsgesetzbuch), the basis of German financial reporting, is geared towards creditor protection and prudence: acquisition cost as the upper limit of valuation, and the realisation and imparity principles (Section 252 HGB). The size classes in Section 267 HGB determine the scope of the financial statements, the audit requirement and disclosure; small corporations have a balance sheet total of up to €7.5 million, revenue of up to €15 million and up to 50 employees. The same facts can result in completely different balance sheets under the HGB and IFRS.

Highest unit value a fund has ever reached. After a loss, a performance fee with a high watermark is only charged again once this level has been exceeded. Without this rule, the investor pays twice for the same gain.

Bonds below investment grade, that is, from BB plus downwards, with a correspondingly higher coupon and default risk. If an issuer is downgraded below the investment grade threshold, it is regarded as a fallen angel, and many regulated investors have to sell its bonds.
Highest unit value that a fund must exceed before a performance fee is charged again. This prevents a fee from being charged merely for making up a loss.
Abbreviation for High Minus Low. The factor buys shares with a high book-to-market ratio (value) and sells growth shares short. The premium is 3.59% p.a. (USA, 1926-2026).

Overweighting of domestic shares in your own portfolio. As of 31 August 2026, Germany has a weight of less than 2.4% in the MSCI World and is not among the five largest countries, while the share of the USA is 72.14%. Investors who fill their portfolio with DAX shares are thus unknowingly placing a concentrated bet on a small segment of the world market.

Form of advice in which only the client pays and inducements from third parties are passed on to the client. The legal bases are Section 64 WpHG (Securities Trading Act) for investment firms and Section 34h GewO (Trade, Commerce and Industry Regulation Act) for independent fee-based financial investment advisers (Honorar-Finanzanlagenberater).

The present value of all a person's future earned income. For most people in work under 50, human capital is their largest asset. It can be neither traded nor borrowed against, but it can be valued and insured.

Harmonised consumer price index calculated according to uniform European rules. The ECB measures its 2% target against the HICP and not against the national CPI, which makes it the relevant measure for monetary policy.

Extreme loss of the value of money, usually from a price rise of about 50% a month. More important than the level of the rate is the collapse of the functions of money. Money first loses its function as a store of value, then as a unit of account and finally as a means of payment.

Rule in Section 19(3) ErbStG (Inheritance and Gift Tax Act) under which, if a value threshold is exceeded, the additional tax may amount to at most half of the excess above the threshold, or at most three quarters for tax rates above 30%.

Index of the Federal Statistical Office (Destatis) for the price development of residential property. It covers the properties sold, including the land, uses a hedonic method to strip out the influence of characteristics such as size and location, and is regularly rebased to a new base year, most recently in June 2026 to 2025 = 100. Values with different base years must not be mixed.

The maximum interest rate permitted under supervisory law that life insurers may use to calculate guaranteed benefits under Section 2 DeckRV (Actuarial Reserves Ordinance). Since 2025 it has been 1.0%, and it applies only to the savings portion after costs, not to the entire premium.

Monthly business climate index based on around 9,000 responses from German companies, made up of the assessment of the current situation and expectations. In August 2026 it stood at 88.8 points, after 86.7 in July. Like every survey indicator, it measures sentiment and is available early, but it does not replace hard data.

International Financial Reporting Standards, geared towards information and investors and considerably more open to fair value accounting than the HGB (Commercial Code). Capital-market-oriented groups in the EU report under IFRS, while the single-entity financial statements remain subject to commercial law. For financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2027, IFRS 18 replaces IAS 1 and requires subtotals as well as the disclosure of self-defined performance measures.
siehe: HGB (German Commercial Code), IFRS 16, Adjusted metrics, Balance sheet

text: Leasing standard, applicable to financial years from 1 January 2019. The lessee recognises a right-of-use asset and a lease liability; exceptions apply only to terms of up to twelve months and to low-value assets. As a result, EBITDA, EBIT, the balance sheet total, net debt and operating cash flow rise, and the equity ratio falls. Time series spanning 2019 and HGB-IFRS comparisons are therefore only meaningful after adjustment.
siehe: IFRS, EBITDA, Net debt, Equity ratio

text: Abbreviation for Investable Market Index. In addition to large and mid-sized listed companies, this index variant also includes small ones and thus covers the investable market almost completely.
Matching the duration of a bond portfolio to the date of a future payment obligation, so that changes in interest rates leave the final value practically unchanged.

Unscheduled write-down to the lower recoverable amount; under IAS 36, goodwill must be tested for impairment at least once a year. Once recognised, a goodwill impairment may never be reversed. Large impairments have no cash effect, but they are an admission that an earlier purchase price was too high.

The excess return over the risk-free rate that can be backed out from the current price level and expected distributions. It is the counterpart to the historically realised premium. The two methods currently produce values that are several percentage points apart.
Costs that are not charged as a fee and arise from a worse price. They include half the spread, market impact and delay costs. They do not appear in any fee statement.

Excess return of equities over the risk-free rate, backed out from the index level and expected distributions, that is, a reverse DCF at market level. As of September 2026, Damodaran reported 4.14% for the S&P 500.

The volatility that, when entered into an option pricing model, exactly reproduces the market price. It is forward-looking, whereas historical volatility looks backwards. On a long-term average, implied volatility is higher than the fluctuation subsequently realised. This difference is the volatility risk premium that option writers receive as compensation for the risk of rare, very large losses.

Growth rate of the cash flows at which the present value of a valuation model exactly equals the current market price. It depends on the other assumptions and should therefore always be stated as a range.

Indicative net asset value, calculated every 15 to 60 seconds during trading hours. Market makers base their binding bid and ask prices on it. Large deviations between the price and the iNAV are a warning sign of market phases with low liquidity.
siehe: Net asset value (NAV), Market maker, Spread

text: Calculated measure that reflects the performance of a defined basket of securities. What matters are the selection rules, the weighting method and whether dividends are included. An index is not investable; it can only be replicated through funds or derivatives.
siehe: Total return index, Price return index, Exchange-traded fund (ETF)

text: Price movement that arises because index funds must buy a newly included security by the effective date and this demand is predictable.

Fund that replicates an index instead of making its own selection decisions. Its aim is the index return less its own costs. Most ETFs are exchange-traded index funds, but there are also actively managed ETFs.
Estimated value of the fund assets per unit, calculated every 15 to 60 seconds during trading hours. Market makers base their binding bid and ask prices on it.

Rise in the general price level, measured by the consumer price index or by the European harmonised HICP. In August 2026, as a result of the surge in energy prices, the rate was 2.9% in Germany and 3.2% in the euro area. The ECB measures inflation using the HICP; since the 2021 strategy review, its medium-term target has been a symmetric 2%.

Bond whose face value and coupon are linked to a consumer price index. It delivers a real return; the issuer bears the inflation risk. Ten-year US TIPS yielded 2.61% in real terms on 17 September 2026.

Active return divided by tracking error: IR = E(Rp − Rb) / standard deviation(Rp − Rb). It measures how much excess return was achieved per unit of deliberate deviation from the benchmark index. As a guide, a value of around 0.5 applies to a manager in the top quartile.
siehe: Tracking error, Alpha, Sharpe ratio (Sharpe-Verhältnis), SPIVA

text: Situation in which market participants only observe the actions of others and no longer use their own information. A cascade looks like a broad consensus but rests on the judgement of a few and can therefore easily reverse.

Security that embodies a claim against the issuer. Certificates, warrants and ETNs belong to this category. If the issuer becomes insolvent, a total loss is possible, regardless of how the underlying performs.

begriff: Bearer bond with delivery claim (Inhaberschuldverschreibung mit Lieferanspruch)
text: Security that embodies a claim to delivery of the deposited metal. For tax purposes, the Federal Fiscal Court (BFH) treats it like physical gold, that is, under Section 23 EStG (Income Tax Act) instead of Section 20 EStG.
Collateral that must be deposited when opening a futures position. It is a pledge and not a purchase price. The clearing house sets its amount on a risk basis.

Change in operating profit divided by the additional capital tied up in the same period. It measures what the most recently invested euro has earned, instead of the average of all earlier investments.

The present value of all payments that an asset will generate over its remaining life. Because every input is an estimate, it can only be stated as a range. The market price shows the price, intrinsic value the equivalent you receive for it.
siehe: Margin of safety, Discounted cash flow method (DCF), Present value, Economic moat

text: Reserve that the community of unit owners builds up to finance major repairs to the common property. Since the Apartment Ownership Modernisation Act (Wohnungseigentumsmodernisierungsgesetz) of 2020, it has been called Erhaltungsrücklage. The flat rates in Section 28 II. BV (Second Computation Ordinance), graduated by the age of the building, serve as a basis for calculation; in 2002 they were €7.10, €9.00 or €11.50 per square metre of living space per year. Since 2005 they have been adjusted to consumer prices every three years, and since 1 January 2026 they have been €11.50, €14.58 or €18.62.
Restoring competitiveness through falling wages, prices and employment when a country has no exchange rate of its own. Within a monetary union it serves as a substitute for a devaluation.
The interest rate at which the present value of all payments of an investment is zero. In spreadsheets, it can be calculated with XIRR, and it is the basis of every investor return.

Remuneration model in which an intermediary is paid for referred, funded accounts or with a share of trading turnover. The intermediary's income depends on the trading volume of the referred customer and not on the customer's trading result.

Situation in which the yields on short maturities are higher than those on long maturities. In the USA, every recession since 1966 was preceded by an inversion, but not every inversion was followed by a recession. The longest inversion in the series, 25 months from November 2022 to November 2024, had not been followed by an NBER recession as of September 2026.

Method of thinking in the tradition of Carl Gustav Jacobi and Charlie Munger. Instead of asking how something succeeds, you ask how it is certain to fail and then avoid those mistakes. Applied to investing, this produces a short list (high costs, concentration, borrowing, acting under stress) whose avoidance achieves more than searching for the best individual security. Not to be confused with the inversion of the yield curve.
Interest-bearing debt plus equity, excluding excess liquidity and non-operating assets. From the asset side, the same amount is obtained as fixed assets plus working capital.

The CMA factor (Conservative Minus Aggressive). Companies with low growth in their balance sheet total earn higher returns on average than those with aggressive asset growth. The US premium from 1963 to July 2026 was 2.74% a year in geometric terms (t = 3.27). The correlation with value is 0.68, so the two characteristics largely describe the same thing.
siehe: Factor premium, Value factor, Fama-French models, Quality factor

text: Rating range from AAA/Aaa to BBB−/Baa3. Below it begins the speculative range (high yield). The boundary is anchored in regulation, because fund mandates, indices and the capital rules for banks and insurers are tied to it.

First listing of a share on the stock exchange (Initial Public Offering), with a prospectus requirement under the EU Prospectus Regulation. The price is set in bookbuilding, in which the syndicate banks collect subscription orders within a price range. The over-allotment option (greenshoe) then serves to stabilise the price. The company receives fresh capital only in a capital increase; if existing shares are placed, the proceeds go to the previous owners.

Position with four legs, namely a short put spread below and a short call spread above the price. It earns the credit as long as the price stays within the middle band. The maximum loss is the wing width minus the credit.

Twelve-character international securities identification number under ISO 6166, beginning with the two-letter country code of the place of issue and ending with a check digit. For ETFs, it shows the fund domicile, for example IE for Ireland, LU for Luxembourg and DE for Germany.
siehe: WKN (German securities identification number), Securities account, Exchange-traded fund (ETF)

text: Agreement between the stated and the achieved hit rate. You are well calibrated if you are right in about 90% of cases with statements made at 90% confidence.

Increase in the real tax burden when incomes rise only because of inflation and the progressive tax scale stays unchanged. The legislator offsets it fully or partly by raising the thresholds of the tax scale every year.
Reducing a position that has grown too large without selling, with new contributions flowing exclusively into the core until the weighting is right again. The method avoids tax but takes time.

Request from a closed-end fund to the investor to pay in part of the subscribed commitment. The timing of the call determines how long capital is tied up and therefore the reported internal rate of return.

The decision on how a company uses the surplus it has generated: reinvestment, acquisition, debt repayment, dividend, share buyback or building up cash. All these uses are measured against the same hurdle, the cost of capital.

Proportion of shares and comparable equity investments that a fund's investment conditions commit to on an ongoing basis. Above 50%, the fund counts as an equity fund, and at 25% or more as a mixed fund, under Section 2(6) and (7) InvStG (Investment Tax Act).

Part of the balance of payments that records the net acquisition of foreign assets less newly incurred liabilities. It is the arithmetical mirror image of the current account. A current account surplus is therefore always also a capital export.

The ability, checked by the bank, to service interest and repayments from income on a lasting basis. It is the basis of the creditworthiness assessment required under Section 505a BGB (Civil Code) and is calculated using flat-rate cost-of-living allowances, not the household's actual expenses.

Issue of new shares in return for contributions, resolved by the annual general meeting or drawn from authorised capital, which may amount to at most half of the share capital. Without participation, the existing shareholder's share of voting rights and profit is diluted.
siehe: Subscription right, Share, Annual general meeting (AGM)

text: The technical form in which the flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) is levied. The domestic bank withholds 25% directly and pays it over to the tax office without naming the investor (source principle). With foreign brokers that do not deduct German tax, this automatic deduction does not take place. You must then declare the income yourself in the capital income annex (Anlage KAP).
The wealth tied up by each euro of monthly withdrawal. The multiple is twelve divided by the assumed withdrawal percentage and, at 3.5%, is around €343 per euro of monthly payout.

Statement of cash receipts and payments, divided under IAS 7 into operating, investing and financing activities. It serves as a check on reported profit, because profits can be shaped, account balances less easily. In practice, the indirect method predominates: profit for the period plus non-cash items plus the change in working capital.
siehe: Free cash flow, Income statement, Working capital, Depreciation

text: Amount of fixed and current assets tied up per euro of revenue. With low capital intensity, growth requires little additional capital.

Straight line of all combinations of the risk-free investment and the tangency portfolio: E(Rp) = Rf + ((E(Rm) − Rf)/Sigma_m) × Sigma_p. Its slope is the market price of risk. It implies Tobin separation, according to which everyone holds the same risky mix and controls risk only through the share of the safe investment.
siehe: Tangency portfolio, Efficient frontier, Sharpe ratio (Sharpe-Verhältnis), Capital asset pricing model (CAPM)

text: Present value of all inflows minus present value of all outflows. If it is positive, the project is worthwhile at the chosen discount rate.
Phase at the end of a bear market in which even the last holders sell on high volume, although it is hard for them. It typically coincides with the worst news and the price low.
Upper limit on the weight of an individual security, set out in the index rulebook. Among other things, it ensures that the index can still be replicated within the investment limits for UCITS funds.
The quantity of goods that a sum of money can buy at a given point in time. It is the relevant measure of wealth; the nominal amount alone says little about it.

The idea that identical baskets of goods cost the same worldwide and that exchange rates tend towards this in the long run. It is in tension with uncovered interest parity and the carry trade. If interest parity held, the carry trade would not be profitable in expected value terms. In the short term, none of the three concepts explains exchange rates reliably.

Real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer, 3.5% to 6.5%), notary and land register (together around 1% to 1.5%) and, where applicable, the buyer's share of the estate agent's commission, which with a common total commission of 7.14% including VAT is 3.57%. In total, depending on the federal state and whether an estate agent is involved, this comes to around 4.5% to just under 12% of the purchase price. The incidental costs do not increase the mortgage lending value and must therefore come from own funds as far as possible. Since the Act on the Distribution of Estate Agent Costs (Gesetz über die Verteilung der Maklerkosten, 2020), a consumer buying a flat or a single-family house as a rule bears at most half of the commission.

Purchase price divided by annual basic rent, also called the multiplier (Vervielfältiger), and therefore the reciprocal of the gross rental yield. A factor of 25 corresponds to 4% gross, a factor of 40 to only 2.5%. It says nothing about location, condition and tenancy law and is no substitute for a net calculation.

Collection of all notarised purchase contracts in a district, kept by the valuation committee (Gutachterausschuss) under Sections 192 et seq. BauGB (Federal Building Code). It is the basis of the property market reports and the standard land values (Bodenrichtwerte) and the only source of purchase prices paid.

Price-to-book ratio, that is, market capitalisation divided by balance sheet equity. For banks and insurers, P/B = (ROE − g) / (cost of equity − g) applies approximately. A P/B above 1 is therefore only justified if the return on equity is above the cost of equity. For companies whose value lies in intangible assets not recognised on the balance sheet, the P/B ratio is largely meaningless.
siehe: Return on equity (ROE), Multiples, Value factor, Net-net

text: Staking rule that maximises long-term geometric growth of wealth. For a bet with win probability p, loss probability q and odds b, f = p − q/b. In continuous form, with logarithmic utility, it corresponds to the Merton fraction (mu − r)/(gamma × Sigma²). Betting full Kelly produces extreme fluctuations, which is why in practice half Kelly is usually used.
siehe: Ergodicity, Geometric mean, Expected value, Maximum drawdown

text: Price index of personal consumption expenditures excluding food and energy, published by the US agency BEA. It takes account of substitution between goods. The Fed's 2% target refers to the overall PCE index and not to the consumer price index CPI; the Fed uses core PCE as a measure of the underlying trend.
Portfolio structure consisting of a broadly diversified, low-cost core and clearly limited deviations. Even without satellites, the core must be a complete portfolio.

Price development excluding energy and food, which are stripped out because they are volatile and obscure the trend, not because they are unimportant. The gap between the headline rate and the core rate shows the nature of a shock. In August 2026, the US headline rate according to the consumer price index (CPI) was 3.4% and the core rate 2.4%, that is, one percentage point lower, which points to a pure supply shock. For your own purchasing power, the headline rate is what counts. The targets of the Fed and the ECB also refer to the headline rate; the core rate serves them as an indication of the underlying trend.

A bank's Tier 1 capital divided by its risk-weighted assets. Basel III requires at least 6% for this ratio and at least 4.5% for the common equity Tier 1 ratio, which counts only common equity Tier 1 capital, in each case plus buffers. Large European banks usually have a common equity Tier 1 ratio of between 13% and 16%. If the ratio falls, the bank has to raise capital or scale back its business.

Chart showing the open, high, low and close for each interval. The body lies between the open and the close, and the wicks extend to the high and the low. A candlestick chart contains the same information as a bar chart.

Share price divided by earnings per share. It links a market figure with an accounting figure and is therefore susceptible to accounting policy, differences in debt levels and earnings cycles. For the S&P 500, the trailing P/E was 26.1 in September 2026, compared with a historical median of 15.1.
An observation defined in advance at which a check is stopped and a candidate rejected. It is noted down before the analysis of the figures begins, so that it cannot be argued away later.

Surcharge of 8% in Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg and 9% in the other federal states, calculated on the capital income withholding tax (Kapitalertragsteuer). Because it also acts as a special expense (Sonderausgabe), the capital income withholding tax rate falls to 24.45% according to the formula e/(4+k) (with k = 0.09). The decisive factor is the place of residence, not the bank's registered office. The bank automatically requests the church tax deduction indicator (Kirchensteuerabzugsmerkmal) from the Federal Central Tax Office (BZSt); a blocking notice (Sperrvermerk) can be lodged until 30 June.

Coded information on religious affiliation that banks retrieve automatically once a year from the Federal Central Tax Office (BZSt) under Section 51a EStG (Income Tax Act). A blocking notice (Sperrvermerk) only prevents the retrieval; the church tax is still owed.
An accumulation of several risks from the same source, for example when your job, a portfolio position and the location of your property depend on the same company or the same industry.

Leveraged product with a strike price and a barrier, whose price roughly equals the distance between the underlying's price and the strike price multiplied by the ratio. If the barrier is touched, the product expires immediately, and a later recovery is of no use. The leverage is not constant and rises as the price nears the barrier.
Price threshold at which a leveraged certificate ends immediately when touched. Monitoring is based on the trading hours of the underlying and not on those of the certificate.

The year in which the pension starts fixes the taxable portion of the pension for life. For pensions starting in 2026, it is 84%. The portion rises by 0.5 percentage points for each cohort and reaches 100% in 2058.
A single order with which all legs of a strategy are executed at a specified net premium or not at all. It prevents risks between the individual executions and double costs from the bid-ask spread.

The area in which an investor can reliably assess a business model. According to Buffett, you must above all know the edge of this area precisely; its size is secondary. Familiarity with a product does not establish a circle of competence.
Enquiry for a non-binding offer, transmitted as “Anfrage Kreditkonditionen”. Unlike the “Anfrage Kredit”, it is not passed on to other contracting parties and does not weigh on the credit score.

Calculated figure under Section 5 of the Article 115 Act (Artikel-115-Gesetz) that is used to strip out the cyclical part of the deficit under the debt brake (Schuldenbremse). It widens permissible borrowing in a downturn and narrows it symmetrically in an upswing.

Fluctuation of overall economic capacity utilisation around the long-term growth path, measured by output, income, employment and consumption. Phases and lengths are irregular, and the turning points are only established in retrospect.
The value that analysts and market participants expect on average for a figure not yet published. Prices already reflect it; price movements only arise from a deviation from it.

Average of all recorded individual forecasts by analysts or strategists for a figure such as an index level, earnings per share or an interest rate. It serves as a benchmark, and deviations from it are regarded as a surprise.
Checking and completing the insurance account with Deutsche Rentenversicherung (German statutory pension insurance, DRV) so that periods of training, child-raising and care are fully recorded.

Risk that the counterparty to a transaction defaults, for example in swaps or securities lending. It is limited by collateralisation, daily valuation and several counterparties, but cannot be eliminated completely.
Number of units of the underlying per option contract, usually 100 shares for equity options. For index options, a multiplier in euros per index point replaces the number of units.

Tendency No. 16 in Munger's list. Amounts are judged relative to the comparison value next to them instead of in absolute terms. That is why ongoing charges look harmless next to a large portfolio value.
The premium over the stock market price that a buyer pays for a majority stake in a company. Synergies must first earn this amount before a takeover creates value for the buyer's shareholders.
The perception of being able to control random outcomes. It is reinforced by tools such as charts, indicators and real-time portfolio views.

Account under Section 7 of the Article 115 Act (Artikel-115-Gesetz) in which deviations of net borrowing during budget execution from the permissible upper limit are recorded. If the negative balance exceeds a threshold, it must be reduced in line with the economic cycle.

Second-order correction that improves the linear approximation given by duration for larger changes in interest rates. Positive convexity works in the investor's favour. When interest rates fall, the price rises more than predicted; when they rise, it falls less sharply.
Risk that a large part of the portfolio's value depends on a few positions. In the MSCI World, around 26.6% was accounted for by ten securities on 31 August 2026.

Normalised covariance between −1 and +1: Rho = covariance / (Sigma_A × Sigma_B). It is not stable and typically rises in crises; diversification therefore tends to help little just when you need it. Values for US equities based on monthly data from 2008 to 2026: with developed market equities 0.87, with emerging markets 0.76, with real estate equities 0.75, with corporate bonds 0.45, with gold 0.08 and with long-dated government bonds −0.07.
siehe: Covariance, Diversification, Standard deviation, Rebalancing premium

text: Covariance divided by the product of the standard deviations. It is dimensionless, lies between −1 and +1 and measures only linear co-movement.
Cycle model with six phases (A1 to A3 upwards, B1 to B3 downwards) that uses trading volume and the number of holders as signals, not the price. Buying takes place in A1 and B3, selling in A3 and B1.

Measure of the co-movement of two return series and the fundamental quantity in portfolio theory. The portfolio variance is Sigma_p² = sum over i and j of wi × wj × Sigma_ij. With equal weighting, it converges towards the average covariance as the number of securities grows. This average covariance is the unavoidable systematic risk.
The third term of the portfolio variance (2·wA·wB·σA·σB·ρ). It is the only part that can become negative and therefore contains the entire mathematical effect of diversification.

A benefit from statutory health insurance paid after six weeks of continued pay from the employer, for the same illness for a maximum of 72 weeks within three years. It replaces around 70% of gross pay, but at most 90% of net pay.
The mutual reinforcement of credit expansion, rising asset prices, rising collateral values and renewed credit expansion, and the reversal of this process in a crisis.
The markedly higher correlation between risky assets measured in periods of stress. It arises from common risk factors, from forced sales and partly from measuring on extreme observations.

Fixed interest rate of a bond, always based on the face value and never on the purchase price. A bond with a 2.5% coupon pays €2.50 per €100 of face value, regardless of whether it was bought at 91.53 or at 112.

Market value divided by balance sheet equity. For financial companies, the P/B ratio is the key valuation measure, because P/B = (ROE − g) / (cost of equity − g) applies approximately. A P/B ratio cannot be interpreted without the corresponding return on equity.

Price per share divided by earnings per share. This corresponds to the number of years' earnings contained in the price. The P/E ratio is a relative classification and not a valuation. The trailing P/E of the S&P 500 was 26.64 on 13 October 2026, while sector values range from around 15 for banks to over 100 for semiconductors.
Market capitalisation divided by annual revenue. On its own, the ratio has no informative value. It can only be interpreted with an assumed target margin, because fair P/S = net margin × fair P/E.

Index without reinvestment of dividends. The S&P 500, Euro Stoxx 50, Dow Jones and Nikkei are usually quoted as price return indices. A direct chart comparison with the DAX is therefore distorted by around two to three percentage points a year.

Price range between the high of one interval and the low of the next (or vice versa) in which no trading took place. A price gap cannot be seen on a line chart, because a line chart connects the closing prices without any gaps.

Price-to-sales ratio, market capitalisation divided by revenue. The ratio can also be applied where there is no profit yet, and for that reason it leaves open whether the revenue will ever turn into profit. EV/sales is more consistent, because the debt then also appears in the numerator.
siehe: Multiples, P/E ratio, Enterprise value, Profit margin

text: Health insurance for pensioners (Krankenversicherung der Rentner). Compulsory membership under Section 5(1) no. 11 SGB V (Social Code Book V, health insurance) for pensioners who had statutory health insurance for nine tenths of the second half of their working life. Contributions are then payable only on the pension, pension-type income (Versorgungsbezüge) and earned income, not on capital income and rents.

Pattern described by Ray Dalio that spans several decades. The level of debt rises over several short interest rate cycles until debt service grows faster than income. After that, the remaining ways out are austerity, default, redistribution and money creation.

The risk of living longer than your own capital lasts. Withdrawal rules can limit it. It can only be handed over completely through lifelong annuity payments, which come at the expense of being able to leave an inheritance and of flexibility.

Flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) that is not yet due on unrealised price gains. It does not appear on any securities account statement, but it reduces the value the investor can dispose of after tax.

Munger's image of a lattice of important mental models from different disciplines into which experiences can be fitted. It is the counter-model to the specialist who tackles every situation with the same tool.
Coupon divided by price. It does not take into account any price gain or loss up to maturity and is therefore lower than the yield to maturity for a bond below par and higher for a bond above par.

The additional interest for tying up capital for a long time. It compensates for the fact that the investor cannot react to interest rates that rise in the meantime and bears the inflation risk for the entire term.
Repayment order in which, once all minimum instalments have been paid, every spare euro goes towards the debt with the highest interest rate. It is mathematically optimal.
Monthly instalment divided by the list price, times one hundred. It makes offers roughly comparable but says nothing about the term, the mileage and the initial payment.

The automatic growth of spending along with income. It lowers the savings rate and at the same time raises the target wealth required. It thus makes financial independence harder to reach in two ways.

Sale of borrowed securities in the expectation of falling prices. The gain is limited to 100%, while the loss is theoretically unlimited. In the EU, uncovered short sales of shares and government bonds are prohibited. Net short positions in shares must be reported from 0.1% of the share capital and are made public from 0.5%; for government bonds, different reporting thresholds apply, without publication.

Summary of cross-border flows of goods, services, primary income and secondary income, broader than the trade balance alone. In the twelve months to May 2026, the euro area recorded a surplus of €271.6 billion (around 1.7% of GDP), while the US recorded a deficit of $212.6 billion in the first quarter of 2026 according to revised figures. Arithmetically, a surplus means capital exports, and it can also arise because imports fall more sharply than exports.

Subsidy from the long-term care insurance fund under Section 43c SGB XI (Social Code Book XI, long-term care insurance) towards the care-related co-payment in a care home. It is graded by length of stay and amounts to 15% in the first year, 30% from the 13th month, 50% from the 25th and 75% from the 37th month.

The interest rate set by the central bank, by which the money market takes its bearings. In the euro area, this is the deposit facility rate. With full allotment since October 2008 and the excess liquidity, it became the decisive rate in practice; since March 2024, the ECB has explicitly steered its monetary policy stance through this rate. The ECB raised it to 2.50% with effect from 16 September 2026; the main refinancing rate is 2.65% and the marginal lending facility rate 2.90%. The Fed raised its target range to 3.75% to 4.00% with effect from 17 September 2026. Changes in key interest rates take effect with long, variable and uncertain lags.
The central bank's role of providing unlimited liquidity to solvent banks against good collateral during a panic. From 1930 to 1933 this role was not performed; since then it has been standard.

ROE = ROA + (ROA − interest rate on debt) × debt/equity. As long as the return on total capital is above the interest rate on debt, borrowing raises the return on equity. If it is below, borrowing lowers the return on equity with the same leverage. A high ROE can therefore only be assessed together with the equity ratio.
siehe: Return on equity (ROE), Return on assets (ROA), Equity ratio, DuPont analysis

text: Spending that rises with income rather than with prices. The savings rate stays constant even though the financial leeway has grown. The effect only becomes visible over years.

Order with a price limit. Purchases are made at no more than the limit, sales at no less than the limit. The limit order protects against execution at a poor price, but it may remain unexecuted or be only partly executed.

The ability to trade larger quantities without any significant price movement. For ETFs, what counts is the tradability of the underlying securities and the number of market makers, not the fund size, because new units can be created at any time.

First-degree liquidity = cash and cash equivalents / current liabilities; second-degree liquidity additionally includes short-term receivables and securities, and third-degree liquidity has all current assets in the numerator. Common benchmarks under the German-language convention are 0.2, 1.0 and 1.2. They are values as of the balance sheet date and can therefore easily be flattered by window dressing around that date.
siehe: Working capital, Current assets, Interest coverage ratio, Balance sheet

text: Axis scaling in which equal vertical distances correspond to equal percentage changes. On such a scale, constant percentage growth appears as a straight line and accelerating growth as an upward curve.

Labour costs per unit produced; their change roughly equals wage growth minus productivity growth. They, and not the size of the collective pay settlement, determine how much price pressure a wage round creates.

Charlie Munger's term for the coming together of several cognitive biases that act in the same direction. Social proof, envy, deference to authority and action bias together explain bubbles and total losses better than any single effect. In practice, individual biases are therefore less dangerous than situations that trigger several of them at once.

Loan secured by a pledge of securities whose lending value is only a fraction of their market value. If the portfolio value falls, the lending value falls too, and the bank makes a margin call or sells the securities. The forced sale typically hits the investor at the worst possible moment.

Error in which an analysis uses information that was not yet available at the simulated decision date, for example annual financial statement figures from the balance sheet date instead of from their publication. It makes backtests systematically too good. A related problem is the retrospective correction of index levels and fundamental data in databases.
siehe: Backtest, Survivorship bias, Overfitting, Smart beta

text: Empirical finding that shares with a low beta deliver higher risk-adjusted returns than the CAPM predicts, and shares with a high beta lower ones. The explanations put forward are borrowing constraints, the preference for lottery-like shares and benchmark incentives.

Shares with low volatility and low beta have historically achieved at least market-like returns with considerably lower risk. Frazzini and Pedersen show that the security market line is too flat in 18 of the 19 markets they examined. The anomaly is explained by leverage constraints, a preference for lotteries and the benchmark incentives of fund managers. Novy-Marx and Velikov counter that a large part of the premium depends on the unusual weighting of the betting-against-beta portfolio and shrinks after trading costs.
siehe: Beta, Factor premium, Smart beta, Capital asset pricing model (CAPM)

text: Add-on to the premium of a mature market, derived from the country's default spread multiplied by the relative volatility of its equity market. According to Damodaran (as of 5 January 2026), it is 0.00% for Germany and 3.24 percentage points for Brazil.
Present-value-weighted average point in time of all the payments of a bond, measured in years. It is also the investment horizon at which price risk and reinvestment risk offset each other.

Greenblatt's ranking system based on two ratios: earnings yield = EBIT / enterprise value and return on capital = EBIT / (net working capital + net fixed assets). The two rankings are added together, financials and utilities are excluded, 20 to 30 shares are held and the list is re-sorted once a year. The formula deliberately combines a low valuation with return on capital, that is, value with quality.
siehe: EV/EBIT, Return on invested capital (ROIC), Value factor, Quality factor

text: Minimum balance that a margin account must hold. If the balance falls below it, a margin call follows. If the additional payment is not made, the position is forcibly closed out.

Ratio of a profit measure to revenue. Gross margin = (revenue − cost of sales)/revenue measures pricing power, operating margin = EBIT/revenue measures operating efficiency, and net margin = net profit/revenue measures what is left after interest and taxes. The gross margin can only be read off directly under the cost of sales method.
siehe: EBIT, Income statement, DuPont analysis, Return on invested capital (ROIC)

text: Collateral for derivative transactions, not a down payment. Eurex calculates it on a portfolio basis and books gains and losses daily as variation margin. If the account falls below the maintenance margin, a margin call follows and, if necessary, a forced close-out.

Graham's margin of safety, the discount between the estimated intrinsic value and the price paid. It protects against your own estimation errors, not against price losses. The more uncertain the forecast, the larger it must be.
siehe: Intrinsic value, Discounted cash flow method (DCF), Net-net, Economic moat

text: Rule from the 2018 ESMA measure. If the account balance falls below 50% of the initial margin required for the open positions, the provider must close the positions.

Price movement that an order triggers through its own volume when it uses up several price levels of the order book. Market impact grows disproportionately with order size and falls the higher the liquidity is.

Market participant who quotes binding bid and ask prices and earns the spread in return. On Deutsche Börse, market makers for shares are called designated sponsors. For ETFs, they take their bearings from the iNAV. The number of market makers and the liquidity of the index constituents therefore determine the spreads more than the fund size does.

Order to be executed at the next available price, without a price limit. Execution is as good as certain, the price is not. In thin order books or outside core trading hours, it can deviate considerably from the last price.
State of low order book depth. Even small orders move the price, spreads widen in periods of stress, and positions can only be unwound over several days.
Weighting of the securities in a portfolio by their market capitalisation. Only with this weighting does a portfolio reproduce the market true to scale. Sharpe's argument rests on this.

Stock market value of a company, calculated as the share price times the number of shares outstanding. It is the usual weighting measure in indices, but it only measures the value of the equity. For the total value of the company, net financial debt has to be added.

Weighting by the stock market value of the freely tradable shares. It is the only weighting that all investors can hold at the same time, and therefore the reference point against which every deviation is an active bet.

Expected excess return of the equity market over the risk-free rate; in the CAPM, the factor by which beta is multiplied. On 1 September 2026, Damodaran reported an implied US premium of 4.14%, and for Germany, as of January 2026, a total equity risk premium of 4.23% with a country risk premium of zero. Valuation practitioners often work with higher, historically derived values. In the KPMG cost of capital study, the figure used for Germany was 6.7%.
siehe: Capital asset pricing model (CAPM), Weighted average cost of capital (WACC), Beta, Discount rate

text: Largest percentage decline from a previous peak to the subsequent low. The recovery is asymmetric: required recovery gain = 1/(1−d) − 1. After −20%, a gain of 25% is needed, after −50% one of 100% and after −80% one of 400%. Measured in euros, the MSCI World lost a maximum of 53.6% between May 2001 and March 2009.
siehe: Standard deviation, Value at risk, Sortino ratio, Compound annual growth rate (CAGR)

text: Problem that arises when many hypotheses are tested at the same time. The number of false alarms then rises linearly with the number of tests, and the usual significance threshold of t = 1.96 loses its meaning.

Pricing rule for exchange auctions. Execution takes place at the price at which the highest volume is achieved; in the event of a tie, the smaller surplus decides. This is how the opening and closing prices are determined on Xetra.
Statement of how many units of foreign currency one unit of the domestic currency costs. EUR/USD 1.10 means that one euro costs $1.10. If the number rises, the euro appreciates.

Richard Thaler's concept of mental accounting. Money is fungible, but people keep it in separate accounts in their minds. Investors who book dividends as income and price gains as wealth make different and usually worse decisions than if they looked at the total return. Likewise, people keep expensive consumer debt while a low-interest savings account sits alongside it.

Money is sorted in the mind into separate accounts according to its origin and purpose and treated differently depending on the account, even though every euro has the same value and the same possible uses.

Purchase of the shares of a takeover target below the offer price after the takeover has been announced. The only thing rewarded is the risk that the deal fails and the price falls back to its level before the offer.

EU Regulation on Markets in Crypto-Assets, which has applied in stages since 2024: first the rules for asset-referenced tokens and e-money tokens, then the authorisation and conduct obligations for service providers. It creates supervision as well as prospectus and reserve requirements, but no investor protection against price losses and no deposit protection.

Imputed deduction for unrecoverable rent, vacancy and unsuccessful legal action. Under Section 29 II. BV (Second Computation Ordinance), it amounts to at most 2% of the income. It is a calculation parameter, not a forecast.

In tight housing markets designated by a federal state ordinance, the rent for a new tenancy may be at most 10% above the local comparative rent under Sections 556d et seq. BGB (Civil Code). In 2025 the rule was extended to the end of 2029. Exempt are new buildings first used after 1 October 2014, comprehensively modernised flats and cases where the previous rent was already higher. For index-linked rents, it applies only to the initial rent, not to later adjustments.

The gross rental yield is the annual basic rent divided by the purchase price, a quick indicator that ignores incidental costs and running costs. Only the net rental yield allows a comparison: (annual basic rent − operating costs not recoverable from tenants) divided by (purchase price + incidental purchase costs). Without an imputed interest charge on your own funds, the purchase is systematically made to look better than it is.

Annual Morningstar study that compares the fund return and the investor return of the same funds over ten years. According to the 2026 edition, they were 9.9% and 8.7% a year respectively in the decade to the end of 2025.

Floor from which contributions to voluntary statutory health insurance are calculated. It amounts to one third of the monthly reference value (Bezugsgröße), around €1,318 in 2026. Even insured persons without regular income pay contributions on this notional amount.

Amount that a Riester saver must pay in personally to receive the full state allowance. It is 4% of the previous year's gross earnings subject to pension insurance contributions, at most €2,100, less the allowances, but at least €60. If less is paid in, the allowance is reduced in the same proportion.

Balances that banks must hold with the central bank. In the Eurosystem, the requirement is 1%, mainly on customer deposits and debt securities with a maturity of up to two years, remunerated at 0% since 20 September 2023. Minimum reserves do not steer the money supply, but they stabilise the money market because they only have to be met on average over a period of six to seven weeks. Accordingly, the money multiplier does not describe a causal chain. The ratio of US M2 to the monetary base fell from around 9.2 in August 2008 to 2.8 in August 2014 and stood at 4.2 in July 2026.

The portfolio with the lowest volatility on the efficient frontier, its left-hand vertex. For two assets: w1 = (Sigma2² − Sigma12) / (Sigma1² + Sigma2² − 2 × Sigma12).
