With a correlation of −1, a portfolio with no variance at all would even be possible arithmetically, which does not occur in real markets.
siehe: Efficient frontier, Covariance, Tangency portfolio, Correlation

text: The point at which leveraged investors have to sell assets in order to service their debts. The sales make prices fall further and force further sales.

Trade concluded at a price that is obviously not in line with the market. Cancellation must be requested promptly (within 30 minutes on Xetra, within two trading hours in specialist trading on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange), and the price must deviate from the fair market price by a minimum amount.

Under Section 559 BGB (Civil Code), 8% of the modernisation costs may be added permanently to the annual rent, capped at €3 per square metre within six years, or at €2 where the initial rent is below €7 per square metre. Pure maintenance expenditure must be excluded and cannot be passed on to tenants.
Macaulay duration divided by (1 + yield). It indicates approximately by what percentage the price falls if the market yield rises by one percentage point.
Measure of the interest rate sensitivity of a bond or a bond fund. It indicates approximately by what percentage the price falls if the market yield rises by one percentage point.

Factor that buys recent winners and sells losers. The return is usually measured from month −12 to month −2; the most recent month is left out because of short-term reversal. With 6.07% a year since 1927, momentum has the highest raw premium after the market, but also a crash risk. In 2009 the factor lost 52.8%, 34.4% in April alone, and the maximum drawdown since 1932 was 78.4%. The crashes typically occur when the market turns after a slump and the losers rise sharply.
siehe: Factor premium, Value factor, Fama-French models, Maximum drawdown

text: Abbreviation for Winners Minus Losers. The factor buys the winners of months −12 to −2 and sells the losers short. Of the factors other than the market, it has the highest premium and the highest crash risk.

Abrupt loss of a momentum strategy at the turning point after a bear market, because the high-beta losers that have been sold short rise the most in the recovery. One example is April 2009, with a monthly return of −34.4%.
Position of the price relative to the strike price: in the money (with intrinsic value), at the money (price roughly equal to the strike price) or out of the money (without intrinsic value).

Method that generates thousands of random return paths in order to obtain a distribution of outcomes instead of a point forecast. A sensible set-up includes real returns after costs and taxes, withdrawals in the correct order, 10,000 or more paths and reporting of the success rate and the size of the shortfall. The assumption of a normal distribution and constant volatility systematically underestimates extreme losses.
siehe: Expected value, Standard deviation, Value at risk, Ergodicity

text: Imaginary figure devised by Benjamin Graham. Mr Market is a business partner who names a price for your share every day, sometimes a reasonable one, sometimes one driven by fear or greed. You may accept his offer, respond to it or ignore it.

Index of around 1,250 constituents from 23 developed markets, weighted by free-float market capitalisation. The US share was 72.9% on 30 September 2026, and the ten largest shares made up 27.9%. In terms of countries, it is therefore not diversified worldwide.

Decline in the valuation multiple (for example the P/E ratio) during the holding period. It reduces the investor's return even if revenue and profit grow as planned, and it is the norm for highly valued growth stocks.

Relative comparison using ratios, not a valuation. Numerator and denominator must match. The P/E and P/B ratios relate equity measures to the price, while EV/EBIT and EV/EBITDA relate measures for total capital to enterprise value. The classic mistake is to mix price with EBITDA or enterprise value with net profit.
siehe: P/E ratio, P/B ratio, EV/EBIT, Enterprise value

text: Decline in the valuation multiple, for example the P/E ratio, while profit stays the same or even rises. It can push the price return below profit growth for years.

Valuation using comparative ratios. The median of a multiple from a peer group is applied to the corresponding figure of the company being valued. The method provides a relative comparison and no absolute value.

Money-weighted return, mathematically the internal rate of return of all payments in and out. It measures what the investor has actually earned, including the effect of the timing of their entries and exits. With regular deposits, a comparison with the time-weighted index return shows a gap even without any bad decision if the later years, in which more money is invested, turn out weaker than the earlier ones.
siehe: Time-weighted return (TWR), Compound annual growth rate (CAGR), Expected value

text: Loss aversion combined with short evaluation periods. The more often a portfolio is looked at, the more often losses are visible and the more risk-averse the decisions become, even though the return stays the same.

Contributions to the statutory pension and to the basic pension (Basisrente) reduce tax today; in return, the later pension is taxable. The decisive factor is the year in which the pension starts. For pensions starting in 2026, 84.0% is taxable; the remainder stays unchanged for life as a fixed tax-free amount in euros. Since the Growth Opportunities Act (Wachstumschancengesetz), the taxable portion rises by only 0.5 percentage points per cohort and does not reach the full 100% until 2058.
The growth rate that a company can achieve on its own, without new shares and without higher borrowing. It is calculated as g = ROE × (1 − payout ratio).

Component of the pension adjustment formula under Section 68 SGB VI (Social Code Book VI, pension insurance). It dampens the pension adjustment when the ratio of equivalent pensioners to equivalent contributors rises. Until 2031, it is overridden by the 48% floor (Haltelinie).
Bond that is serviced after all other creditors in the event of insolvency. The higher coupon is the compensation for this weaker position in the ranking.

Loan with a qualified subordination agreement (qualifizierter Rangrücktritt). Repayment can only be demanded once all other creditors have been paid, and only if it does not drive the debtor into insolvency. Common form of contract in real estate crowdinvesting, without segregated fund assets and without deposit protection.
Demand by the lender to put up additional collateral or cash after a fall in prices. If it is not met, the institution sells the securities itself.

Obligation to pay in money beyond the amount invested if a leveraged position goes into the red. BaFin (Federal Financial Supervisory Authority) prohibited it for contracts for difference with retail clients in 2017.
Right to increase the insured benefit without a new health check on certain occasions such as marriage, the birth of a child, a jump in salary or the purchase of a property.

Line connecting the two intermediate lows of a head-and-shoulders pattern. In chart analysis, a break of this line is regarded as the trigger signal. The calculated price target is the height of the head above the neckline, projected from the breakout point.
The unemployment rate at which inflation neither rises nor falls. It cannot be observed and can only be estimated, with uncertainty bands of several percentage points.
Tendency to derive causal stories from random data because an explanation feels more right than chance. A remedy is to ask which verifiable figure supports the story.

The tendency to construct a coherent story from unconnected events after the fact. On the stock exchange, it leads to every price movement being given an explanation, even though the explanation only arose after the movement. The term was coined by Taleb.

The real interest rate at which an economy grows with full employment and stable prices, called r-star in the literature. It cannot be observed, is estimated and has fallen in the developed economies since the 1980s. Central banks use it to judge whether their policy is expansionary or restrictive.
siehe: Key interest rate, Real interest rate, Monetary policy

text: The real interest rate at which the economy operates at full capacity without generating price pressure. It cannot be observed and is estimated with a considerable band of uncertainty.

Limitation of a retail client's loss to the balance of the CFD account concerned. An obligation to make additional payments beyond this balance is excluded. The protection applies per account and not per position.

For bonds, the amount to which the coupon and repayment relate; the price is quoted as a percentage of this amount. For shares, the portion of the share capital. Today, German companies almost without exception use no-par-value shares.
Current assets less all liabilities and provisions, with fixed assets valued at zero. Graham only bought below two thirds of this value.

Graham's net current asset value: current assets minus all liabilities. Graham systematically bought shares only below two thirds of this value, so that the current assets alone covered the price. In developed markets, genuine net-nets are rare today and are mostly very small, illiquid stocks.
siehe: P/B ratio, Margin of safety, Value factor, Current assets

text: Interest-bearing financial liabilities less cash and short-term securities. The figure is not defined by law, which is why companies treat pensions and leases differently.
Value of all the fund's assets less liabilities, divided by the number of units. It is determined once a day and is the price for issues and redemptions as well as in a fund liquidation.

Gross pay less wage tax (Lohnsteuer), solidarity surcharge and church tax where applicable, and social security contributions. In 2026, these are 18.6% for pension insurance, 14.6% for health insurance plus an average additional contribution of 2.9%, and 3.6% for long-term care insurance (4.2% for childless persons aged 23 and over). In addition, there is unemployment insurance. Apart from the long-term care supplement for childless persons, employer and employee each pay half of the contributions.

Annual basic rent less the operating costs not recoverable from tenants, divided by the purchase price plus incidental purchase costs. Of the rental yield ratios, it is the only one that is comparable with the return on other investments.

Policy without a built-in sales commission, where the advice is paid for by a fee. It is only comparable with a commission-based policy or a securities account if the fee is included in the cost calculation.
Balance of the premiums paid and received across all legs. A debit means a cash outflow on opening and is also the maximum loss. A credit means an inflow and is the maximum profit.
The sum of all assets (accounts, securities portfolio, property, surrender values) less all debts. It is the only figure that accurately reflects the progress of wealth building.

Short-term and long-term financial liabilities including lease liabilities under IFRS 16, less cash and short-term securities. There is no binding definition; pension provisions are included or not, depending on the convention. The usual covenant ratio net debt / EBITDA shows how many years of EBITDA would be needed for repayment.
siehe: Debt-to-equity ratio, Enterprise value, EBITDA, IFRS 16

text: Each additional participant increases the value of the offering for all existing ones. This must be distinguished from mere size, where additional customers only bring revenue but no additional value.

Deutsche Börse market segment for growth companies that existed from 1997 to 2003, with its own set of rules and more than 300 listed companies. Its selection index, the Nemax 50, lost more than 96% between March 2000 and October 2002.

Certificate issued by the tax office for the place of residence (form NV 1 A) for persons whose taxable income remains below the basic tax-free allowance (Grundfreibetrag). It exempts all capital income from withholding, is valid for at most three years and is subject to revocation under Section 44a(2) EStG (Income Tax Act).
Right to use an asset and to draw its income without being the owner (Section 1030 BGB, Civil Code). Its capitalised value under Section 14 BewG (Valuation Act) reduces the taxable value of a gift.

Announcement on 15 August 1971 that the convertibility of the dollar into gold would be suspended, combined with a wage and price freeze and an import surcharge. Since then, the international monetary system has been based on pure fiat money without metal backing and, since March 1973, also on flexible exchange rates between the major currencies.
The value of the underlying to which a contract relates, for the FDAX, for example, index level × €25. It is neither the capital invested nor the market value of the contract.
Operating profit after tax but before interest, calculated as EBIT times (1 − tax rate). It belongs to all providers of capital jointly.

Earnings obtained by applying the average margin over a complete business cycle to current revenue. They correct the distortion that makes cyclical stocks look cheap at the earnings peak and expensive in the trough.

Operating profit adjusted for one-off and non-cash items, but not for recurring expenses that a company reports as special items. It typically lies between the income statement figure and the company's own adjusted figure.
Response, laid down in advance, to a crash, a loss of income and an automatic tax debit. It also covers the cases in which, explicitly, nothing happens.

A savings buffer of three to six months' expenses, available daily and without price risk, usually in an instant-access savings account covered by deposit protection. It protects against forced sales and against using the arranged overdraft, and it is not an investment.
The currency in which a fund unit or an index is reported. It is purely a unit of account and says nothing about the currencies of the securities held, and therefore nothing about the currency risk.

Non-assessment certificate (Nichtveranlagungsbescheinigung) for persons whose taxable income is not expected to exceed the basic tax-free allowance (Grundfreibetrag) of €12,348 (2026). It is applied for at the tax office using form NV 1 A. It exempts all capital income at the bank from withholding, that is, also above the €1,000, is valid for at most three years and always ends on 31 December.

Segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen) made up of properties, with continuous issue of units. Since the KAGB (German Investment Code) of 2013, a minimum holding period of 24 months and a notice period of 12 months apply; in the event of liquidity shortages, redemptions may be suspended for up to 36 months.

German abbreviation for undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities (Organismus für gemeinsame Anlagen in Wertpapieren), UCITS in English. The EU framework for retail funds contains requirements on diversification, redemption, derivatives and supervision and is implemented in Germany in the German Investment Code (KAGB).
Effective leverage of an option or a warrant, calculated as simple leverage times delta. Omega indicates by what percentage the instrument responds to a 1% movement in the underlying.

Outright Monetary Transactions, an ECB programme announced in 2012 for the unlimited purchase of short-dated government bonds, tied to reform conditions. It was never used and worked through its announcement alone.
Cash surplus from ongoing business operations. Under the indirect method, it is derived from net profit, plus non-cash expenses and less the increase in working capital.
Forgone return of the best alternative not chosen. It does not appear on any statement and is often the largest item when capital is tied up.
The after-tax return that the own funds tied up in the property would have earned elsewhere. If this item is missing from the comparison, the purchase appears cheaper than it is.

Physical replication with a subset of the index constituents. An optimiser selects the positions so that the country, sector and size structure of the index is matched, and leaves out illiquid micro-caps. This saves trading costs and creates a small additional tracking error.

The right, but not the obligation, to buy (call) or sell (put) an underlying at the strike price. The buyer pays the premium, and the option writer takes on the obligation. The loss risk of an uncovered short call is theoretically unlimited, while that of a short put is limited to the strike price minus the premium.

Securitised option issued by a bank, with a small denomination and a ratio, tradable without access to a derivatives exchange. Differences from a standard option: issuer risk, pricing by the issuer with its own volatility assumption, and no possibility of becoming an option writer yourself.
The benefit of available money that, irrespective of the interest it earns, lies in the actions it makes possible and in the forced decisions it avoids. It increases with uncertainty.

List of all open buy and sell orders by price and quantity. The spread results from the highest bid price and the lowest ask price, and market depth from the order volumes at the best price and at the following price levels. In a thin book, large orders move the price against the order itself.

Part of a data series that was not used when developing a strategy, for example the period after a product was launched. Only in this part can an excess return count as a finding, because there it is not a consequence of the selection.

Testing a pattern that has been found on data that was not used in its construction, for example data from other periods, countries or asset classes. It is the most important safeguard against overfitting.
Stake above the Kelly fraction. From twice f* upwards, the growth rate is zero or negative, even though the expected value per trade remains positive.

Overconfidence in three forms: overestimation of your own ability, overprecision through forecast intervals that are too narrow, and overplacement relative to others (in Svenson 1981, 93% of the US students surveyed placed themselves in the better half of their group for driving skill). It is measurably costly. In Barber and Odean's study, men traded 45% more than women, which reduced their net return by 2.65 percentage points a year, compared with 1.72 percentage points for women.

Fitting a model to random patterns in past data instead of to a genuine relationship. Hou, Xue and Zhang replicated 447 published anomalies; 64% failed the usual significance threshold and 85% failed a t-statistic above 3.0. Because of the multiple testing problem, Harvey, Liu and Zhu call for this higher hurdle for every new factor.
siehe: Backtest, Look-ahead bias, Factor premium, Smart beta

text: Buffett's concept of earnings from the 1986 Berkshire annual report, calculated as reported earnings plus depreciation and other non-cash charges minus average annual maintenance capital expenditure. It differs from free cash flow in the third item, because only maintenance investment is deducted and no growth investment. Buffett explicitly stresses that this figure has to be estimated.
siehe: Free cash flow, Depreciation, Intrinsic value, Cash flow statement

text: Deliberately or unconsciously varying the period, filters, weighting and definition of ratios until a result clears the significance threshold. Every discarded variant is a hidden additional test.

The higher and more uniform the skill of all participants, the more luck decides the ranking. The observed dispersion consists of skill and luck. If the share of skill becomes smaller, luck predominates.

A price of exactly 100% of the face value. A security with a coupon that is high compared with the market interest rate trades above par, and one with a coupon that is too low trades below par. Only at par are the coupon, current yield and yield to maturity equal.

Rebate paid by a trading venue or market maker to the broker for the client orders routed to it. Prohibited in the EU since 28 March 2024 (Article 39a MiFIR), in Germany with a transition period until 30 June 2026.
Group of comparable companies whose multiples are used for a valuation. What matters is similarity in growth, margin, capital intensity and risk, not the industry label.

P/E ratio divided by the expected earnings growth rate as a percentage. Values around 1 are regarded as fair. The ratio combines a fixed figure with an estimate and is only as reliable as that estimate. For the US market as a whole, the PEG stood at 1.90 in January 2026 according to Damodaran.
siehe: P/E ratio, Multiples, Gordon growth model

text: P/E ratio divided by the expected earnings growth rate in percentage points. The ratio takes into account neither risk nor capital requirements and fails when growth is low or negative.
One of the four legally required performance illustrations in the key information document under the PRIIPs Regulation. The four scenarios are called stress, unfavourable, moderate and favourable.

Index in which distributions are notionally reinvested. The DAX is a total return index and stood at 24,490 points at the end of 2025, whereas its price index stood at 9,175 points. Both started at 1,000 on 30 December 1987.

Half-yearly report by S&P Dow Jones Indices that tracks how many of the funds once ranked at the top remain in the top quartile in the following years. The benchmark is the chance expectation of 25% a year.

Rule of thumb for calculating maintenance costs, according to which 1.5 times the construction costs are incurred over 80 years, that is, 1.875% a year. It is not a legal standard and is systematically above the rates in Section 28 II. BV (Second Computation Ordinance), because it includes the full renewal cycle.

Property of leveraged and inverse products that are reset daily, whose result depends on the path in between as well as on the start and end levels of the index. Fluctuations reduce the value, roughly in proportion to the square of the range of movement.

Covered bank bond with dual recourse to the bank and, with priority, to a separate cover pool. This statutory preferential right in insolvency explains the very low spreads. The volume of German Pfandbriefe outstanding was €410.9 billion at the end of 2025.

Classification from 1 to 5 based on a weighted score from six assessment modules of the Medical Service (Medizinischer Dienst). The yardstick is the remaining independence and not the diagnosis. The care level determines the amount of benefits under SGB XI (Social Code Book XI, long-term care insurance).

Private supplementary insurance that pays an agreed fixed amount once a care level (Pflegegrad) has been determined, regardless of the costs incurred and of where the care takes place. Without an indexation option, the benefit loses value in real terms over the term.

Offer to all remaining shareholders that an acquirer must make as soon as it reaches 30% of the voting rights (Section 29(2) WpÜG, Securities Acquisition and Takeover Act). The minimum consideration is based on prior acquisitions and the average share price.

Monetary claim amounting to half of the statutory share of the inheritance, to which descendants, the spouse and, if there are no children, the parents are entitled even if they have been disinherited. It only gives a claim to money and no say in the estate.

Nine yes/no criteria from the balance sheet and cash flow: four on profitability (positive ROA, positive operating cash flow, rising ROA, operating cash flow above net profit), three on leverage and liquidity, and two on operating efficiency. Eight to nine points are regarded as strong, zero to two as weak. Piotroski published the score in 2000 to separate winners from losers within the value universe.
siehe: Value factor, Altman Z-score, Return on assets (ROA), Cash flow statement

text: Purchasing managers' index, a diffusion index with a threshold of 50; values above it indicate growing activity, values below it shrinking activity. It measures the breadth of the change, not its strength. A value of 54 means that more companies are reporting increases, but it does not say by how much. In August 2026, the euro area composite stood at 52.0 and the German manufacturing PMI at 54.3, while German industrial production in July was 1.8% below the previous year's level according to revised figures. Sentiment and revenue can therefore diverge.

Hedging technique that replicates a put option by automatically selling index futures when prices fall. When many market participants follow the same rule, it has a procyclical effect and amplifies the crash, as on 19 October 1987.
Share of the portfolio value that is reallocated within a year. A turnover of 75% corresponds to an average holding period of around 16 months.
Thought experiment before the decision. You assume that the position has turned into a disaster a few years from now and write down the reasons why. This forces you to look for counter-evidence.
Weaker form of market segmentation. According to this theory, investors have a preferred maturity segment and only leave it in return for sufficient compensation.
Process by which prices arise from executed buy and sell orders. It takes place in ongoing trading, with the most recently executed orders, and not in the dormant holdings of investors.
Ability to pass on cost increases to customers without losing volume. It can be checked by looking at how the gross margin develops during periods of inflation.

Difference between government revenue and government expenditure excluding interest payments. Unlike the interest burden from past debt, the primary balance can be controlled directly by policymakers.

Sale of an asset from private assets within the holding period under Section 23 EStG (Income Tax Act), which is one year for movable assets and ten years for land. The gain is taxed at the personal marginal tax rate, and not at all once the period has expired.

Voluntary insurance against the statutory liability under Section 823 BGB (Civil Code), which is unlimited in amount. It covers personal injury, property damage and pure financial loss caused to third parties. A flat-rate sum insured of €50 million is recommended.

Computer-controlled trading that triggers orders according to fixed rules. In the crash of October 1987, the portfolio insurance that was widespread at the time amplified the fall, because falling prices triggered automatic sales that pushed prices down further. The same feedback loop exists today with stop-loss cascades and risk parity strategies.

The German income tax schedule is linear-progressive; the marginal tax rate rises steadily with income from 14% to 42% instead of jumping in steps. Bracket creep (kalte Progression) occurs when incomes grow into higher tax rates purely because of inflation, without any increase in purchasing power. The legislature offsets this by shifting the threshold values of the tax schedule. Under the progression proviso (Progressionsvorbehalt), by contrast, tax-free wage replacement benefits increase the rate applied to the remaining income.

Rule in Section 32b EStG (Income Tax Act) under which tax-free wage replacement benefits such as parental allowance (Elterngeld) or short-time work allowance (Kurzarbeitergeld) increase the tax rate applied to the remaining income.

Consensus mechanism in which deposited coins, instead of computing power, secure validation. In the event of misconduct, part of the stake is lost. Ethereum switched to this mechanism in 2022 and reduced its energy consumption by around 99%.

Consensus mechanism in which computational work decides who has the right to append the next block. Security is paid for with electricity costs. An adjustment of the difficulty keeps the block time at around ten minutes.

Decision theory by Kahneman and Tversky (1979) with four building blocks: evaluation relative to a reference point instead of in terms of final wealth, diminishing sensitivity, loss aversion and non-linear probability weighting. This gives rise to the fourfold pattern: risk-seeking for small probabilities of gains (lottery), risk-averse for high ones (taking a sure gain), risk-averse for small probabilities of losses (insurance) and risk-seeking for high ones (sitting out a loss).

Share or fund position combined with a purchased put whose strike price is below the current price. The loss is limited to the price minus the strike price plus the premium, while the upside is retained.
The premium collected in relation to the capital tied up for it. Extrapolating it to a full year assumes that the rare large loss never occurs.
Analysis before a decision that assumes the decision has already failed and asks for the causes. It produces concrete chains of causes instead of probability estimates (Gary Klein, 2007).
The impression of accuracy that arises when a model turns estimated inputs into a point value with decimal places. The precision of the calculation says nothing about the quality of the assumptions.

Comparison method in which the payments into and out of a closed-end fund are replicated with a stock index on the same dates and the final values are compared. It is the only method that compares irregular cash flows fairly with the stock market.

The decline in an anomaly's return after its publication, because investors know the pattern and act on it. McLean and Pontiff put it at around 32 percentage points in addition to the overfitting discount.

The inevitable convergence of the bond price towards face value as maturity approaches. When a bond is bought below par, it is the second source of return alongside the coupon; when it is bought above par, it is the planned price loss.

Driving up the price of a thinly traded security through coordinated promotion, followed by selling into the demand this creates. It is market manipulation under Articles 12 and 15 MAR (Market Abuse Regulation).

Data set that contains prices, ratios and index compositions in the state in which they were available on each historical day, including securities that later became insolvent or were delisted. Such data are a prerequisite for tests free of look-ahead and survivorship bias.
Forecast that states exactly one value for a point in time, for example an index level at the end of the year. Without a stated probability, it cannot be evaluated afterwards.
Arbitrage relationship for European options with the same strike price and expiry: C − P = S − K·e^(−rT). It holds independently of any valuation model.

Quantitative Analysis of Investor Behavior, DALBAR's annual report on the return gap of US fund investors, published since 1994 with data from 1985 onwards. The four to six percentage points cited in the past were based on a methodology that has since been revised.

Quantitative easing, in which the central bank buys bonds and creates central bank money to pay for them in order to lower long-term interest rates when the key interest rate is at its lower bound. The Eurosystem's balance sheet grew from around €1,154 billion at the beginning of 2007 to a peak of €8,836 billion on 24 June 2022, and the Fed's balance sheet from around $870 billion in August 2007 to $8,965 billion on 13 April 2022.

Quantitative tightening, in which the central bank lets bonds run off or sells them, thereby withdrawing liquidity. As a result, the Eurosystem's balance sheet had shrunk to €5,911 billion by 11 September 2026. Excess liquidity stood at around €2,161 billion in mid-2026 and was still falling. In the US, the process has ended; the Fed's balance sheet reached its low of $6,536 billion on 3 December 2025 and has been growing again since then.

RMW (Robust Minus Weak) captures the higher average return of companies with high operating profitability. Asness, Frazzini and Pedersen define quality more broadly in terms of profitability, growth and safety and find significant results in the US and in a global sample of 24 countries including the US. The US premium of RMW is 2.81% a year, with the lowest volatility of all the standard factors after CMA. Profitability is one of the few of the many published factors that also withstand rigorous tests.
siehe: Factor premium, Fama-French models, Return on invested capital (ROIC), Value factor

text: Reduction of a central bank's securities holdings, usually by not replacing securities as they mature. It withdraws central bank money from the banking system and acts alongside the key interest rate as a second, slower instrument of monetary policy.

Reduction of a central bank's securities holdings, usually passively, by not reinvesting maturing securities. QT works through the stock held and not through the pace, and it does not reverse previous purchases point for point.

Tax withheld by the state of the payer, typically on dividends. Under Section 32d(5) EStG (Income Tax Act), it is credited separately for each item of capital income, at most at 25% and at most up to the amount permitted under the double taxation agreement, usually 15%. Anything beyond that, for example with the Swiss 35%, must be reclaimed in the source country.

Share of dividends that is withheld in the company's country of domicile and does not reach the fund. It reduces the net asset value and, since the 2018 investment tax reform, can no longer be credited by private investors.

Internal bank memo item for creditable foreign withholding tax that could not yet be credited. The bank offsets it against flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) arising in the same year. Unlike the loss pots, the pot is not carried forward; any balance left at the end of the year can only be credited in the tax return for that same year.
Strategy that ranks securities by their past return, buys the strongest and sells the weakest short. It bets on relative strength and not on the direction of the market.

Result of a trade, measured in units of the loss amount set in advance. 1R is the planned loss, and a gain of 2R is twice that amount. Stating results in R makes trades of different sizes and in different markets comparable.

Model in which price changes are random and independent of each other, so that the best estimate for tomorrow is today's price plus any drift. It is the formal counter-position to chart analysis and the practical consequence of the weak form of the efficient market hypothesis. The random walk explicitly includes a positive drift, that is, the risk premium.
siehe: Efficient market hypothesis, Monte Carlo simulation, Standard deviation, Alpha

text: An agency's opinion on the relative probability of default, not a guarantee and not a buy recommendation. The boundary between investment grade and the speculative range lies between BBB minus and BB plus. According to the S&P series from 1981 to 2008, no AAA bond defaulted in any year, while CCC/C reached an annual default rate of 44.6% in 2001.

Return after deducting inflation; in retirement planning it is also taken after taxes. If requirements and capital are stated in today's purchasing power, only this return may be used in the calculation.
Standard deviation of the log returns over a past period, annualised using the square root of the number of periods (252 for daily data). It is a backward-looking measure, not a forecast.
Return after deducting inflation. The correct calculation is (1 + nominal return) divided by (1 + inflation rate), minus 1, rather than the simple difference.
The nominal interest rate minus the inflation rate. It shows how purchasing power changes. With interest at 2.50% and inflation at 2.9%, it is around minus 0.4 percentage points.

Nominal interest rate less capital income withholding tax (Kapitalertragsteuer) and less inflation. For German investors it is the only meaningful figure, because the tax is deducted before inflation. In this way, with inflation at 2.9% (August 2026), a Bund yield of 3.52% (18 September 2026) turns into around -0.3 percentage points of purchasing power.

Resetting the portfolio weights to the target allocation, usually on a schedule or when a band is exceeded. It keeps the risk profile stable and inevitably sells what has risen. Costs and taxes limit how often it makes sense.

Tolerance range around the target allocation, for example five percentage points in absolute terms or a quarter in relative terms. Trading only takes place when the allocation leaves this range. This significantly reduces the number of transactions.

Tolerance band around the target allocation that is set in advance. If the allocation leaves it, the portfolio is shifted back. The question of whether to trade is thus replaced by an observable condition.

Additional return from resetting to the target weights, measured against the weighted average of the individual returns, approximately RB = w1 × w2 × [sd1 × sd2 × (1 − Rho) + (sd1 − sd2)²/2]. It is never negative and is larger the lower the correlation and the higher the fluctuations. For a 50/50 US portfolio of shares and long-term corporate bonds, it amounted to 0.49 percentage points a year from 1926 to 1994 (8.34% versus 7.85%), but without rebalancing the portfolio achieved 9.17%. Compared with a portfolio that is never adjusted, rebalancing costs return when returns diverge strongly; its primary purpose is risk control.
The function of money as a common measure of value. It reduces the number of prices needed from n×(n−1)/2 exchange ratios to n prices.

Cut-off date for determining who is entitled to a distribution or a right. In Germany, it follows the ex-dividend date and serves only for settlement purposes. Voting rights at the annual general meeting are instead determined by the date for proof of shareholding (Nachweisstichtag) on the 22nd day before the meeting (Section 123(4) AktG, Stock Corporation Act).
Second fraud against the same victim. The recovery of lost investment money is offered in return for payment in advance, usually by the same group of perpetrators.

The benchmark value against which an outcome is perceived as a gain or a loss. On the stock exchange, this is usually your own purchase price, less often the all-time high or a target value, but never final wealth itself.

Trade that was executed even though the written set of rules did not provide for it, or provided for it differently. The share of such trades in the trading journal shows whether there is a strategy problem or a discipline problem.

The risk that laws or regulations change the earnings of an industry, through price caps, volume requirements, levies or bans. If a position is heavily concentrated on the regulated business, the risk cannot be eliminated through diversification.
Share of NOPAT that remains in the company as net investment. Multiplied by the ROIC, it gives the sustainable growth rate.

Listed property company that is exempt from corporation tax and trade tax (Gewerbesteuer) at company level and in return must distribute at least 90% of its distributable profit. A German REIT needs at least a 75% property share and a 15% free float. Existing rented residential properties built before 2007 are excluded, which is why the German market has remained very small.
Oscillator between 0 and 100 that indicates the share of the average upward movement in the total movement over the last 14 periods. The usual thresholds are 70 and 30.

Gain in relation to the capital invested, meaningful only when the period, the currency and whether it is adjusted for inflation are stated. From 1928 to 2025, the S&P 500 achieved a geometric nominal return of 10.02% a year, or 6.79% in real terms. At 11.86%, the arithmetic mean is systematically higher and does not describe any achievable performance.

Yield to maturity, the interest rate at which the present value of all future payments equals today's price. It is determined iteratively, because the equation cannot be solved analytically. This implicitly assumes that all coupons are reinvested at this rate.

Permanent reduction of 0.3% per month for starting the pension early, that is, 3.6% per year, up to a maximum of 14.4% for 48 months. The reduction remains in place for life, even after the standard retirement age has been reached, and carries over to the survivor's pension. For those born in 1964 or later, the pension without reductions for particularly long-term insured persons with 45 years counting towards the qualifying period (Wartezeit) only starts at 65.
Number of annual amounts needed as capital to fund a withdrawal over n years at a real return r. The factor is (1 − (1 + r)^−n) / r.

The annuity conversion factor states how much monthly pension is paid per €10,000 of policy value, and thus determines the value of the entire accumulation phase. Annuitisation is based on very cautious mortality tables. A guaranteed annuity conversion factor is therefore more important than a non-binding projection, but it is rarely compared.

The tax-free portion of the pension. It is determined in the first full year of the pension and then fixed as a set amount in euros. Because it does not grow with the pension, later pension increases are fully taxable.
Agreed period during which the pension continues to be paid to surviving dependants even after the death of the insured person. An annuity guarantee period lowers the annuity conversion factor.

Annual statement from the Deutsche Rentenversicherung (German statutory pension insurance, DRV) under Section 109 SGB VI (Social Code Book VI, pension insurance), sent from the age of 27 once five years of contributions have been paid. From 55, the more detailed pension report (Rentenauskunft) follows every three years.

Transitional currency introduced on 15 November 1923, which from 20 November was equivalent to 1 trillion paper marks. It was nominally backed by land charges on agriculture, industry and commerce, but it was not convertible. What stabilised it was the fixed cap on the quantity issued and the end of central bank lending to the Reich.

Defined by law as the pre-tax safeguard level (Sicherungsniveau vor Steuern), that is, the ratio of the disposable standard pension after 45 years at average earnings to disposable average earnings. In 2026 it is 48.0%; under current law, the floor (Haltelinie) applies until 2031. It is a model ratio and not your personal percentage of your last salary. For above-average earners, the gap is considerably larger in percentage terms.

The way in which an ETF tracks its index: physical full replication buys all index constituents, optimised sampling only a representative selection, and the synthetic variant uses a swap. Sampling lowers transaction costs for broad indices but creates an additional tracking error.
Sale of a security combined with a simultaneous agreement to buy it back, economically a secured loan, often overnight. The haircut determines how much money you receive against a security.
Claim to whatever is left after all senior claims have been met. It is what distinguishes equity from debt, and it is the reason for the higher expected return and the greater volatility.
(ROIC − WACC) × invested capital. Only this part of the profit lies above the cost of capital and creates value. The operating variant is called Economic Value Added.

The loan amount still outstanding at the end of the fixed-rate period, calculated as S_k = S0 × (1+i)^k − instalment × ((1+i)^k − 1)/i. With an initial repayment rate of 2%, a large part of the debt is typically still outstanding after ten years and has to be covered by follow-up financing at the interest rate then applicable. This is the central risk of any mortgage financing.

Insurance that covers loan instalments in the event of death, incapacity for work or unemployment. It is only included in the effective interest rate if taking it out is compulsory. For general consumer loans such as instalment loans, it may be concluded no earlier than one week after the loan agreement has been concluded (Section 7a(5) VVG, Insurance Contract Act).

The value that can realistically be obtained at the end of the useful life. With residual value leasing, the lessee is liable for the difference from the calculated value; with mileage-based leasing, the lessor is.

Reversal of the valuation logic in which the current price is taken as given. The calculation shows which growth and which margins the market is pricing in. After that, all that remains is to check whether this expectation is plausible. This is more robust than a point forecast, because your own estimation uncertainty does not enter into the result.
siehe: Discounted cash flow method (DCF), Terminal value, Intrinsic value, Margin of safety

text: Subsequent correction of a published statistic. GDP, employment and industrial production are revised regularly, sometimes considerably. The first release is an estimate and not a measured value.

Two consecutive quarters of shrinking real GDP are regarded as a technical recession; this definition is a rule of thumb used by the press. In the US, a committee of the NBER dates recessions on the basis of the depth, duration and breadth of several data series, often only with a delay of around a year. Because GDP figures are revised several times, the first flash estimate is only an estimate.

State-subsidised private retirement provision with state allowances and a deduction as special expenses (Sonderausgaben). Until the end of 2026, the basic allowance is €175, the child allowance €185 or €300, the minimum own contribution 4% of the previous year's gross income less allowances, and the deduction up to €2,100. The number of contracts is shrinking; at the end of 2025 there were still 14.66 million contracts, of which just over a fifth to just under a quarter are dormant.
The amount of risk needed to reach the goal. If the goal is already secured, the need falls, and an additional equity allocation then brings more danger than benefit.

A bank's total assets, weighted by the default risk of the individual items. Cash and government bonds of the highest credit quality are included with a zero or low weighting, unsecured corporate loans in full. The risk-based capital ratios are measured against this figure, so two banks with the same balance sheet can be capitalised very differently. The leverage ratio (Verschuldungsquote), by contrast, measures Tier 1 capital against an essentially unweighted figure, the total on- and off-balance-sheet exposure.
siehe: Tier 1 capital ratio, Basel III, Bank run

text: Objective ability of a household to bear losses. It results from the investment horizon, income stability, savings buffer, fixed costs and debts.
Subjective willingness to endure fluctuations without selling. It only shows itself reliably in a real decline, and not in a questionnaire.

The degree of fluctuation and loss that someone can withstand without having to abandon the plan. It depends on the investment horizon, the liquidity buffer and how dependent your own income is on the business cycle.

Risk-adjusted net present value. Each cash flow is weighted by the probability that it occurs, so the present value of the success case is weighted by the probability of success and the costs of later development phases by the probability of reaching those phases. The method is standard in the valuation of individual biotech and exploration projects.

Return on total capital: (net profit + interest on debt) / average total capital. The interest is added back because the ratio is intended to measure the return on all the capital employed, regardless of how it is financed. Unlike ROE, it cannot be flattered by borrowing.
siehe: Return on equity (ROE), Return on capital employed (ROCE), Return on invested capital (ROIC), Leverage effect

text: Return on capital employed: EBIT / capital employed, where capital employed = total assets minus current liabilities, that is, equity plus long-term debt. Because it is calculated before tax, it is suitable for comparisons between countries. Old assets that have been largely written off distort it, because their low book value artificially increases the ROCE.
siehe: Return on invested capital (ROIC), EBIT, Return on assets (ROA), Fixed assets

text: Return on equity: net profit / average equity. A high ROE can stem from high borrowing alone and must therefore never be assessed without the equity ratio. Share buybacks shrink the denominator and increase the ROE further. The DuPont decomposition shows which of the three drivers is behind it.
siehe: DuPont analysis, Leverage effect, Equity ratio, P/B ratio

text: Futures contract on a physical commodity that must be delivered at maturity or rolled over beforehand. To stay invested permanently, the investor sells the expiring contract and buys the next one. This gives rise to the main difference in return compared with the spot price.

Return on invested capital, calculated as NOPAT / invested capital, with NOPAT = EBIT × (1 − tax rate). It is the central measure of value creation, because value is only created when the ROIC is above the WACC. Growth with a ROIC below the WACC destroys value.
siehe: Weighted average cost of capital (WACC), Economic value added (EVA), Economic moat, Return on capital employed (ROCE)

text: Analysis of all overlapping sub-periods of equal length in a data series. It shows the range for each holding period, but makes the amount of data seem larger than it is. From 56 years, 42 fifteen-year windows can be formed, but only just under four independent periods.
Contribution to returns that arises solely from switching from an expiring futures contract to one that matures later, regardless of how the spot price develops.

A complete trading transaction consisting of entry and exit. The round-turn costs, made up of order fees, spread and slippage, are expressed relative to the nominal volume traded and multiplied by the trading frequency.

With fractional betting, the probability of falling below a set capital threshold at some point. This does not mean the probability of exactly zero euros, because with this approach the capital never reaches that value.

Price history of an index for periods before it was calculated live, determined by applying today's rules to old data. Because the rules were drawn up with knowledge of these data, the backfilled history systematically overstates the prospects of success.

The amount that a life insurance or pension insurance policy pays out if it is surrendered early. In the first years of the policy, it is usually below the total of the premiums paid in, because acquisition and distribution costs are deducted up front.

Statistical consequence of the fact that an extreme value usually consists of skill and favourable luck. The luck component does not repeat itself, so the next value falls back on average. The effect is purely arithmetical and is not based on any force.

Share of an observed lead that repeats itself on average. It corresponds to the share of skill in the total observed dispersion and grows with the length of the observation period, because the dispersion due to luck shrinks with the square root of the duration.

Parts of equity alongside subscribed capital: the capital reserve from share premiums on the issue of shares, and revenue reserves from retained profits. They show the source of funds on the equity and liabilities side and are not a stock of cash. Only the assets side shows whether liquidity is available.
All costs incurred when a decision is reversed, that is, taxes, fees, cancellation charges, lapsed deadlines and time spent. They are measured as a percentage of the amount invested.

After the fact, an event seems predictable, and your own earlier expectation is unconsciously shifted towards the outcome. It harms investors in two ways, because it makes past crises look harmless and creates the illusion that you will be able to get out in time next time. An effective remedy is a decision journal with dated reasoning, because it makes memory verifiable.

Items on the liabilities side for obligations that are uncertain as to their existence, amount or timing, such as pensions, warranties or litigation risks. Under the HGB (Commercial Code), pension provisions are discounted at the ten-year average market interest rate for their remaining maturity, or optionally at the flat rate for a remaining maturity of 15 years; under IAS 19, they are discounted at the reporting-date yield on high-quality corporate bonds. As a result, HGB and IFRS figures for the same company often differ considerably.
siehe: Balance sheet, HGB (German Commercial Code), IFRS, Reserves

text: Life annuity paid for life (also called basic pension, Basisrente) with full deduction as special expenses (Sonderausgaben), in 2026 up to €30,826 for single people and €61,652 for joint assessment, reduced by contributions to the statutory pension, including the employer's share, or to a professional pension scheme (Versorgungswerk). In return, the contract cannot be surrendered, taken as a lump sum, borrowed against or freely passed on to heirs, but it is protected against seizure and insolvency. The tax advantage is a deferral and not a permanent remission.
Asset with physical substance. The term says nothing about inflation protection; what matters for that is whether there is a cash flow that grows with the price level.

Signal that is triggered when the three-month average of the US unemployment rate is 0.50 percentage points or more above the lowest of the three-month averages over the previous twelve months. Claudia Sahm herself stresses that the rule was intended as a real-time description and not as a forecasting model. In 2024 it was triggered without a recession following. In August 2026 the indicator stood at −0.07 percentage points, so there was no signal.
Upper limit for all active deviations, set in advance as a percentage of total wealth and in euros. Above the limit, positions are capped; below it, they are not topped up.
Many positions carrying the same risks, for example several funds with the same heavyweights or individual shares from one industry.

Nominal increase in value that merely reflects inflation and creates no purchasing power in real terms. German tax law does not adjust capital income for inflation and therefore also taxes illusory gains.
Income credited but not actually earned in a Ponzi scheme. According to case law of the Federal Fiscal Court (BFH), it can nevertheless be taxable (Section 20(1) no. 7 EStG, Income Tax Act).

Personal allowance under Section 16 ErbStG (Inheritance and Gift Tax Act) of €500,000 for spouses and registered civil partners, €400,000 per child, €200,000 for grandchildren, €100,000 for parents and grandparents in the case of inheritance, and €20,000 in tax classes II and III. Under Section 14 ErbStG, all acquisitions from the same person within ten years are added together; after that, the allowance is fully available again. Making gifts early in ten-year steps is therefore the most effective legal form of tax planning.
A repayment order in which the smallest debt is repaid first, regardless of the interest rate. It costs slightly more interest but brings the first visible success sooner.
Investment model in which payouts to existing investors come from the deposits of new investors. It inevitably ends, because the required inflow grows exponentially.

First publication of an official statistic, estimated on an incomplete data basis, for example of gross domestic product around 30 days after the end of the quarter. It is later corrected by the second estimate, the detailed results and benchmark revisions.

Rule in Articles 109 and 115 of the Basic Law (Grundgesetz) that limits the federal government's structural new borrowing to 0.35% of GDP, with a cyclical component and an emergency clause. In 2025 it was relaxed for defence and infrastructure.
Cycle described by Irving Fisher in 1933 in which falling prices increase the real burden of debts fixed in nominal terms. Debtors sell in order to repay, and in doing so push prices down further.

Government debt in relation to annual GDP. In the first quarter of 2026 it stood at 64.4% in Germany, 88.9% in the euro area (89.4% excluding Bulgaria, which joined in 2026) and 122.6% at federal level in the USA, compared with a Maastricht reference value of 60%. Inflation and real growth increase nominal GDP and lower the ratio even without repayment, as long as the level of debt grows more slowly than nominal GDP.
Partial waiver of claims by the creditors of a state. In Greece in 2012, private creditors gave up 53.5% of the nominal value; the loss in present value was around 75%.

According to Nassim Taleb, an event that lies outside expectations, has an extreme impact and seems explainable only after the fact. The third property is the most dangerous, because the event appears inevitable in hindsight and the illusion arises that the next one can be predicted. In practice, an asset structure that rules out a total loss helps more than trying to make better forecasts.

Risk that an optimisation selects the investments with the most favourable estimation errors instead of the best investments. The risk grows with the number of investments and falls only slowly with longer data series.

Numerical value from a credit reference agency that assigns a person to a statistical comparison group and reflects that group's historical default rate. It says nothing about the individual case. Since 2026, the new SCHUFA scale has run from 100 to 999.

Research method coined by Philip Fisher in which customers, suppliers, competitors and former employees are systematically questioned. This produces a picture that does not emerge from the financial statements alone.

For Howard Marks, the first level asks whether a company is good, the second whether it is better than the price assumes. In his view, market sentiment swings between greed and fear. You cannot forecast the cycle, but you can assess where you stand in it. What is meant is checking whether an opinion is already reflected in the price, not contrarianism at any price.

Investment model that assigns typical winning sectors to each phase of the business cycle. It is plausible in retrospect but weak as a forecast, because the phase is unknown in real time and the market anticipates the rotation.
Trading in securities that have already been issued, between investors. The issuer receives no money from it, but its cost of financing depends on the price level on the secondary market.
An agreed amount the policyholder pays per claim. It lowers the premium, because small claims, which are expensive to process, are no longer settled through the policy.

With a lump-sum investment without deposits or withdrawals, the order of returns makes no difference; with a savings plan, bad years towards the end do the most damage; and in the withdrawal phase, the order determines the outcome. Bad years at the start of withdrawals do the most harm, because units have to be sold continually at depressed prices, which is the cost-averaging effect in reverse. Withdrawal planning based on average returns overlooks the case in which the assets are used up prematurely.

The risk that the order of returns determines the outcome. With ongoing withdrawals, bad early years do lasting damage to the portfolio, because units that have been sold no longer take part in the recovery. With a lump-sum investment without cash flows, this risk does not exist.

Disclosure categories of the EU regulation on sustainability-related disclosures. Article 8 applies to products that promote environmental or social characteristics, Article 9 to those with a sustainable investment objective. The classification is not a quality label and can be changed at any time.
The return above the risk-free rate divided by the standard deviation of returns. It measures the return per unit of total fluctuation and treats upward swings in the same way as downward swings.

Excess return per unit of total risk: (Rp − Rf) / standard deviation. It is annualised using the square root of the number of periods, which is why figures without the measurement frequency and period are worthless. Over the long term, broad indices are usually below 1; advertised values well above that should therefore first be checked for period and method.
siehe: Sortino ratio, Information ratio, Standard deviation, Tangency portfolio

text: Price divided by the inflation-adjusted ten-year average of earnings, which smooths out earnings cycles. For the S&P 500 it stood at 40.9 in September 2026, compared with a historical average of 17.4 and a peak of 44.2 in December 1999. Historically it says little about the next one to two years, but it correlates with long-term subsequent returns.
siehe: P/E ratio, Buffett indicator, Multiples, Intrinsic value

text: Price divided by the inflation-adjusted average earnings of the past ten years, also called CAPE. The ratio smooths out business cycles and serves as a valuation measure from which valuation-based withdrawal rules derive their rate.

Share of starting assets that is withdrawn in the first year of retirement and thereafter only adjusted for inflation, without the portfolio running out before the end of the planned period. It is based on historical data, is not a guarantee and depends on the period, market, taxes and costs.

Highest share of starting assets that could be withdrawn, adjusted for inflation, over a fixed period without the capital being used up before the end of the period in any historical starting year. In English it is called SAFEMAX or safe withdrawal rate.

Discount below the estimated intrinsic value at which you buy (Margin of Safety, Graham). It is meant to offset estimation errors. In the model Z/(r − g) with r − g = 7%, a 30% discount can absorb an error of around three percentage points in the denominator.

Ratio of the disposable standard pension after 45 years at average earnings to disposable average earnings, in each case after social security contributions and before taxes. In 2026 it is 48.0%, secured until 2031 by the statutory floor (Haltelinie). It is not a personal percentage of your last salary.

SMB (Small Minus Big) describes the thesis that small companies earn higher returns. Over 100 years of US data the premium is 1.42% a year, but with t = 1.82 it is the only main factor that is not statistically significant. Since 1994 it has been −0.29% a year; it was negative in 35% of all rolling ten-year windows.
siehe: Factor premium, Fama-French models, Survivorship bias, Value factor

text: Long-short return series of small minus large shares according to Fama/French. From 1926 to 2026 it delivered around 1.4% p.a., not statistically significant and negative since 1994.

The dependence of implied volatility on the strike price. For equity indices the curve slopes downwards (reverse skew): out-of-the-money puts are more expensive than calls the same distance away. For currencies it is more symmetrical (smile).
Difference between the price a backtest assumes for execution and the price actually achieved. Slippage arises with market orders, with thin liquidity and with price gaps across a stop level.

Rule-based index strategies intended to make a factor premium investable. They differ from the academic factor for five reasons: long-only instead of long-short, inconsistent factor definitions among index providers, capacity and capping rules, rebalancing costs, and fees and taxes. According to Huang, Song and Xiang, such indices delivered around 3% excess return a year before the ETF was launched, and −0.5% to −1% afterwards.
siehe: Factor premium, Backtest, Overfitting, Tracking error

text: Abbreviation for Small Minus Big. The factor measures the return of shares with a small market capitalisation minus that of shares with a large market capitalisation. Over 100 years the premium is 1.42% p.a., but it is not significant and has been negative since 1994.

Conversion of a lump sum into a lifelong annuity that starts immediately. It hedges longevity risk and thereby eliminates the sequence risk of your own withdrawals, but costs flexibility and the ability to leave the money to heirs. The amount depends on the annuity conversion factor (Rentenfaktor) and on costs. Only the income portion (Ertragsanteil) is taxed.

A 5.5% surcharge on the tax assessed. The exemption threshold (Freigrenze) in force since 2021, which relieves around 90% of taxpayers on income tax, does not apply when capital income withholding tax (Kapitalertragsteuer) is deducted at source. On top of 25% flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer), 1.375 percentage points are always added. On 26 March 2025 (2 BvR 1505/20), the Federal Constitutional Court confirmed that the surcharge is still constitutional.

Pure interest rate on a loan, excluding ancillary costs. In property financing it is fixed for the duration of the fixed-rate period; after that, the market rate prevailing at that time applies. The annual percentage rate (APR) is better suited to comparing offers.

Additional advance payment adopted by resolution when the reserve does not cover a measure. It is allocated according to the applicable cost allocation formula and must be paid by the owner entered in the land register when it falls due.

Legal status of the assets of an investment fund set up in Germany in contractual form (Section 1(10) KAGB, German Investment Code), which are held separately from the assets of the fund management company at an independent depositary. If the company becomes insolvent, these assets do not form part of the insolvency estate. This structurally distinguishes them from certificates, ETCs and ETNs. For funds from other countries, such as Ireland or Luxembourg, the law of that country applies.

Variant of the Sharpe ratio, calculated as (R − target) / downside deviation. It only takes into account deviations below a target return, because upward fluctuations are not regarded as risk. It favours right-skewed returns and therefore also strategies whose rare large losses have not yet occurred in the observation window.
siehe: Sharpe ratio (Sharpe-Verhältnis), Standard deviation, Maximum drawdown, Value at risk

text: Tendency to adopt the behaviour of the majority when uncertain. In Asch's experiments, unanimous group pressure led to 35.7% wrong answers; without a group, the error rate was below 0.7%.

Flat-rate deduction for income-related expenses (Werbungskosten) on income from capital assets under Section 20(9) EStG (Income Tax Act), amounting to €1,000 per person per year, or €2,000 for spouses assessed jointly. This rules out deducting the income-related expenses actually incurred.

€1,000 per person per year, €2,000 for joint assessment (Section 20(9) EStG, Income Tax Act), unchanged in 2026. It is granted as a flat rate; costs actually incurred, such as custody fees, specialist literature or advisory fees, cannot additionally be deducted from capital income.

Automated purchase of fixed amounts at fixed intervals, usually via fractional units. In Germany and continental Europe, around 15.1 million ETF savings plan contributions were executed each month in 2025. Many brokers execute them free of charge; some direct banks charge a percentage of the contribution.
Automatic annual increase in the monthly contribution by a fixed percentage, typically 1% to 10%. It keeps the savings rate constant without a new decision having to be made every year.
The percentage of net income that is not spent. There is no generally binding definition. Whether loan repayments and retirement contributions count is up to you, and you then stick with that choice.

Situation in which planned saving persistently exceeds planned investment. Ben Bernanke described it as a global savings glut; it is regarded as one of the standard explanations for the long-term decline in interest rates.

A transaction whose expected return comes solely from a future price change and not from ongoing value creation. According to Graham, speculation is anything that does not combine thorough analysis, safety of principal and an adequate return.

Holding period after which a private capital gain remains tax-free: ten years for property, one year for other assets such as gold or cryptocurrencies. For securities it has not existed since 2009; there, the flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) applies regardless of the holding period. For owner-occupied property the period does not apply if the owner lived in it throughout, or in the year of sale and the two preceding years.

Separation of a business unit into an independent company whose shares are credited to the existing shareholders' securities accounts. In Germany the transaction is tax-neutral under Section 20(4a) sentence 7 EStG (Income Tax Act); the acquisition costs are split between parent and subsidiary.

Semi-annual analysis by S&P Dow Jones Indices of how many active funds fall short of their category benchmark, including funds closed during the period. As of June 2025, over 20 years 93.8% of active US equity funds lagged behind the S&P Composite 1500; for euro-denominated global equity funds the figure over ten years was 98.2%, and for Germany equity funds 93.7%. The most consistent finding of the series is that the proportion rises with the length of the period.
siehe: Efficient market hypothesis, Survivorship bias, Alpha, Information ratio

text: Difference between the bid and ask price, which is incurred immediately on purchase and again with every trade. For large MSCI World ETFs, the Xetra Liquidity Measure (XLM), which captures the spread and market depth for a purchase and sale of €100,000, stood at around 2 to 4 basis points in September 2026; outside core trading hours the spread is considerably wider.

Court proceedings to review compensation payments (Abfindung and Ausgleich), for example under Sections 304, 305 AktG (Stock Corporation Act) or Section 327b AktG. The court estimates the appropriate amount under Section 287 ZPO (Code of Civil Procedure), usually on the basis of an expert opinion under IDW S1.

Compulsory exclusion of minority shareholders in return for cash compensation. The squeeze-out under stock corporation law requires 95% of the share capital (Section 327a AktG, Stock Corporation Act), the squeeze-out under merger law 90%; the adequacy of the compensation can be reviewed in appraisal proceedings (Spruchverfahren).

Crypto-asset intended to maintain a stable value against a currency, usually through reserves held in bank deposits and short-dated government bonds. Its stability depends entirely on the quality, auditing and availability of these reserves. Algorithmic variants without genuine backing have collapsed in the past.

Simultaneous high inflation and weak or shrinking output, typically the result of a supply shock. The textbook case is the 1973 oil crisis, when after the embargo the oil price rose from around $3 to over $5, and in the following year to just under $12 per barrel. Monetary policy does little to help; tightening dampens output further, while easing entrenches inflation expectations.

Square root of the variance, the most common measure of fluctuation. From 1928 to 2025 the annual returns of the S&P 500 were dispersed around their mean by 19.4%. As a risk measure it assumes an approximately normal distribution and therefore underestimates extreme losses; in addition, it weights upward and downward movements equally.
siehe: Covariance, Sortino ratio, Value at risk, Maximum drawdown

text: Defaults have a stronger effect than education. For organ donation, Johnson and Goldstein (2003) show consent rates of 12% in Germany (opt-in) compared with 99.98% in Austria (opt-out), even though switching was easy in both cases. For investing, automation through a savings plan and a fixed rebalancing date therefore achieves more than discipline.

Annual certificate from the paying agent under Section 45a(2) EStG (Income Tax Act), which must be issued on request. Its fields are structured according to an official template and correspond to the sections of the capital income annex (Anlage KAP).

Account under Section 27 KStG (Corporation Tax Act) in which contributed capital outside the share capital is recorded. Distributions from it are not capital income; however, they reduce the acquisition cost of the share. This defers the tax until the sale.

Tax saving that arises because interest expense is tax-deductible. In Germany it is smaller than the nominal tax rate on profits suggests, because under Section 8 no. 1 letter a GewStG (Trade Tax Act) a quarter of the remuneration for debts is added back to trade income.

Advantage of a portfolio that is not sold. As long as no gain is realised, the share of tax that will fall due later also remains invested and earns a return. Every realisation ends this effect for the amount concerned.

Number of trades needed for a measured average profit to be distinguishable from zero, calculated as n = (t × s / E)². Since E is squared in the denominator, halving the edge quadruples the number required.

Inheritance and gift tax are assessed on the values on the day the tax arises (Section 11 ErbStG, Inheritance and Gift Tax Act), which in the case of inheritance is the date of death. Later price changes are disregarded.
The difference between the book value of an item and its real value. It arises from the historical cost principle and from scheduled depreciation and is not visible in any ratio.
The seller of an option. The writer collects the premium and takes on the obligation to deliver (call) or to take delivery (put) if the option is exercised. Only the other side has a choice.

Payment for granting an option. It is taxable in full in the year it is received (Section 20(1) no. 11 EStG, Income Tax Act). Premiums paid for a closing transaction only reduce income in the year the position is closed out.
Buy order placed above the current price that is only triggered when that level is exceeded. It is used to enter on a breakout and carries the same execution risk as a stop-loss.
Combination of a trigger level and a price limit. Once the stop is reached, a limit order is placed. This prevents execution at any price, but can mean that nothing is sold at all in a rapid crash.

Sell order that enters the market as a market order when a threshold is reached. Execution can therefore be well below the threshold. If the price gaps down at the open, the stop acts only as a trigger and not as a floor.
siehe: Stop-limit order, Trailing stop, Market order

text: Version of the efficient market hypothesis according to which even non-public information is reflected in the price. It has been refuted empirically, and bans on insider trading presuppose that it does not hold.

German equivalent of free float. The MSCI World covers around 85% of free-float market capitalisation in 23 developed markets; for inclusion in the DAX, Deutsche Börse requires a free float of at least 10%.
A quantity that refers to a period, such as income or expenditure per month. Its counterpart is the stock variable, which applies to a reference date, for example wealth.

Share without a printed nominal amount that represents a notional portion of the share capital. Under Section 8 AktG (Stock Corporation Act), this proportionate amount must be at least €1; the share capital of a public limited company (AG) is at least €50,000.

Interest accrued since the last coupon payment but not yet paid out, which the buyer reimburses to the seller in addition to the price. Calculation: coupon times days since the last payment divided by days in the interest period; German federal bonds use act/act (ICMA).

Sum of the fair market values (gemeiner Wert) of the individual assets less debts. Under Section 11(2) BewG (Valuation Act) it forms the lower limit for business valuation for tax purposes, but it is not a yardstick for the value of a going concern.

Distortion that arises because failures disappear from the statistics. Elton, Gruber and Blake (1996) put the effect for US funds at 0.9 percentage points a year, since closed and merged funds no longer appear. Rankings of the best funds of the last ten years therefore look systematically too good.

Exchange agreement in which a synthetic ETF swaps the return on a collateral portfolio for the index return. Under UCITS, counterparty risk per counterparty is limited to 10% of net asset value; collateral valued daily, typically 100% to 120%, keeps it well below that.
High that is flanked on the left and right by several lower highs in each case. Only a fixed number of neighbouring bars turns a high into a verifiable statement.

Instead of the index shares, the fund holds a substitute basket and swaps its return for the index return via a total return swap. This results in very close tracking of the index, combined with counterparty risk.
The fast, automatic and effortless mode of thinking. It works associatively, is always active and delivers an answer immediately, even to questions it cannot actually answer.
The slow, rule-based and effortful mode of thinking. It calculates, compares and checks, but is only switched on when something forces it to be.
Market risk that affects all securities together. It remains even in the broadest portfolio and is the part of risk for which there is a premium.

Method in which, instead of a point forecast, several possible states are described and the consequences for the portfolio and income are examined for each. The aim is an allocation that remains bearable in all cases.

Measure of how many standard errors a measured value lies away from zero. From around 2, a single test is regarded as significant. When many candidates are tested at the same time, Harvey, Liu and Zhu call for at least 3.

Bank deposit available daily and covered by statutory deposit protection. The interest rate follows the ECB deposit facility rate (2.50% since 16 September 2026), usually at a distance and with a lag of several weeks, because banks pass on changes in the key interest rate with a delay and only partially.
siehe: Fixed-term deposit, Deposit protection, Money market fund

text: Total addressable market, the entire market that a product can address. It serves as an upper limit for revenue estimates and usually comes from company information. It is therefore not a neutral starting point for a valuation.

The point at which the capital market line touches the efficient frontier, that is, the risky portfolio with the highest Sharpe ratio. According to Tobin separation, every investor holds the same risky mix and controls their risk solely through the share of risk-free investment. This is the theoretical basis of the simple model consisting of a broad world index and an instant-access savings account.
siehe: Capital market line, Efficient frontier, Sharpe ratio (Sharpe-Verhältnis), Minimum variance portfolio

text: Claim or liability of a national central bank in the Eurosystem's payment system. The balance arises automatically as the offsetting entry for cross-border payments and is not a specially granted loan.

Only part of the order is executed because there are not enough matching orders in the order book at the limit. If execution takes place over several days, several contract notes and therefore multiple minimum fees may be incurred.
