Flat-rate compensation for the fact that, since the 2018 Investment Tax Act (InvStG), funds themselves pay 15% tax on domestic dividends and real estate income (Section 20 InvStG). For privately held investments, 30% of the income is tax-free for equity funds, 15% for mixed funds, 60% for real estate funds, 80% for foreign real estate funds and none for bond and money market funds. For this reason, losses on an equity fund can likewise only be offset at 70%.

Deed that divides a property into separate ownership units (Sondereigentum) and assigns co-ownership shares to each unit. Its second part, the community rules (Gemeinschaftsordnung), sets out cost allocation, voting rights and rules of use.

Total expense ratio of a fund, which includes ongoing management and operating costs but neither transaction costs within the fund nor the investor's trading costs; it therefore covers only part of the costs. Large standard ETFs are between 0.05% and 0.20% a year.

Value of all payments after the detailed planning period; for ordinary companies it typically makes up the largest part of the DCF value. Two methods are common: Gordon growth with TV = FCFF(n+1)/(WACC − g), or an exit multiple applied to the final EBITDA, in each case then discounted. The perpetual growth rate g must be below the discount rate and nominal economic growth; otherwise the company would mathematically become larger than the economy.
siehe: Gordon growth model, Discounted cash flow method (DCF), Weighted average cost of capital (WACC), Discount rate

text: Transaction in which a cash settlement of differences or a sum of money depending on a variable reference value is obtained (Section 20(2) sentence 1 no. 3 EStG, Income Tax Act), for example with CFDs, futures and cash-settled options. The results go into the general loss pot. The former offsetting limit of €20,000 was abolished by the Annual Tax Act 2024 (Jahressteuergesetz).
Rate for a future period derived from two points on the yield curve. At this rate, short-term investment with reinvestment and a long-term commitment produce the same final wealth.

ETF on an index that selects companies by a thematic keyword instead of by market coverage. It usually contains a few dozen stocks, is highly concentrated and is typically launched after a price rise.

Reinvestment of income within the fund instead of paying it out. Since the 2018 investment tax reform, the difference from the distributing version has been small. With both, price gains are tax-deferred until sale; the only part taxed differently on an ongoing basis is the part of a distribution that exceeds the capped base return (Basisertrag) of the advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale); in loss years and when the base interest rate is negative, that is the entire distribution.
Change in the option price for each calendar day that passes. Theta is negative for option buyers and positive for option writers; its magnitude increases disproportionately towards expiry.

The initial repayment portion of the instalment, expressed as an annual rate, usually 2% to 3%. Together with the interest rate, it determines the term. The lower the initial repayment, the larger the outstanding balance at the end of the fixed-rate period and the greater the impact of a rise in interest rates on the follow-up financing.
Also called the one-fund theorem. According to it, investors with the same expectations hold the same risky mix and control their risk solely through the share of the risk-free investment.
Sensitivity chart in which only one assumption is changed at a time and the resulting value is plotted against the base case. It shows which assumption the valuation depends on most.

Difference in return between a fund and its index over a period, the more meaningful measure of costs. For the iShares Core MSCI World it has averaged 0.03% a year since 2010, compared with a TER of 0.20%, because securities lending and withholding tax effects act as an offset.

Standard deviation of the difference in return between a portfolio and its benchmark index. For index funds it measures the quality of replication; for active funds, the deviation risk taken on deliberately. It captures the fluctuation of the deviation and not its size, which is why even a constant shortfall in return due to costs has a tracking error of zero; it is also the denominator of the information ratio.
siehe: Information ratio, Alpha, Smart beta, Standard deviation

text: Trading venue aimed at private investors, with long trading hours into the evening, where many neobrokers execute orders. Outside Xetra core hours, reference liquidity is lower and spreads widen. For world ETFs they are narrowest from 15:30, when the US stock exchanges are open.

Stop order whose level follows the price upwards at a fixed distance and stays put when prices fall. It locks in gains already made, but is regularly triggered by normal fluctuations if the distance is set too tight.
Seniority class of a securitised instrument. Interest and repayments flow from the top tranche downwards; defaults are allocated from the bottom tranche upwards.

Change in reported revenue and profits caused solely by translating the financial statements of foreign operations into the group currency, without any cash flow or operational change behind it. It must be distinguished from the transaction effect, which affects real revenue and costs.

begriff: Transmortal account power of attorney (transmortale Kontovollmacht)
text: Account power of attorney that expressly applies beyond death and allows access to payments without a certificate of inheritance (Erbschein). It governs the authority to dispose, not ownership.

Calculation rule for options in diluted earnings per share. The cash inflow from the exercise prices is notionally used to buy back the company's own shares at the average share price for the year. Only the new shares in excess of this increase the share count.

The contradiction that a country whose currency is the world reserve currency can only supply the world with liquidity through persistent balance of payments deficits. Precisely by doing so, it weakens the backing and credibility of its currency.
Body made up of the European Commission, the ECB and the IMF which, during the euro crisis, negotiated the conditions of the assistance programmes and monitored compliance with them.

The basket of liquid securities that a synthetically replicating ETF owns itself. It belongs to the fund assets, which are kept separate from the assets of the management company, and its content need not have anything to do with the target index.

Time-weighted return (German: zeitgewichtete Rendite). It chains together the period returns, adjusted for deposits and withdrawals. It measures the performance of the investment, not that of the investor, and is therefore the standard for comparing funds and indices. Its counterpart is the MWR.
siehe: Money-weighted return (MWR), Compound annual growth rate (CAGR), Geometric mean

text: Adjustment of the leveraged position to the target leverage at the close of trading, based on the new fund assets. It forces purchases after price rises and sales after declines, and as a result the promised leverage applies for only one day.

EU framework for retail funds (German: OGAW). It requires fund assets held at a depositary separately from the assets of the management company, a regular redemption option (as a rule at least twice a month, daily being usual) and diversification limits: under the 5/10/40 rule, at most 5% per issuer, up to 10% with a special provision in the fund rules, and all positions above 5% together at most 40% of the fund assets.
siehe: Segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen), Exchange-traded fund (ETF), Counterparty risk

text: The square root of the mean of the squared distances from the previous peak. It captures the depth and duration of declines and is the basis of the Martin ratio.

Financing principle of the statutory pension in which the contributions of those in work directly finance current pensions; no individual capital is built up. Contribution income is not sufficient for this. In 2025, around €98 billion in federal subsidies from tax revenue flowed in, about a quarter of income. At the end of 2025, the sustainability reserve (Nachhaltigkeitsrücklage) was equivalent to only around 1.4 months' expenditure.
Ratio of nominal output to the money supply, that is, how often a unit of money is used for purchases in a year. In the USA it fell from 2.19 (1997) to 1.13 (2020), and in mid-2026 it stood at 1.418.

Assets that do not serve the business permanently: inventories, receivables, securities, cash in hand and bank balances (Section 266 HGB (Commercial Code), assets side, item B). It is the part of the balance sheet that turns over during the financial year and in which liquidity is tied up. If inventories and receivables grow faster than revenue, that is a classic warning sign.
siehe: Fixed assets, Working capital, Cash conversion cycle, Net-net

text: Layout of the income statement by function (production, selling, administration) under Section 275(3) HGB (Commercial Code). It shows gross profit but does not report depreciation and personnel expenses as separate items.

Market capitalisation divided by annual revenue. For companies without profits, the ratio serves as a substitute for the P/E ratio. Since it ignores the margin, it is only as meaningful as the assumed future profitability.

A written option for which the corresponding holding or cash amount is missing. The premium is the same as for the covered variant, and for a put so is the loss potential. With an uncovered call, by contrast, the loss is theoretically unlimited, and in the event of assignment there is no cover.
Risk that affects only individual companies or industries. It can be eliminated through diversification and is therefore not rewarded with a risk premium.
Broader measure in German statistics that, in addition to the unemployed as defined in Section 16 SGB III (Social Code Book III), also covers participants in labour market policy programmes.

A judgement that was recognised but not acted on, where no purchase or sale was made despite a reason being in place. The error does not appear in any securities account statement and is therefore not recorded without a dedicated section in the log.

Central German register to which annual and consolidated financial statements subject to disclosure are submitted under Section 325 HGB (Commercial Code). For financial years from 2022 it is the relevant place to find them; older financial statements are in the Federal Gazette (Bundesanzeiger).

Market risk of the operating business without financial risk, also called asset beta. It is extracted from an observed beta using the Hamada equation and then relevered to your own target capital structure.

Loss threshold that will not be exceeded over a given period with a given probability, for example a 1-day VaR of 3% at 99% confidence. However, it says nothing about the size of the losses in the remaining cases. This gap is closed by expected shortfall, which measures the average loss beyond the threshold.
siehe: Standard deviation, Maximum drawdown, Monte Carlo simulation, Expected value

text: HML (High Minus Low) describes the finding that low-valued shares earn higher returns on average than highly valued ones. The US premium since 1926 is around 3.59% a year (geometric, t = 3.46). The major period of weakness from December 2006 to September 2020 brought a decline of 57.8%, the deepest value drawdown since 1926. The recovery since 2021, at 8.71% a year, had not made up the shortfall by July 2026.
siehe: Factor premium, P/B ratio, Momentum, Fama-French models

text: Share that looks cheap and stays cheap because its earning power falls faster than its price. Its hallmark is the absence of a catalyst that ends the discount.
Daily settlement of the profit and loss on a futures position at the settlement price. Unlike a book loss, the amount is debited from or credited to the account as a payment.

German counterpart to the VIX, indicating the 30-day volatility of the DAX expected by the derivatives market, renamed VDAX (ticker V1X) in September 2024; the European equivalent is the VSTOXX. Volatility indices are negatively correlated with the stock market and revert to their mean.
Change in the option price per percentage point of implied volatility. Vega is the same for calls and puts, is greatest at the money and falls as the remaining term shortens.

National price index of the Federal Statistical Office with the base 2020 = 100. It measures the price development of a weighted basket of goods. The inflation rate is the change in the index compared with the same month of the previous year.
Conversion of a bundle of loans into tradable securities. A special purpose vehicle buys the receivables and finances the purchase by issuing securities whose payments come from the loan pool.
The problem that every test of market efficiency simultaneously tests the assumed pricing model. If the test is negative, it remains unclear whether the market was inefficient or the model was wrong.
The period in which capital doubles at a constant rate of interest. It is t = ln(2) / ln(1+i).

Tax valuation method under Sections 199 to 203 BewG (Valuation Act). The sustainably achievable annual earnings are multiplied by the statutory capitalisation factor of 13.75; the asset-based value serves as the minimum value.

Probabilities are estimated according to how easily examples come to mind, not according to frequency. According to a Franklin Templeton survey, 66% of investors believed that the S&P 500 had stayed flat or fallen in 2009, although it rose by 26.5%. Their assessment followed the memory of 2008.

Annual report by the management board and supervisory board under Section 162 AktG (Stock Corporation Act) on the remuneration granted and owed to board members, which the auditor reviews formally. The report names the ratios on which variable remuneration depends.
Gap between the return of a fund and the money-weighted return of its investors. It arises from the timing and size of deposits and withdrawals.

Losses weigh more heavily than gains of the same size. The meta-analysis by Brown, Imai, Vieider and Camerer (2024) of 607 estimates from 150 studies arrives at a factor of 1.955 with a confidence interval of 1.82 to 2.10; the often-cited classic value of 2.25 comes from Tversky and Kahneman 1992. A loss therefore weighs roughly twice as heavily as a gain of the same size.

Investors with securities accounts at several banks have to combine their losses themselves. The certificate under Section 43a(3) sentences 4 and 5 EStG (Income Tax Act) must be requested by 15 December of the current year. The application is irrevocable, the bank's internal loss carryforward then lapses, and offsetting takes place via the capital income annex (Anlage KAP).

Separate determination of the remaining loss carryforward by the tax office under Section 20(6) sentence 3 in conjunction with Section 10d(4) EStG (Income Tax Act), split into share losses and other losses. It only comes about through the tax return and, unlike the bank's internal pot, is independent of the bank.

Banks keep three pots: a share loss pot, a general pot for everything else and a withholding tax pot. Losses from the sale of individual shares may only be offset against gains from share sales (Section 20(6) sentence 4 EStG, Income Tax Act); funds, bonds, interest and derivative transactions (Termingeschäfte) go into the general pot. The former €20,000 limits for derivative transactions and bad debt losses were abolished without replacement by the Annual Tax Act 2024 (Jahressteuergesetz).

Separate pot for losses from share sales under Section 20(6) sentence 4 EStG (Income Tax Act). Such losses can only be offset against gains from share sales, not against fund income or interest income.

An additional payment by the employer into a savings contract, if the collective agreement or employment contract provides for it. It is only paid on application and can be supplemented by the state employee savings bonus (Arbeitnehmersparzulage).

Cash account through which the purchases, sales, distributions and tax deductions of a securities account are processed. Having sufficient funds is particularly important at the start of the year, because the bank automatically collects the tax on the advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale) and, if funds are insufficient, draws on other accounts held with it or reports the matter to the tax office.

Debt divided by equity. A ratio of 2:1 corresponds to an equity ratio of around 33%. On its own it says little as a measure of risk, because it ignores maturities, fixed-rate periods and earning power; it should be supplemented by net debt / EBITDA and the interest coverage ratio.
siehe: Equity ratio, Net debt, Interest coverage ratio, Leverage effect

text: Income comparable to a pension within the meaning of Section 229 SGB V (Social Code Book V, health insurance), such as a company pension, a pension from a professional pension scheme (Versorgungswerk) or a civil servant's pension. As a rule, the full health insurance contribution is payable on it, borne by the pensioner alone; for company pensions, an allowance of €197.75 a month applies in 2026 for those with compulsory insurance. Lump-sum payments are notionally spread over 120 months and are subject to contributions for ten years.

Amounts that are irretrievably lost once paid. With property, these are the incidental purchase costs. They do not increase the mortgage lending value and have to be earned back over the holding period.

Combination of a bought and a sold option of the same type with the same expiry date and different strike prices. Maximum profit and maximum loss always add up to the difference between the strike prices.

Legally independent credit institution that holds the fund assets in custody, issues and redeems units and monitors the management company. If the management company becomes insolvent, the depositary takes over the management of the fund.

Number of shares including all subscription rights, convertible bonds and share-based payments that can lead to new shares. Only this figure is suitable for converting a company value into a value per share.

Earnings per share on the assumption that all dilutive options, convertible bonds and subscription rights have been exercised. Under IAS 33, it must be presented with equal prominence alongside the basic figure.

Decline in the stake of existing shareholders due to new shares from capital increases, convertible bonds or employee programmes. The relevant figure is therefore the diluted share count, which includes all outstanding subscription rights. Share buybacks that merely offset the dilution from remuneration programmes at best keep the stake per share constant.
siehe: Share-based payment, P/E ratio, Free cash flow

text: Principle of first removing sources of harm instead of looking for sources of gain. It rests on the fact that what does harm is known with greater certainty than what helps.

Registered share whose transfer requires the company's consent (Section 68(2) AktG, Stock Corporation Act). It is tradable, but the buyer is only entered in the share register once consent has been given.

Index of the 30-day volatility of the S&P 500 expected by the market, calculated model-free from the prices of liquid OTM options. A level of 20 means an annualised standard deviation of 20%, that is, an expected fluctuation of around 5.8% over 30 days. The highest closing level was 82.69 in March 2020.
The gap between the average of the annual returns and the annual growth of the capital. It is approximately sigma^2/2 and therefore depends solely on fluctuation.

Standard deviation of returns as a measure of the range of fluctuation. From 1928 to 2025 the annual returns of the S&P 500 were dispersed by 19.40%, those of the MSCI World in euros since 2001 by 17.71%, and those of emerging markets by 24.39%.
Gap between the expected and the experienced return, approximately σ²/2. It arises solely because returns are multiplied.
The fall in implied volatility after a scheduled event such as quarterly results. It reduces the value of options bought, regardless of the direction of the price.

The systematic excess of implied volatility over subsequently realised volatility. Economically, it is the insurance premium that option buyers pay to option writers. In return, the writers bear the risk of rare, very large losses.
Temporary suspension of continuous trading when a potential price leaves a predefined corridor. Trading then resumes via an auction.

begriff: Power of attorney beyond death (Vollmacht über den Tod hinaus)
text: Bank power of attorney that does not expire when the account holder dies. It gives the authorised person access to the account and securities account before the heirs have proven their status.
Loan whose fixed-rate period matches its term. No outstanding balance remains at the end, but the instalment is high and a later change in the repayment rate is usually ruled out.

Rule with an observable trigger, a specific action and an execution date, which is decided in calm conditions and automated where possible so that it is no longer up for debate in a stressful situation.

Notional minimum return on funds that is taxed annually under Section 18 InvStG (Investment Tax Act), ending the former tax deferral. Base return (Basisertrag) = value at the start of the year × base interest rate (Basiszins) × 0.7, capped at the increase in value during the year plus distributions; the advance lump sum is the base return less distributions, so it also affects distributing funds with distributions below the base return, and it does not apply in a loss year. It is an advance payment, because on sale it reduces the capital gain by its full amount (Section 19(1) InvStG).
siehe: Base interest rate for fund taxation (Basiszins)

text: A fee for repaying a loan early. For general consumer loans such as instalment loans, the charge is limited to 1% of the amount repaid (0.5% if the remaining term is one year or less) and never exceeds the interest for the remaining term. This limit does not apply to mortgage loans.

Written authorisation for a trusted person to make decisions for the grantor if the grantor becomes incapable of acting. It prevents the court from appointing a guardian and, unlike the emergency right of representation between spouses, also covers banking, contractual and official matters.

Class of shares without voting rights that receives preferential treatment on the dividend in return. Non-voting preference shares may make up at most half of the share capital; if the preferential dividend is not paid for two consecutive years, the voting right revives (Sections 139, 140 AktG, Stock Corporation Act).

Weighted average cost of capital: WACC = E/(D+E) × cost of equity + D/(D+E) × cost of debt × (1 − tax rate). The weights must be market values. The tax shield arises because interest is tax-deductible, but dividends are not. The KPMG cost of capital study 2025 reported an average WACC of 8.5% for companies from Germany, Austria and Switzerland, with a cost of equity of 9.7%.
siehe: Capital asset pricing model (CAPM), Market risk premium, Return on invested capital (ROIC), Discounted cash flow method (DCF)

text: Component of prospect theory according to which people do not translate probabilities into decisions linearly. They overweight small probabilities and underweight medium to large ones.

Rolling test procedure in which optimisation is carried out on one data window and testing on the immediately following, untouched segment. Both windows are then shifted. Only the concatenated test segments count as the result.

Bond with the right to exchange it for shares of the issuer. It combines a price floor from its bond character with participation in price increases. In return, investors receive a considerably lower coupon than on a normal bond from the same issuer.

Percentage gap between a convertible bond's conversion price and the share price at issue. It determines how far the share must rise before the conversion right has intrinsic value, that is, before conversion yields more than repayment. The right has time value even before that.

Minimum insurance period for entitlement to a pension. It is five years for the standard old-age pension, 35 years for early drawing from age 63 with a reduction, and 45 years for drawing without a reduction from age 65 (Sections 50, 36, 38 SGB VI, Social Code Book VI).
Cost in money, time, data and operational risk that a customer bears when changing supplier. Switching costs protect the existing supplier even when the competing product is objectively better.

The Apartment Ownership Act (Wohnungseigentumsgesetz) and at the same time the short form for the community of unit owners (Gemeinschaft der Wohnungseigentümer), which has had its own legal capacity since the 2020 reform. The owners' meeting decides on the common property, and the property manager implements its resolutions; the individual flat is held in separate ownership (Sondereigentum). Anyone who buys a flat (Eigentumswohnung) therefore always also becomes a member of a decision-making body.

When someone moves abroad, a capital gain is deemed to have been realised even though no money changes hands. Under Section 6 AStG (Foreign Tax Act), this applies to people who have had unlimited tax liability for seven of the last twelve years and hold at least 1% of a corporation. Payment in seven annual instalments is possible on application; if the person returns within seven years, the tax lapses. Since 1 January 2025, it has also applied via Section 19(3) InvStG (Investment Tax Act) to fund holdings of 1% or more or with acquisition costs of €500,000 or more per fund.

Expenses incurred to acquire, secure and maintain income, such as interest, tax depreciation (AfA) and administrative costs in the case of letting. For capital income they have been excluded since 2009; there, only the saver's allowance (Sparerpauschbetrag) applies (Section 20(9) EStG, Income Tax Act). Pensioners receive a lump-sum allowance of €102 a year on the taxable portion of their pension.

For capital income, income-related expenses (Werbungskosten) actually incurred, such as custody fees or specialist literature, cannot be deducted (Section 20(9) EStG, Income Tax Act). They are replaced solely by the saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag).

Tax loss from letting in which the income-related expenses (Werbungskosten) exceed the income. It reduces total taxable income and can be carried back or forward under Section 10d EStG (Income Tax Act).

A share that looks cheap on the basis of ratios because the earnings figure in the ratio cannot be repeated. Examples are the profit of a cyclical company at the peak or the dividend of a shrinking business.

The central component of prospect theory, an S-shaped valuation curve through the reference point. It flattens out in both directions and is around twice as steep in the loss range as in the gain range.
Loan from a bank or broker secured by your own securities account. The lending value for each security is set by the institution and can be reduced unilaterally.

Lending of fund holdings in return for a fee and collateral. The overcollateralisation, valued daily, is typically 102% to 105% in the industry. At iShares, 62.5% of the income goes to the fund and the provider keeps 37.5%.
siehe: Counterparty risk, Tracking difference, Short selling

text: Graphical representation of the CAPM with expected return on the vertical axis and beta on the horizontal axis. The line starts at the risk-free rate and rises with the market risk premium. Empirically, the observed line is flatter than the theoretical one.
Cycle of cash-secured put, assignment, covered call and renewed sale. Economically, it is a short volatility position with capped profit and full price risk.
Price range in which sell orders cluster, usually around previous highs and round numbers. It is given as a range and not as a line, because the rebounds are scattered.
Investing income received, such as interest, coupons or dividends, again. With accumulating funds, it happens automatically within the fund assets; otherwise the investor has to arrange it.
The risk that coupons received can no longer be invested at the interest rate assumed by the stated yield to maturity. The yield actually achieved then differs from the planned one.
Updating of an average as (previous value × (n−1) + current value)/n, as used in the RSI and ATR. It corresponds to an EMA with α = 1/n, which in EMA notation means a period count of 2n−1.

Dutch expression for trading in delivery contracts for goods that do not yet exist, in 1636/37 for tulip bulbs that were still in the ground. Payment was only made on delivery, which made it possible to speculate without capital.

Six-character German securities identification number (Wertpapierkennnummer) that older systems and order screens still use. It is national and less unambiguous than the ISIN, which is therefore preferable for orders and comparisons.
siehe: International Securities Identification Number (ISIN), Securities account

text: Notional account under the home-ownership Riester scheme (Wohn-Riester) in which the subsidised amounts that have gone into the property are recorded and compounded at 2% a year until the start of the pension. After that they are taxed on a deferred basis, or at 70% in the case of one-off taxation. For capital used for owner-occupied housing from 2028, the compounding no longer applies, and the account is taxed over 5 years in the pension phase instead of being spread until age 85 as before.

Annuity payment plus running costs (maintenance, property tax, insurance, non-recoverable service charges) in relation to net household income. It is more meaningful than the pure loan instalment ratio, because it includes the running costs of the property.

Current assets minus current liabilities; in a narrower sense, inventories plus trade receivables minus trade payables. An increase ties up cash and reduces free cash flow, even if profit remains unchanged. Negative working capital is normal in food retailing and not a sign of crisis.
siehe: Current assets, Cash conversion cycle, Free cash flow, Liquidity ratios

text: Weighting of the groups of goods in the price index according to the spending pattern of an average household. It determines how strongly an individual price increase affects the overall rate.

The risk that changes in exchange rates alter the return measured in your home currency. It arises at the level of the currencies of the securities and the business currencies of the companies, not at the level of the currency in which the fund is quoted.

Electronic trading system of Deutsche Börse and the reference market for German shares and ETFs, with continuous trading from 9:00 to 17:30. In March 2026, Xetra order book turnover in the ETF, ETC and ETN segment was €51.80 billion.
All gifts from the same person to the same person are added together over ten years. After that, the personal allowance for inheritance and gift tax is available again in full.

The thesis that equities become safer with a longer investment horizon. The probability of a loss does fall, but the possible size of the loss in euros rises. The horizon does not appear in the Merton formula for the optimal equity allocation.
Chaining of the period returns, independent of deposits and withdrawals. It measures the performance of the manager and is abbreviated to TWR.

A government's incentive to allow more inflation in the short term even though it promises price stability in the long term. Because markets price in this incentive, the result is higher inflation without any gain in employment. Time inconsistency is the most important rationale for central bank independence.
Growth rate of a single path over many periods. For wealth, the time average is the geometric mean of the return factors.
The tendency to value consumption today more highly than the same consumption later. It explains why interest is demanded even with complete certainty and no inflation.

Also called absolute momentum or trend following. Each instrument is compared only with its own past. If the twelve-month return is positive, a long position is held; if it is negative, cash or a short position.
Premium minus intrinsic value, that is, the price paid for the possibility that something may still happen before expiry. It is greatest at the money and inevitably falls to zero by the expiry date.
Money created by the central bank, that is, cash and banks' balances at the central bank. So far, private individuals can only hold it in the form of cash.
Clearing house that steps into every contract for exchange-traded derivatives. It is the seller to every buyer and vice versa, calls for collateral and settles daily.

Bearer bond (Inhaberschuldverschreibung) issued by a bank whose repayment depends on an underlying. Regardless of the payout profile, it remains legally a claim against the issuer and is not covered by deposit protection.
The price at which a tested thesis delivers the required return. It separates the judgement on the business from the judgement on the price and is set before buying, not afterwards.
Fixed share of the risky part in total wealth. The target allocation determines how much the portfolio loses in euros in a market decline.
Buying an economically abandoned company far below its asset value in order to take one last profit. The approach only works with small sums and forces constant selling.

Buffett's image for Graham's asset-based purchases. It refers to an abandoned company that is still good for one last free puff. The approach cannot be scaled up at will and requires constant selling.

Offsetting of the acquisition and distribution costs of a life or pension insurance policy against the first premiums. For the surrender value, Section 169(3) VVG (Insurance Contract Act) requires these costs to be spread over at least five years. For accounting purposes, a maximum rate of 25 per mille of the total premiums has applied since 2015 under the LVRG (Life Insurance Reform Act) of 2014.
The gap between the average nominal interest rate on the stock of debt and nominal GDP growth (r − g). If it is negative, the debt-to-GDP ratio falls of its own accord with a balanced primary budget.

Period for which the borrowing rate (Sollzins) is contractually fixed. Longer fixed-rate periods are more expensive and provide planning certainty. At the beginning of September 2026, according to the broker Dr. Klein (3 September 2026), effective interest rates in offers were around 3.93% for 5 years, 3.97% for 10 years, 4.17% for 15 years, 4.30% for 20 years and 4.48% for 30 years. Independently of this, under Section 489(1) no. 2 BGB (Civil Code) the borrower can terminate the loan ten years after receiving it in full, with six months' notice and without an early repayment charge.

EBIT divided by interest expense; variants use EBITDA in the numerator. It indicates how many times operating profit covers the interest burden. As a rule of thumb, values below about 2 are regarded as critical; there is no standardised threshold.
siehe: Debt-to-equity ratio, Net debt, EBIT, Liquidity ratios

text: Interest on capital to which earlier interest credits have already been added. The final value is K × (1 + i)^n. Compound interest requires the returns to be reinvested.

Band formed by the marginal lending facility rate (top), the main refinancing rate (middle) and the deposit facility rate (bottom), within which the money market rate moves. Since 18 September 2024 the spread between the main refinancing rate and the deposit facility rate has been only 15 basis points.

Tax restriction on deductions under Section 4h EStG (Income Tax Act), applied to corporations via Section 8a KStG (Corporation Tax Act). Net interest expense is only deductible up to 30% of tax EBITDA, with an exemption threshold (Freigrenze) of three million euros. The interest barrier thus limits the tax advantage of debt.

Representation of the yields of the same debtor across maturities. An inversion, that is, short-term rates above long-term rates, has preceded every recession in the US since 1955, with a lead time of six to twenty-four months and one false alarm in 1966; however, the sample comprises only about a dozen cases. On 18 September 2026 the spreads were +0.25 percentage points (10 years minus 2 years) and +0.87 percentage points (10 years minus 3 months); the curve was therefore normal.
siehe: Base interest rate for fund taxation (Basiszins)

text: Risk that the price of a fixed-income security falls because market interest rates rise. It exists regardless of the creditworthiness of the debtor and only leads to a realised loss if the security has to be sold before maturity.

According to Kostolany, investors who lack at least one of the first three of his four Gs: money, thoughts or patience (Geld, Gedanken, Geduld). They buy in the exaggeration phase and sell in the panic.

Kostolany's classification of investors. Shaky hands are debt-financed, driven by opinions and impatient, and have to sell when prices fall. Strong hands are financed with their own money and can wait.

By the definition of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), a company at least ten years old whose operating profit has not covered its interest expense for three years in a row. Such firms survive as long as they can refinance cheaply.

Tax base of the income tax schedule. It is the income that remains after deducting income-related expenses (Werbungskosten), special expenses (Sonderausgaben), extraordinary expenses (außergewöhnliche Belastungen) and allowances, and it is not the same as gross pay.

Restoring the target allocation solely by directing new savings contributions, dividends and interest into the underweight asset class. In Germany this does not trigger flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer).

Factor in the pension formula for the timing of the start of the pension. It is 1.0 at the standard retirement age, minus 0.003 for each month drawn early and plus 0.005 for each month deferred (Section 77 SGB VI, Social Code Book VI). The effect lasts for life.

Statutory matrimonial property regime for marriages without a marriage contract. The partners' assets remain separate during the marriage; only on divorce or death is the increase in wealth achieved during the marriage equalised. On death, the spouse's statutory share of the estate increases by a flat-rate quarter.
The exercise of an option by the other side, from the option writer's point of view. With American options it can happen at any time and is not announced in advance.

Collective term in the WpHG (Securities Trading Act) for commissions, fees and benefits in kind that an investment services firm receives from third parties. Under Section 70 WpHG, inducements are permitted only if they improve the quality of the service and are disclosed to the client.
Company set up specifically, with no business of its own, that holds and finances assets. Before 2008 it often remained off the bank's balance sheet, even though the bank had given guarantees for it.

Way of thinking, following Howard Marks, that examines whether something is better than the price already assumes, instead of merely asking whether it is good. Only the difference between reality and the priced-in expectation produces outperformance or underperformance.

The passing on of a one-off price shock to wages and from there back to prices. Without a second-round effect, a shock remains a one-off jump in the level; with one, it becomes a self-sustaining process.

The provision on private disposal transactions (private Veräußerungsgeschäfte) from which the speculation periods (Spekulationsfristen) derive. All gains falling under it in a year remain tax-free if together they amount to less than €1,000 (exemption threshold, Freigrenze); if they reach €1,000, the entire gain is taxable and not just the excess. The gains are subject to the personal tax rate, not to the flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer).
Also called residual income or EVA, calculated as (ROIC minus WACC) times invested capital. A company creates economic value only from economic profit.
Systematic overestimation of your own ability, your own precision and your own position compared with others. On the stock exchange it shows up measurably in increased trading frequency.
Distortion that arises because those who failed disappear from the statistics. In trading it has a double effect, because people who give up appear neither in broker analyses nor in forums.
Form of overconfidence in which estimation intervals are set too narrow. In practice, a stated 90% interval is right considerably less often than in nine out of ten cases.

Banks' central bank balances to the extent that they exceed minimum reserves. In the euro area, excess liquidity stood at around €2,161 billion in mid-2026, and it is falling because monetary policy securities holdings are running off.

Finding described by Robert Shiller in 1981 that share prices fluctuate more than the dividends subsequently paid justify. It is regarded as the most important empirical objection to the semi-strong form.
Third tray alongside buy and reject, for cases in which no judgement is possible. These cases are not assessed individually and are instead held as part of the broad market.
The euro short-term rate is the reference rate of the euro money market. The ECB calculates it daily from completed unsecured overnight loans taken out by banks. On 17 September 2026 it was 2.440%.
